comments: Example: We define 5<sup>1/3</sup> to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ = 5(<sup>1/3</sup>)³ to hold, so (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ must equal 5.

ADFA1280DFE3013113D268A86D17958E.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

comments: The Algebra I course builds on foundational mathematics content learned by students in Grades K-8 by expanding mathematics understanding to provide students with a strong mathematics education. Content is designed to engage students in a variety of mathematical experiences that include the use of reasoning and problem-solving skills, which may be applied to life situations beyond the classroom setting. This course serves as the cornerstone for all high school mathematics courses; therefore, all subsequent mathematics courses require student mastery of the Algebra I content standards.

ADF7EC40DFE3013113CE68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
ADF76DB0DFE3013113CD68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.
ADF57B20DFE3013113C968A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

comments: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

ADF47EE0DFE3013113C768A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

ABEEC770DFE30131113D68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

ABEE7A90DFE30131113C68A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

ABEE2BF0DFE30131113B68A86D17958E.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

ABEDDB60DFE30131113A68A86D17958E.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

ABED8560DFE30131113968A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

ABEC8950DFE30131113668A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

ABEBD310DFE30131113468A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

ABE98180DFE30131113368A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

ABC3D9C0DFE30131113268A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

ABC38870DFE30131113168A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

ABC331D0DFE30131113068A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

ABC2CD70DFE30131112F68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

ABC277B0DFE30131112E68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

ABC1E0C0DFE30131112C68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

ABC19170DFE30131112B68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

ABC13580DFE30131112A68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

ABC08FB0DFE30131112868A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

ABC04140DFE30131112768A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

ABBFEA60DFE30131112668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

ABBF8BB0DFE30131112568A86D17958E.description: Synthesize information from a range of sources (e.g., texts, experiments, simulations) into a coherent understanding of a process, phenomenon, or concept, resolving conflicting information when possible.

ABBF2080DFE30131112468A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the hypotheses, data, analysis, and conclusions in a science or technical text, verifying the data when possible and corroborating or challenging conclusions with other sources of information.

ABBED500DFE30131112368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., quantitative data, video, multimedia) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

ABBE3EC0DFE30131112168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text, identifying important issues that remain unresolved.

ABBDF190DFE30131112068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the text structures information or ideas into categories or hierarchies, demonstrating understanding of the information or ideas.

ABBD9FE0DFE30131111F68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 11—12 texts and topics.

ABBCB410DFE30131111D68A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a complex multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks; analyze the specific results based on explanations in the text.

ABBC5C70DFE30131111C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; summarize complex concepts, processes, or information presented in a text by paraphrasing them in simpler but still accurate terms.

ABBC0C90DFE30131111B68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts, attending to important distinctions the author makes and to any gaps or inconsistencies in the account.

ABBB5EC0DFE30131111968A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

ABBB05B0DFE30131111868A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

ABBA9CE0DFE30131111768A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

ABBA4030DFE30131111668A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from diverse sources, both primary and secondary, into a coherent understanding of an idea or event, noting discrepancies among sources.

ABB9DAA0DFE30131111568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate an author's premises, claims, and evidence by corroborating or challenging them with other information.

ABB980D0DFE30131111468A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, as well as in words) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

ABB8E6B0DFE30131111268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate authors' differing points of view on the same historical event or issue by assessing the authors' claims, reasoning, and evidence.

ABB89880DFE30131111168A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how a complex primary source is structured, including how key sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text contribute to the whole.

ABB847C0DFE30131111068A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including analyzing how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

ABB79170DFE30131110E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate various explanations for actions or events and determine which explanation best accords with textual evidence, acknowledging where the text leaves matters uncertain.

ABB73700DFE30131110D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary that makes clear the relationships among the key details and ideas.

ABB6DE90DFE30131110C68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, connecting insights gained from specific details to an understanding of the text as a whole.

ABB63D60DFE30131110A68A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

ABB5CFC0DFE30131110968A86D17958E.description: By the end of Grade 12, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the Grades 11-College and Career Readiness (CCR) text complexity band independently and proficiently.

ABB581C0DFE30131110868A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

ABB53010DFE30131110768A86D17958E.description: Analyze seventeenth-, eighteenth-, and nineteenth-century foundational U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (including The Declaration of Independence, the Preamble to the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address) for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

ABB4E200DFE30131110668A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents) and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy (e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses).

ABB49260DFE30131110568A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

ABB3DD60DFE30131110368A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

ABB389E0DFE30131110268A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

ABB32FB0DFE30131110168A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

ABB27930DFE3013110FF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

ABB219D0DFE3013110FE68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text.

ABB1B410DFE3013110FD68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

ABB091F0DFE3013110FA68A86D17958E.description: By the end of Grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the Grades 11-College and Career Readiness (CCR) text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

ABB03FC0DFE3013110F968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

ABAF9680DFE3013110F768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of foundational works of European literature with a concentration in British literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics.

ABAFEAD0DFE3013110F868A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (Include at least one play by Shakespeare.)

ABAE4300DFE3013110F368A86D17958E.description: Analyze a case in which grasping point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

ABADE370DFE3013110F268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

ABAD80E0DFE3013110F168A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

ABACCED0DFE3013110EF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and developed).

ABAC7FD0DFE3013110EE68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

ABAC2DF0DFE3013110ED68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

ABAB0B80DFE3013110EA68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

ABAAB720DFE3013110E968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

ABAA69D0DFE3013110E868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

ABAA1AD0DFE3013110E768A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

ABA9B9B0DFE3013110E668A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

ABA91C90DFE3013110E468A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

ABA8CE00DFE3013110E368A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

ABA87DB0DFE3013110E268A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

ABA7D890DFE3013110E068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

ABA78A60DFE3013110DF68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

ABA73A00DFE3013110DE68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

ABA68E00DFE3013110DC68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Social Studies

8E8C0BABCEE04A29BFB13E26FF7C8EF1.description: Identify contemporary American issues since 2001, including the establishment of the United States Department of Homeland Security, the enactment of the Patriot Act of 2001, and the impact of media analysis.

E5ABEF7F1A4F4AEDA899AC58BAED16DD.description: Determining ways to participate in the political process
comments: Examples: voting, running for office, serving on a jury, writing letters, being involved in political parties and political campaigns

FC050438725A4DD8A49E27BFFE88D3EF.description: Identifying options for civic and community action
comments: Examples: investigating the feasibility of a specific solution to a traffic problem, developing a plan for construction of a subdivision, using maps to make and justify decisions about best locations for public facilities

6BE637353E354EF99CEF175567F0B4B8.description: Describe how the United States can be improved by individual and group participation in civic and community activities.

4D5B385F4C0347848507CBE348F94A63.description: Tracing the political and social impact of the modern Civil Rights Movement from 1954 to the present, including Alabama's role

92FCB9B16F114BBF85B1DB0B98D629AA.description: Determining benefits of Alabama's role in world trade

AF2ED8174E42445DB2E084334C5444E6.description: Compare changes in social and economic conditions in the United States during the twentieth and twenty-first centuries.
comments: Examples: social—family values, peer pressure, education opportunities, women in the workplace; economic—career opportunities, disposable income, consumption of goods and services

EF1ED85DDFE24DBFAF33C0B7B778E222.description: Explaining character traits that are beneficial to individuals and society
comments: Examples: honesty, courage, compassion, civility, loyalty

B07FE66EBA404EE298019BD58495A5BB.description: Explaining how United States' citizenship is acquired by immigrants

8A9F0B97F1D042708D1CF34C443F95CC.description: Differentiating rights, privileges, duties, and responsibilities between citizens and noncitizens

19C9623ABACD4AF5AFFAC527DF46E272.description: Describe individual and civic responsibilities of citizens of the United States.
comments: Examples: individual—respect for rights of others, self-discipline, negotiation, compromise, fiscal responsibility; civic—respect for law, patriotism, participation in political process, fiscal responsibility

773924893CCE4837A00D902B2B17BD64.description: Apply principles of money management to the preparation of a personal budget that addresses housing, transportation, food, clothing, medical expenses, insurance, checking and savings accounts, loans, investments, credit, and comparison shopping.

C0DC5F49CF484C52908C9708D35E8359.description: Comparing economic systems, including market, command, and traditional

71D44BD31DFC4EFF886011C963712E02.description: Identifying laws protecting rights of consumers and avenues of recourse when those rights are violated

999E5DDAD28840ACA03C6F18E28EA9D8.description: Describing effects of government policies on the free market

CABFD0C5BD5B43CEACE93215A2858C5D.description: Appraise the relationship between the consumer and the marketplace in the economy of the United States regarding scarcity, opportunity cost, trade-off decision making, and the stock market.

595D27FAD4284BF6AF3A5AABD6463CFE.description: Analyzing agriculture, tourism, and urban growth in Alabama for their impact on economic development

37A6A38260014468A413FE2D0C1E0843.description: Using economic concepts to explain historical and current developments and issues in global, national, state, or local contexts
comments: Example: increase in oil prices resulting from supply and demand

91945D2AA6D2476183537791AF81DEB8.description: Determine how people organize economic systems to address basic economic questions regarding which goods and services will be produced, how they will be distributed, and who will consume them.

19FDCF53CD91471E9DC3296E30AD8780.description: Contrasting juvenile and adult laws at local, state, and federal levels

7B8939B5D4234125AD4E5C934940C9BD.description: Justifying consequences of committing a civil or criminal offense

7302923C081848D29F00BF48DBE9B31B.description: Explaining what is meant by the term rule of law

7A1D7A73BD524A3AAB01701E2E7B19AE.description: Explaining rights of citizens as guaranteed by the Bill of Rights under the Constitution of the United States

CE8424B7A98244D28ECBB4253E0B3840.description: Explain the importance of juvenile, adult, civil, and criminal laws within the judicial system of the United States.

89BD5911DAA54C178FC59868EB8A0919.description: Explaining concepts of separation of powers and checks and balances among the three branches of state and national governments

37C433ABE7F3426B8684A7C276B0BD57.description: Describing the organization and jurisdiction of courts at the local, state, and national levels within the judicial system of the United States

17CF28E2A8B54B268AB2B086D7754F83.description: Locating political and geographic districts of the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of Alabama's local and state governments and of the national government

855D9CEF18E349469B8A1C4EDCAD790C.description: Compare duties and functions of members of the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of Alabama's local and state governments and of the national government.

7B81F420C2154472BB544CFBF1B45303.description: Describing how local and state governments are funded

24878DDEF4DD4328BA6A118A3220F24F.description: Describe structures of state and local governments in the United States, including major Alabama offices and officeholders.

216CACA6712B4FBB8FDEA3C584F71981.description: Compare the government of the United States with other governmental systems, including monarchy, limited monarchy, oligarchy, dictatorship, theocracy, and pure democracy.

B4455A62445F419B83D28AFFF349C660.description: Describing the influence of John Locke, Thomas Hobbes, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Thomas Paine, Niccolò Machiavelli, Charles de Montesquieu, and François-Marie Arouet (Voltaire) on the political system of the United States

2F7BF496851C429B86BC2E92B902F471.description: Explain essential characteristics of the political system of the United States, including the organization and function of political parties and the process of selecting political leaders.

A367E44EA62148D5B1960CD1DF6119A4.description: Compare influences of ancient Greece, the Roman Republic, the Judeo-Christian tradition, the Magna Carta, federalism, the Mayflower Compact, the English Bill of Rights, the House of Burgesses, and the Petition of Rights on the government of the United States.

A6887721EA57498B8FBE723699D206E9.description: Explain ways geographic features and environmental issues have influenced historical events.
comments: Examples: geographic features—fall line, Cumberland Gap, Westward Expansion in the United States, weather conditions at Valley Forge and the outcome of the American Revolution, role of ocean currents and winds during exploration by Christopher Columbus; environmental issues—boundary disputes, ownership of ocean resources, revitalization of downtown areas

D493327245EF4845B0C03DBB7048E14A.description: Identifying issues regarding depletion of nonrenewable resources and the sustainability of renewable resources
comments: Examples: ocean shelf and Arctic exploration for petroleum, hybrid engines in cars, wind-powered generators, solar collection panels

47F11F9B3CD14793B6482328E14B0B98.description: Evaluating various cultural viewpoints regarding the use or value of natural resources
comments: Examples: salt and gold as valued commodities, petroleum product use and the invention of the internal combustion engine

8D18785189A0480980C9B52907D1E893.description: Explain the cultural concept of natural resources and changes in spatial distribution, quantity, and quality through time and by location.

95D5D160385542159AA8C712A9BB0117.description: Differentiating ways people prepare for and respond to natural hazards, including building storm shelters, conducting fire and tornado drills, and establishing building codes for construction

C68AEB1B8D964E5DAF82F3E9071CD24B.description: Identifying types, locations, and characteristics of natural hazards, including earthquakes, hurricanes, tornadoes, and mudslides

1C4E2E19E5CC49AEBBB7B39901629F5F.description: Explain how human systems develop in response to physical environmental conditions.
comments: Example: farming practices in different regions, including slash-and-burn agriculture, terrace farming, and center-pivot irrigation

0C5F5F2022674F26988F0320F72E6A7C.description: Explain how human actions modify the physical environment within and between places, including how human-induced changes affect the environment.
comments: Examples: within—construction of dams and downstream water availability for human consumption, agriculture, and aquatic ecosystems; between—urban heat islands and global climate change, desertification and land degradation, pollution and ozone depletion

18A3DA9F182944CDBF126DBBEC278271.description: Describing the eruption of territorial conflicts over borders, resources, land use, and ethnic and nationalistic identity
comments: Examples: India and Pakistan conflict over Jammu and Kashmir, the West Bank, the Sudan, Somalia piracy, ocean fishing and mineral rights, local land-use disputes

C0F49F163308437B96A09259C135396A.description: Identifying effects of cooperation among countries in controlling territories
comments: Examples: Great Lakes environmental management by United States and Canada, United Nations (UN) Heritage sites and host countries, Antarctic Treaty on scientific research

DC3173C66CA6434DBC2AF3D93B3D6A37.description: Identifying political boundaries based on physical and human systems
comments: Examples: physical—rivers as boundaries between counties; human—streets as boundaries between local government units

D109B6A149FA4779B61A3978C7EA25BF.description: Determine political, military, cultural, and economic forces that contribute to cooperation and conflict among people.

4E790086AE9F4B9EB608B0C4D4AFE3D9.description: Describing ways in which urban areas interact and influence surrounding regions
comments: Examples: daily commuters from nearby regions; communication centers that service nearby and distant locations through television, radio, newspapers, and the Internet; regional specialization in services or production

67A5991C21C64F2F84D4D9E18F17B66B.description: Describing settlement patterns in association with the location of resources
comments: Examples: fall line settlements near waterfalls used as a source of energy for mills, European industrial settlements near coal seams, spatial arrangement of towns and cities in North American Corn Belt settlements

5B6490BF07054696BF480B232DA32495.description: Explaining human activities that resulted in the development of settlements at particular locations due to trade, political importance, or natural resources
comments: Examples: Timbuktu near caravan routes; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Birmingham, Alabama, as manufacturing centers near coal and iron ore deposits; Singapore near a major ocean transportation corridor

F52361AD05974414BC362C0890ED757B.description: Classify spatial patterns of settlement in different regions of the world, including types and sizes of settlement patterns.
comments: Examples: types—linear, clustered, grid; sizes—large urban, small urban, and rural areas

E05F125B54B64BE8846E95772DADCB5E.description: Explaining why countries enter into global trade agreements, including the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), the Dominican Republic-Central America Free Trade Agreement (DR-CAFTA), the European Union (EU), the Mercado Común del Sur (MERCOSUR), and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)

DB35EE36DAA84B82A49EAADB14A33D26.description: Analyzing the impact of economic interdependence and globalization on places and their populations
comments: Examples: seed corn produced in Iowa and planted in South America, silicon chips manufactured in California and installed in a computer made in China that is purchased in Australia

AB86F278B65B4F4DBED9689DCBC04E42.description: Comparing one location to another for production of goods and services
comments: Examples: fast food restaurants in highly accessible locations, medical offices near hospitals, legal offices near courthouses, industries near major transportation routes

6233027FAC604013B4D3757EE5F3033A.description: Illustrate how primary, secondary, and tertiary economic activities have specific functions and spatial patterns.
comments: Examples: primary—forestry, agriculture, mining; secondary—manufacturing furniture, grinding coffee beans, assembling automobiles; tertiary—selling furniture, selling caffé latte, selling automobiles

82F8EF92819E46BC804D84A9AFD516FE.description: Explain how cultural features, traits, and diffusion help define regions, including religious structures, agricultural patterns, ethnic enclaves, ethnic restaurants, and the spread of Islam.

6F3FC5EF470B4C1E856AE33228EDA2A4.description: Predicting reasons and consequences of migration, including push and pull factors
comments: Examples: push—politics, war, famine; pull—potential jobs, family

8C026FC00B6F45829A2781214EC5636E.description: Evaluate spatial patterns and the demographic structure of population on Earth's surface in terms of density, dispersion, growth and mortality rates, natural increase, and doubling time.
comments: Examples: spatial patterns—major population clusters; demographic structure—age and sex distribution using population pyramids

9747C5AAA3E04D96BD7387439BFBA9E3.description: Comparing geographic issues in different regions that result from human and natural processes
comments: Examples: human—increase or decrease in population, land-use change in tropical forests; natural—hurricanes, tsunamis, tornadoes, floods

EB0ADCEBE2334AC2A2C3B0DC1D0C97EC.description: Comparing how ecosystems vary from place to place and over time
comments: Examples: place to place—differences in soil, climate, and topography; over time—alteration or destruction of natural habitats due to effects of floods and forest fires, reduction of species diversity due to loss of natural habitats, reduction of wetlands due to replacement by farms, reduction of forest and farmland due to replacement by housing developments, reduction of previously cleared land due to reforestation efforts

D1341A8403D944EB95B13C56203C3BC2.description: Describing characteristics and physical processes that influence the spatial distribution of ecosystems and biomes on Earth's surface

5F8A3D9704104E1E9F4556A9E1A984C6.description: Explaining processes that shape the physical environment, including long-range effects of extreme weather phenomena
comments: Examples: processes—plate tectonics, glaciers, ocean and atmospheric circulation, El Niño; long-range effects—erosion on agriculture, typhoons on coastal ecosystems

CE9AD055506C4F699AF606A802E0CA47.description: Comparing Earth-Sun relationships regarding seasons, fall hurricanes, monsoon rainfalls, and tornadoes

3A71493F374F40388C2BE96E19F461BF.description: Compare geographic patterns in the environment that result from processes within the atmosphere, biosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere of Earth's physical systems.

89B16CD113CD4B77A52583EAD44B5104.description: Explaining globalization and its impact on people in all regions of the world
comments: Examples: quality and sustainability of life, international cooperation

C6F0E6EED25A4B3BA11B06C9A4D48872.description: Comparing how culture and experience influence individual perceptions of places and regions
comments: Examples: cultural influences—language, religion, ethnicity, iconography, symbology, stereotypes

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: English Language Arts

A7E847C0DFE301310A1C68A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe (e.g., When other kids are happy that makes me happy).

A7E7F940DFE301310A1B68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).

A7E7A4F0DFE301310A1A68A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or juicy).

A7E74730DFE301310A1968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

A7E6F380DFE301310A1868A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.

A7E69C60DFE301310A1768A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).

A7E64C90DFE301310A1668A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).

A7E5FC80DFE301310A1568A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).

A7E5A8D0DFE301310A1468A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

A7E55BA0DFE301310A1368A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

A7E4B8A0DFE301310A1168A86D17958E.description: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

A7E43940DFE301310A1068A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

A7E38840DFE301310A0E68A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

A7E33C70DFE301310A0D68A86D17958E.description: Form uppercase and lowercase letters in cursive.

A7E2E170DFE301310A0C68A86D17958E.description: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage → badge; boy → boil).

A7E29310DFE301310A0B68A86D17958E.description: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.

A7E22E50DFE301310A0A68A86D17958E.description: Use commas in greetings and closings of letters.

A7E1C680DFE301310A0968A86D17958E.description: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.

A7E171C0DFE301310A0868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A7E12610DFE301310A0768A86D17958E.description: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (e.g., The boy watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little boy).

A7E0DC50DFE301310A0668A86D17958E.description: Use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

A7E090C0DFE301310A0568A86D17958E.description: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, told).

A7DFE360DFE301310A0368A86D17958E.description: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, fish).

A7DF4C80DFE301310A0168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A7DE36D0DFE3013109FE68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

A7DDED20DFE3013109FD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A7DDA1C0DFE3013109FC68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

A7DCFC20DFE3013109FA68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

A7DC5240DFE3013109F868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A7DC0900DFE3013109F768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A7DB7C30DFE3013109F568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

A7DB2F00DFE3013109F468A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

A7DADEF0DFE3013109F368A86D17958E.description: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

A7DA7780DFE3013109F268A86D17958E.description: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.

A7D9CD00DFE3013109F068A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.

A7D98090DFE3013109EF68A86D17958E.description: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

A7D93160DFE3013109EE68A86D17958E.description: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.

A7D8E280DFE3013109ED68A86D17958E.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.

A7D88AF0DFE3013109EC68A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

A7D83CA0DFE3013109EB68A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

A7D74880DFE3013109E868A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

A7D6F880DFE3013109E768A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

A7D6A2A0DFE3013109E668A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A7D60970DFE3013109E468A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

A7D5B3F0DFE3013109E368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

A7D53CD0DFE3013109E268A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

A7D49380DFE3013109E068A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

A7D33BC0DFE3013109DC68A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

A7D2F0D0DFE3013109DB68A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).

A7D2A350DFE3013109DA68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

A7D25680DFE3013109D968A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

A7D20AD0DFE3013109D868A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.

A7D11AC0DFE3013109D568A86D17958E.description: Write narratives in which they recount a well-elaborated event or short sequence of events, include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide a sense of closure.

A7D0CEF0DFE3013109D468A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.

A7D07810DFE3013109D368A86D17958E.description: Write free verse poetry to express ideas.

A7D017E0DFE3013109D268A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section.

A7CF10D0DFE3013109CF68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

A7CE7330DFE3013109CD68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

A7CE1710DFE3013109CC68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

A7CDABE0DFE3013109CB68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

A7CD5390DFE3013109CA68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

A7CD0A70DFE3013109C968A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

A7CCB870DFE3013109C868A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

A7CC6BF0DFE3013109C768A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A7CBDB10DFE3013109C568A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

A7CB8F80DFE3013109C468A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

A7CB2750DFE3013109C368A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

A7CA5CA0DFE3013109C168A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

A7CA1610DFE3013109C068A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

A7C9CFC0DFE3013109BF68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

A7C986B0DFE3013109BE68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

A7C93C00DFE3013109BD68A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

A7C89B50DFE3013109BB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

A7C83FF0DFE3013109BA68A86D17958E.description: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.

A7C7F0A0DFE3013109B968A86D17958E.description: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.

A7C796F0DFE3013109B868A86D17958E.description: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.

A7C74E30DFE3013109B768A86D17958E.description: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.

A7C6F940DFE3013109B668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.

A7C6AF00DFE3013109B568A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

A7C5B660DFE3013109B268A86D17958E.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 2—3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

A7C569A0DFE3013109B168A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

A7C51530DFE3013109B068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.

A7C4CA90DFE3013109AF68A86D17958E.description: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.

A7C47F10DFE3013109AE68A86D17958E.description: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.

A7C3E340DFE3013109AC68A86D17958E.description: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.

A7C38470DFE3013109AB68A86D17958E.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.

A7C31D80DFE3013109AA68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.

A7C268A0DFE3013109A868A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.

A7C1F590DFE3013109A768A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.

A7C1A8E0DFE3013109A668A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

A7C0C6A0DFE3013109A368A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2—3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

A7C07BA0DFE3013109A268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

A7C02F30DFE3013109A168A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.

A7BFD900DFE3013109A068A86D17958E.description: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.

A7BE95A0DFE30131099C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.

A8FCA3E0DFE301310C0868A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

A8FB3FF0DFE301310C0468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A8FAC9D0DFE301310C0368A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

A8FA1D80DFE301310C0168A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

A8F8EBA0DFE301310BFD68A86D17958E.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

A8F89FA0DFE301310BFC68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

A8F7E5F0DFE301310BFA68A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

A8F78D80DFE301310BF968A86D17958E.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

A8F47820DFE301310BF068A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function in particular sentences.

A8F43060DFE301310BEF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A8F2FAF0DFE301310BEB68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A8F10DA0DFE301310BE568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A8C8C6B0DFE301310B6B68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

D538C92323C147A4A2F77D3453964558.description: Interpret legends, stories, and songs that contributed to the development of the cultural history of the United States.

comments: Examples: positive—restocking fish in lakes, reforesting cleared land; negative—polluting water, littering roadways, eroding soil

7FF7B9C58CE3401283A13A5222EC73D2.description: Identifying map elements, including title, legend, compass rose, and scale

126D03C99F2C4FE4A1C918511D4BF471.description: Identify states, continents, oceans, and the equator using maps, globes, and technology.

36E7C9D71C80419187A4E2477611D25B.description: Using vocabulary associated with geographical features, including latitude, longitude, and border

BD2FC3E0702E4A1089480CFCF8F41EEC.description: Differentiate between a physical map and a political map.

8C30A00DBBA3463A901875F0157495BA.description: Use vocabulary to describe segments of time, including year, decade, score, and century.

FE9DD9CC15BC47D18DCF6A851593774A.description: Use various primary sources, including calendars and timelines, for reconstructing the past.

550D80D062634A7BB615A9F5070FDC74.description: Describing the history of American symbols and monuments

5BDF1E6DC3F047079B73B0873AAFA1EE.description: Describing the significance of national holidays, including the birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr.; Presidents' Day; Memorial Day; the Fourth of July; Veterans Day; and Thanksgiving Day

5B840724DF074869A81502A4E41B0890.description: Recognizing historical female figures, including Abigail Adams, Dolley Madison, Harriet Tubman, and Harriet Beecher Stowe

993979A0DA484414895AF62DDDA1A642.description: Recognizing our country's founding fathers, including George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Franklin, Patrick Henry, John Adams, John Hancock, and James Madison

7F8CB3A04F3C4E53BF5AD114AB4699B0.description: Identify national historical figures and celebrations that exemplify fundamental democratic values, including equality, justice, and responsibility for the common good.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Science

F3FA13607D4B4E1FA8E0316544F12B68.description: Examine and test solutions that address changes caused by Earth's events (e.g., dams for minimizing flooding, plants for controlling erosion).

1E3197189C1A47BA85DF8F00FBFC0DCA.description: Collect and evaluate data to identify water found on Earth and determine whether it is a solid or a liquid (e.g., glaciers as solid forms of water; oceans, lakes, rivers, streams as liquid forms of water).

B5F2B9D6B563467F91533ACEB7F32F15.description: Create models to identify physical features of Earth (e.g., mountains, valleys, plains, deserts, lakes, rivers, oceans).

563BE82EDFF746F5AEA500791548A7AC.description: Make observations from media to obtain information about Earth's events that happen over a short period of time (e.g., tornados, volcanic explosions, earthquakes) or over a time period longer than one can observe (e.g., erosion of rocks, melting of glaciers).

FE86562FC60E4C04AD7ADC6ED9B0C3DC.description: Obtain information from literature and other media to illustrate that there are many different kinds of living things and that they exist in different places on land and in water (e.g., woodland, tundra, desert, rainforest, ocean, river).

ABD1546281094D46B0AA2FE1A10B2DE3.description: Design and construct models to simulate how animals disperse seeds or pollinate plants (e.g., animals brushing fur against seed pods and seeds falling off in other areas, birds and bees extracting nectar from flowers and transferring pollen from one plant to another).

1CB2C72E9D4F454CBF61955E238F6804.description: Plan and carry out an investigation, using one variable at a time (e.g., water, light, soil, air), to determine the growth needs of plants.

F0F0042708F84720B857D206B7067BB6.description: Provide evidence that some changes in matter caused by heating or cooling can be reversed (e.g., heating or freezing of water) and some changes are irreversible (e.g., baking a cake, boiling an egg).

33AC5BAD642A4BD297070131F040C5C9.description: Demonstrate and explain how structures made from small pieces (e.g., linking cubes, blocks, building bricks, creative construction toys) can be disassembled and then rearranged to make new and different structures.

218152B48F4547599F0B688035898AB0.description: Collect and evaluate data to determine appropriate uses of materials based on their properties (e.g., strength, flexibility, hardness, texture, absorbency).

261A4925CCA74CBF8DBD6C21756313BC.description: Conduct an investigation to describe and classify various substances according to physical properties (e.g., milk being a liquid, not clear in color, assuming shape of its container, mixing with water; mineral oil being a liquid, clear in color, taking shape of its container, floating in water; a brick being a solid, not clear in color, rough in texture, not taking the shape of its container, sinking in water).

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Languages Other Than English—Foreign Languages

6BF582F04D5F49519E9BDA45971B192D.description: Recite learned nursery rhymes from a target culture for a school or community audience.

0036AE05083341A7970A54B4ED02F652.description: Identify similarities or differences between a target culture and their own.
comments: Examples: flags, music, gestures

8A558B3326E248B9BBC3339ECC037FC5.description: Relate concepts learned in other disciplines to concepts learned in the target language.
comments: Examples: weather and calendar topics in science, continents in geography, differences in numerical punctuation in mathematics, differences in capitalization rules in English language arts

1801260E627E4522A77A1D4585910125.description: Identify various elements of a target culture.
comments: Examples: music, history, food, clothing, landmarks

1DEEC57A943640D3923884A6A8274E0D.description: Describe cultural behaviors in a variety of social situations.
comments: Examples: greetings, gestures

6C64F3C70E7B497F971755B591F85869.description: Recite a variety of high-frequency learned words, phrases, and sentences in the target language, imitating correct and appropriate intonation and pronunciation.

A39A7776E92C4B309C04A57518FCDF04.description: Identify rhythm or speech patterns in culturally authentic materials.
comments: Examples: poetry, music, dance

197E6151810D4852BBB748EBA3312B86.description: Use learned target language vocabulary to express simple commands.

FD2E712ED94D4903A77BFCDAE2E89FD8.description: Respond appropriately to simple classroom directions given in the target language.
comments: Examples: repeating a statement or phrase, opening or closing a book, standing up

C45EF3E2EF634A2BB6136957F4A9897F.description: Use descriptive words in the target language to express opinions about a variety of materials, including stories, foods, or videos.
