A6BA31AB91894776B527C28B5D67C6A2.description: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.

541CCED1B9424CA99CA037BB6758FBB1.description: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.

C824B9DF247A4F1096C91B4E1C672FC8.description: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.

F4658E1778AC40A0B92B7917D56FD4F9.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).

078D5E596BA24F54AD24DCDCB738C3F1.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

65764CC06AC6489FAA06713EF88F6CDA.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

C44873EF28F3402A8BCD976F4572A8AE.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and express opinions about them).

BE7C83C148A5450EBA5C4B2BE14BF6F1.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

6214F8CADB1B41918986E3D2C77EDBDB.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

6625AA9CCD4640D9B60E91290123857D.description: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

080447EC2E034AC8B3BA48410678C5BD.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or several loosely linked events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide a reaction to what happened.

4E3F1653371C448D84B3F92E26E1C4D1.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative or explanatory texts in which they name what they are writing about and supply some information about the topic.

7C9B53F8DB0547D2AD5E0F059B604426.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces in which they tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is . . .).

5A63221446754162B588C40AB8DC3038.description: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.

7DDFD812C525400F9E69861FACCAB728.description: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.

E4AD8B3077F14E219206ED73AC145429.description: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).

CC5CC941166C48DF926E18F8C0657BF7.description: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.

C7C051D456EB42F7A3DAA1647C89749C.description: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sounds for each consonant.

08821219CE2D4147B766B00298756AD6.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

57ED7BC203DA48D48C7673408D86B541.description: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.

23FC4A7C3B0C40A0A9484CBCB399BC8F.description: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonant-vowel-consonant, or CVC) words. (This does not include CVCs ending with /l/, /r/, or /x/.) (Words, syllables, or phonemes written in /slashes/ refer to their pronunciation or phonology. Thus, /CVC/ is a word with three phonemes regardless of the number of letters in the spelling of the word.)

F17F4318C0144B9AAEA3E23E1B85B0AC.description: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.

4660A18F267A4DF391DF1A4C954B3148.description: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.

35BEB9CB5AFF4160BD1BB17D208487C9.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

3C11D9FB89DA40C28FC8D4B6F76EB3F1.description: Recognize and name all uppercase and lowercase letters of the alphabet.

DA037C432C85468588C40BEC312C7C64.description: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.

27AFD83625A44983866273A253B2E277.description: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.

91AB4C342FCA4BAD89F836AE226CB92E.description: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.

DA06FD5084374FD9AB1B90E38E29BBCF.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

23AF81F0A9214B1FB9B69EC07C63D41A.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

5F4D95A5ABF64C77965AF7C99DB2A6D9.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

CE51454749A148CF8039197B1D8AF651.description: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

01D6EAE5D0AC42358E15C479B8563F02.description: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

0252B7391B264FB5A38A4AE1B111380F.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).

06222045B1B04B74A0A2350D4DE67FA8.description: Name the author and illustrator of a text and define the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in a text.

C976649950654E1D9F06FCEE231AB287.description: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.

799F662DC47444568100BA39986BF396.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

4E55937FCA554842BC89692AA28A47B4.description: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

964D7FDA882C49B097982B0682F35FEB.description: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

5F3FB3DECAF947EF80556286A5EE7F8A.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

81424D16011F45638B864E2CFAC301CA.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

376BBFAF303B48B486907E23EE9F73DD.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

AD7514FE6D944D7C8CB618C71838A156.description: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.

832D7F2169454724BE3626665CA85EF7.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).

C165B0F59A9942E99F867EB844B6438D.description: With prompting and support, name the author and illustrator of a story and define the role of each in telling the story.

5CDFB594F0D04ED88FB88A2B45F3AAB5.description: Recognize common types of texts (e.g., storybooks, poems).

22E8A0A5080E4061AAEA93C5916035CB.description: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

6A602D71F0A34C69AE3D1BA65E448DA9.description: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.

BB966D6ED23F45A2A52EDF0B0A8B96F7.description: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details.

F3C8E39DD6484BB2914134F3C0287088.description: Make predictions to determine main idea and anticipate an ending.

D5444DD4902F42789E1C16300C1EC3CE.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

7BF44BE7EF2140A5952F111E6584A15F.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression

6230296079924A6497F890BBF4506E50.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

EBF1CABCC62D46BCAF227CE931B8E020.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

C5332CD0562749A29A338FFFBEFC16AA.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

EAAE8CAEA403497683DAE7911293D7F5.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

430C7C75B7644303A74FF80F460D4647.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A0F4EE9652494C2A99496DE673C0BD85.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

1BF04E9DF2154848BCC3EC24D823CEA5.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4B6A41CB8ED249099993F32CC74D0E79.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

0C781201B33B408E8659B01343B0C744.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A5864813BF7C42A6A3D2ACD32D8540E1.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

82F6D2BA0C50437F852DD57EDA4AE670.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

5E3ABB2586234BFB822148F55CCDB97D.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

E5A46741F4294C919DD93E17FE13CCE6.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

93A7AEA14A04408B9A23C734524F783E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames, including time for research, reflection, and revision, and shorter time frames such as a single sitting or a day or two for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

3CE3D1CBE8B44A1792ED7A3E20CDD235.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

420656A96B4148B397932E7917DAC38C.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

D79424B5651D4394AD36D52E92E4F8BD.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

68517799E18A4325865F3E61D0E8491E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

25306D45B7F846ECA852BAF7BFDAC026.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

4921B36129F54078AAA15AFDF1D6A49B.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

A10686E2CF2E4FFE823463983D9B1DB7.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4DF060B7CBFD42B28FFD47C9063D1E89.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

3086000732AC4938A6C1B90BB221DFB5.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

0D8347D786EB42EF9032CD876CC316C3.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

8FDA250FBD684EF98ED6D309D12ADA55.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

9AE2ECEDD37940ABBDA552D6C3D70374.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

F82FE29B19AB4A1186C3AEFEF7C9FB4E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

94A4C84878B944069D3BC6411F022805.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

25B7C9DA582544C88342F6AA0949670A.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

B9B847A091E34D2BB6F73B18C238100C.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse formats and media, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

F7ED29CF2FD046128C4679E01321855F.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

0AAC7D87EBD74C6BAEAE0D84B48CBC6F.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

6AEE31BBE25D4D96A79534CC026935D6.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

2CCE648517ED42B3A1476AE08BDC9FC0.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

4C0AF31CEDEE4390B7203CB45D2FFD33.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

76877CC987004277ACDA2B247F0C096F.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

E3743A1861E54CA983B1C64DA87303AC.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

883F33BFF9684391B894BD13E41DF227.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

C972CD67FCCA4B988ADD5E439DA4849E.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

E288965B85CC498A8BFE4EE1986783A1.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100. (Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.)

34B26BE9862442798923CDEF1A30214F.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

C363C3FADB6E493CB65BEEDF0187A0D5.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

A2D14C13A2AD477EBD24CEB676B2F936.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

D8BBFADBA3FA49C8A057081BD1E7F3F0.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.

628F0F352EDD4E388A0B8C560AAEFEA0.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

85E905F1C1854B76B9E446F6364DD539.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

1F26E625818A46D1AF0ADB5DD3CDA725.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

9E418FEABB0C42E6BCB2692D88122ED2.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

09B964422BD146068662F20C0B9A6DBC.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

B562C5F875DB40BCAD12A1A11D8BC48E.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

4E8D7C22464C491BB5F04C454AE8B5FB.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

D7F0604DE2C44029A82791E29BD41C74.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as ½. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

7FE37E2F296A40E884C9FCE9521FFBC9.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n×a)/(n×b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

A79B4F921B044577ADBEEF8FB82BC7BA.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

0F4170013B0646749F3DBB3FFC70A0B0.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

4EE7AD2DD74B4B29A6C09BA2F8F5F1BC.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

123E0BA13E6544F597574F1B38FA2681.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

77B18453C1554951A76DB726150794C7.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

89358E43584A40179FC291C4AB1DB252.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into nonoverlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world or mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

69918F0378DB4EB1A0068275F9156AD4.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

2DEA283FCE7047AEAC46B2DFDCB62D84.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

A9EC449AD4CE420FB74F8F03334C55D5.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle" and can be used to measure angles.

E83C09845EB141D7954A4DC0889611CB.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.

522A9DBD3BF4435EBA7209D86DA4FBBF.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

0B43CED6C5AE4534A9005A4188304767.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and mathematical problems.

0C8829F19FE94F81AA4D50B194C300CC.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

9865FE32E72247018EA0B5F1A29865C1.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units, including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz; l, ml; and hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.

E697BE0D090C443F8ABEFD1895350A4E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

830DDC9CFC6D49CDB166B8243DCA47A4.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

8D29D7B88BE74047B6DEE319BCE58BF8.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

9864AE2E11FE4C81AB99FA494A72291D.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

E7A37DAA7B6440A98189AFBA04359A02.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

568606FAAEC94E64A454BAC7A91C721D.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

7E8206052B9844738FAB0780F3934C38.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

1B1AE9CE83BC43E0B424C791015EADA3.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

ACDAA6D159004A8E9AC78FB6D2EF3310.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

AE7148E0EFC34AF8AB665E10CD7106B2.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

DF31100D660C4916A0FBA4BCD7BB8082.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

53967EC41412465BACA153288F7A1769.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.

B2E32F0AFACE490D87A3972D3EA9392A.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1-100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1-100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1-100 is prime or composite.

A03CB255B2C245509F1F12B81019255F.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

50353A8FC86D42DDAA13BA401A7A36C0.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

62D94AB04A55498683C11D272BAB9BB3.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

04842BA57B224BD99A90C2010E873DC7.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

CB948AC638E04F27A5804C3DE9B3DF18.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

B0E13927B10F4798BDA1CA87604FE8EA.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

80729F62A23F4062899D87BE1210077B.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x,y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of linear function in terms of the situation it models and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

A2D473E1C5BF443497ACB61D9039AB37.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

FF0F340DEAF04564B97CD1FCFCE79A6B.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

2A8943F5EA0544D8890E38EC95932B22.description: Compare properties of two functions, each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

06930E59E1F74A61A5A9E5559E354F63.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.

EC95913454344040BE71217D0C31C55B.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.

04A3C55D53D2489ABBE2C8F32DC1FD7F.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.

F9FCC5DB47594B6BB9E38BB84CCE81AA.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

785F8454B1D84BE886812E0B59EF64D2.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

3BCE7D9662BC47AE82D283C119F8D576.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

193D1946948B4943B1247F0B0085A77F.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.

8689926F94BF43F48B26892559D77807.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.

1A67ACD07CDE434AB6C6DE50D4C81F60.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersections of their graphs because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

C6DF60AD847B49359E12F2DB6A58A053.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

0C15EFB5B69D407BB0AEFE0EA8911137.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions, using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

8BBC96E4A9354C3FAFCAABF007A0DBFB.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. 8E95FF96B73A409C861C3EBE04F51FE9.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

601874D7E98347DBBB180F4916CB312F.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).

F94CDD6B95874CCCBC6FCD4B7B06F463.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

50855DE90DC04881B8BBCB4EDABC1BBB.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.

BE8DD8A669454DD2B59EE6BBA45CAC57.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

EBEAE7000E7F4EBF87811F10EB12C74F.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator, characters, or both; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

BA2C2E5CF46D4FC0A726E9E110742926.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

3763783D553A4827AA7DFE98E0AFDC75.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

9FDB0DD3004B4BAEA5ABB2BFBC3B4D26.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

60800367FF3247519D66F08D9AC3EB46.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

DEE03503C0214C7DBA8BACB0809D46DB.description: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

675716E6F29D49AE96FA15B1AFEACB0D.description: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

58F4C80CEA3C4E9FA58D9D45CB6DB8BB.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison or contrast, and cause and effect; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

5C779291A5434748802D941542C7E8DA.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

1FFB559F1B8A45FC863D864C7485E322.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

DA94794A5CD147989C99B067E75CA3DB.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

4F212999D81B4BB0A6EDB1F7F4C13862.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), reasons, and evidence.

C5CE42CC7C27480AB1A628EE5E90A643.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

A308C01737444619A1693CB4A1B04840.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

99994247D3674A6FA86C7BDF67914B37.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

1241635AAC9240D3A0D5808BD91C4F2F.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the Grades 6-8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

FCB6269F78C24AA3B4D706C4F3A5566F.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

0912204B3BB842009C1781B4EA8F97B1.description: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing different interpretations of facts.

D95DC117F1DC420F84C5371997AA9F52.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.

5406CFFF05BD4571A94E0882D970A80B.description: Compare and contrast a text to an audio, video, or multimedia version of the text, analyzing each medium's portrayal of the subject (e.g., how the delivery of a speech affects the impact of the words).

2728360C09B7429EAF9953584DE89974.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.

BEC2587D8E1A49B88ECDCBF4B531BEC5.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas.

A85F499FC9944EAC89947DEBE6BCEECB.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

1BF72971E42B4585B3FFAFD7E3299E78.description: Analyze the interactions between individuals, events, and ideas in a text (e.g., how ideas influence individuals or events, or how individuals influence ideas or events).

C58B592BD9014AB191CAEE97AB3E185A.description: Determine two or more central ideas in a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

EA676008EEB043B4906691308A7390FE.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

BA0B6503BD3C4B04850B55802ACF123F.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the Grades 6-8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

4132E1EDF290436F89686918CCCEEAA9.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

A7D7E29BE3384A4FBED06B8AF1811BDE.description: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history.

7EF96A0FEAC84FF1B122C92975374118.description: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multimedia version, analyzing the effects of techniques unique to each medium (e.g., lighting, sound, color, or camera focus and angles in a film).

5286A7D03C6B4C0A8D290E2D3804D283.description: Analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.

A69A1B3541974A449789DC0D6D9554F0.description: Analyze how a drama's or poem's form or structure (e.g., soliloquy, sonnet) contributes to its meaning.

583B3E1079A8402F808A7DF9ED812AC9.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of rhymes and other repetitions of sounds (e.g., alliteration) on a specific verse or stanza of a poem or section of a story or drama.

C9270D96F8EB4B66879AF90851FEAB43.description: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).

83EE5079183B4ED0A1034C9E07358F07.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

80D4E2803BBF45F289BB76D0C2E51EC0.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

4D59864C85AE41BBA1487E43B062EFFB.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression

FC222A2D9D1844D68099C54ABB73803A.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

E2D5106649584B108D2E3D6C2D6AA14E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

536FFB2148534093859D1E27812ABF50.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

79383A4AC61341129EBFF711DD61852C.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A2A27364CF684C2A9F3992EAC42B7A84.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

23FA46F427864B7A994B3ADAF9288A08.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

3371399EE4924C678052E26243C9D673.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

EB5510F3C79945A6A01F9819E3D59D4D.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

F6A0C6FB19414407B9B47AB3F4633431.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A91BB05E79664E1E975A62FFE9EBFEBD.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

B6BCA1DAF5D04D6886F56E3136BD1919.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D6DC894C0CFF49BCA856AEE1B671B80B.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

128D38FDC04B4D0FBB70B158DD547F36.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

E26BC8B19CC34C3EBBBCC1561747F254.description: Write routinely over extended time frames, including time for research, reflection, and revision, and shorter time frames such as a single sitting or a day or two for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

8E4A84276C3F4A45AC75932A19B2F77E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

E2059044EE8C4F9FA811ACB7F159086A.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

4D86E7085EB54E8BB51276D7F2912B5B.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4A1F45F14F0E4403B72EA1C60BD50164.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

17C8EAB8E4954D659D0F3398733B3635.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

58C28DAECF8A4089B663857149EC0348.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

8457FC132C8F449984EA53F10A624CBD.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

610D6C86856A499FB2F886976743B5AC.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

817DA36621CE4F59960B496F78F9DBCA.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

9BA8B400C2BE4A98A3E030D8E12F7840.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

0A73599FA2AC45C18D9A399A2F512557.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

8BEC719022E84629A204BEE36A135CCA.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

3B351A93C92942EBBF747D276F22CE6F.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

01C53CAFCC354F0BBFFE5967ADF5B7E9.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

82371F16AB0C4BD4888AC574A9E9E1DA.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

540067CE5DD945F7B778694A9649BD77.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse formats and media, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

A913D766E45B4B639C757A4553CA55BC.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

7C22A2F7F21E4B66A401BC7E22BCF6FC.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

FC0AC62DE1E74344B5241F58DFE0695F.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

FEE30A5F4B2F41BE8A67184C8D50DBFE.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

E4780E6734494E198D24DD130D911637.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

F51F4867B34F48E9AEAE0B73CC336170.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

E699D076803F4703A638DFAAD18FF6FD.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

2440BEA9999B4E3CAA14752C9E21BB72.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

B4F017EC419E461C92936273B16A43EE.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation) as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.

01B7202BB4F3474888F40FD9843C44CA.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

92AF03100E814F5AB9A1103E1F00FDCA.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

AE5AE48C12324018A0A6BE0CD8ACDEF5.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

543324F5BE7741809A2EAEFA79B4A330.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.

E2398BD0E51C45BBB08F8D033BAF5A98.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

365C20403B254807B6643FA06030A655.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

383B4CB86E1944BB81F4D954EC7EF1B5.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

9338F914622E4B6FAB4C8721B0728619.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

05230C3DDC8449D3BB51E16EC9CA60BA.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

A6A7888ADB4047079AD55CFF060BE77D.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q, and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

7E4C5160820E48E394FFDEA9DC01F756.description: Use variables to represent numbers, and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

CA266F5545514D86B8717C120AF3FC2A.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

E16B735A05AE45D0866F0D13EF0298F4.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

08053D80F7344C6AB3B4AB98B5160DCB.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).

178B6F76182549EFAF1C12BF1A1AC21A.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

23D16556435E484E91FAFBA7E6027253.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

95EA744D337E44E090634EFA257BEEB6.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.

F7170C6ADCB442A2B0416BB16239AB65.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

7D5C65DFCB6D468AA739DA433538E075.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

CEEFF63714B2430CBE251F7FB5ECE85C.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

BE5E193A88144DBB9B10168073484BB1.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

FDC12FAE599E4213A17FB6698D24EDF1.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

44276B06F3BE44D3A631F93F428D00C3.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

33D627875A144C29A8B540CA783E00AE.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.

D0C36AB36D9E420A80A874F9675E5B75.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

F024E1A5713F4006B7B64DAD3FC60D03.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

87AD5AFF55DD413482DBCFED8992AA17.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

58136E0A7C5647929DCB3EC823704553.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

727453C8C56A43BE8CE9D5284A450E05.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., –(–3) = 3, and that 0 is its own opposite.

15EFC697DDA44467A66F9A2DF51AAEFF.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

51C1E4322BB4493E8AAB64DF80B61041.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

77F69A3F22A44085A5BE879E37161CC9.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

90F97D2376A94C76996A25070FEF9DF7.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1-100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.

6D75E00B8CD54EE4B2E6A319B473B959.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.

1E839A08C3074384A0937E7B992DB9EE.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

1756D67A3BFA40CD97FB2DE93120AF1D.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

D9005FAC169B4ECA8169D920562EE50C.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

6B8F1354BF314AFB9E56635239155CAC.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide by fractions.

34AF2EA2DBBC4DA281E1A571ABE86B29.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

2C92D7560DAA402E871CC3415C68AD05.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

2B208C3F9C0C40898CF50804AF66F529.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.

1FBC81B154D746378710039302C6660C.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

0560CC1CE963461BB3FD414A1F6ACD58.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.

E3C11150FCD54C31897FD0781B3BB7D2.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

4241F5165D04424EB3DEB8436D99DC78.description: Understand the concept of a ratio, and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

813C0A4219314791A7A788B74329BCDD.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

7CE747FA8D8347D89B2E09490C161030.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

F11DC489933A4770BDD79C5F3BE979D7.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

EED4ABB83E8E4A7C837E3FD7E04BFDF7.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas V = lwh and V = Bh to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

60278023B5B94AC2875E0E3BDC1D7807.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

19D9722B9FF34CD89CDD1515FB8D1B67.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

7C7A5B4047C74168896321812CD1CEBC.description: Apply Euler's and deMoivre's formulas as links between complex numbers and trigonometry.

1F91ACC2E22C462A90586E35C494627E.description: Prove the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines and use them to solve problems. Understand Law of Sines = 2r, where r is the radius of the circumscribed circle of the triangle. Apply the Law of Tangents.

F9E5BED48A1442B29E6F07A17A4DDBBC.description: Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

0374ACA7FBA7472FB95DDB6B12FDB995.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

EE1C224206CF473C8B8950477AA2DC17.description: Reduce the degree of either the numerator or denominator of a rational function by using partial fraction decomposition or partial fraction expansion.

3065BA64305D4B02AE1446A2780893A4.description: Arithmetic With Polynomials and Rational Functions

E1540D2FA3814D53A5E5CB02FD3B3E43.description: Use logic symbols to write truth tables.

12C5F62FDE0246BB9D2C6C88BF13935B.description: Use the laws of Boolean Algebra to describe true/false circuits. Simplify Boolean expressions using the relationships between conjunction, disjunction, and negation operations.

66968D742A6748B484FD2248AD9F8EBB.description: Calculate the limit of a sequence, of a function, and of an infinite series.

821E9907BDF640DAA40D619FD586075F.description: Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials. Understand the importance of using complex numbers in graphing functions on the Cartesian or complex plane.

2CB022D3BFA942728C80FF5F161C86BB.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

CAA810AF34BF4E259DA3421B8AC56EFF.description: Work with 2 × 2 matrices as transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area. Solve matrix application problems using reduced row echelon form.

B32F9BD92220449E855D680D01E162FF.description: Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors, including matrices larger than 2 × 2.

BF7C415EE64B4836A68A29F3F7A69763.description: Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse. Solve matrix equations using augmented matrices.

124A6369021E48EDB20D0F47A493DFB7.description: Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled, including rotation matrices.

0FB3BA6965E14953898D4BF26F805542.description: Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network, including linear programming.

F3E55816E7D5460F9340DF862EDBF333.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

4D59CC3EDF5140AA87D7964E63B2DF9F.description: Understand vector subtraction v – w as v + (–w), where (–w) is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise, including vectors in complex vector spaces.

EE74E5191E4E4B3F98405FB56755F8C7.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum, including vectors in complex vector spaces.

FE5335A0D74B417ABFF7C61C19E7B633.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes. Find the dot product and the cross product of vectors.

CE54E1127DC24B30B5CB686B5D46C0F1.description: Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors, including navigation (e.g., airplane, aerospace, oceanic).

2C5A200F21CF4E2D9BF16B0345DD9509.description: Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. 7130D201E7DB4396A2BB6BBC13C1B5BC.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

9F954729C2534151B7B6A044674C6D3E.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data.

848A823A8B034D01A91FF8F502AC0882.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

DC3897668D5B402FB8E5A077ABCDC027.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. 269E6D6F96F6434B9426954F22A2CEBE.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

9019A830C9254946B6405DE0861BBAFF.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

36BF1CACE2C04FF0906963C16889C1D1.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

2982D3286FBD4187B5ED09AAA89FF1B7.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

64B947AD159642108D5C1A4B6E76A2C6.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model. (Linear and exponential of form f(x) = b<sup>x</sup> + k.)

77B479732BFB4EBB9D8626560F08BA2F.description: Observe, using graphs and tables, that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

6CEA4BA2DCE8460F99C137069E6EC5BB.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

9D4005682483462EA307804CE367B645.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

3D356B6195EA4C24AC3C47FE974CDD3B.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

4CFFCFBB1E7A40DEABE17F20862FC34A.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

F3908D5F25EB43C7A724866F6CF557DD.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

E7521F7079D441838C35B0983ED8F1E5.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

731C2B22308A4FABB1DA845E3DE603D1.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

B816F8D9DB2D4176A21DF91F88D0CD95.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.

FF46AFD558EA40BEB0B6024E6D36692D.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

DEEE096FDB3044249EABEA0FF55D0A8C.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

0E2806FD766C4BC699DF6DBBF02B917E.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

EF742E310E03405085B36D202D74750F.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

C2656060A0C6435983D2911D7B71ADFB.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

480D5D0DBE954D629C331931F6CDD3B2.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

06C05CA709604617927711F8B56E2FE2.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

A1C1AE69B16645C09ED3DB7340B51C46.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

4D1FBEE98D294A519ED60815E1280182.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship.

8A561C5276D24473B663A4631CDDCB8A.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

CA6BC16E4D144494937400B8114C7539.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.

3DBDE2C1BF6E48C69BD12B74268440EC.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

F5C3B5B928FD42D7B3FA906C3A94AD92.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

95472A966E5149DBBE896E7037BCA98E.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

58898624BDBA475C9E70A3E028F7A3F1.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

282F7046E4AA40C1B27110366BF185AD.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

7D746BED415D43F18692EEAB0D564D7E.description: Solve systems of equations. (Linear-linear and linear-quadratic.)

63707C16035446EC8BBA60C14EEC4414.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square and the quadratic formula, and factoring as appropriate to the initial form of the equation.

113972CF228B4CA3A045CF1BBDAE0D81.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

EBA67079008448B2954EFBE863180A7E.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

EDF0A391D43943F4B05A07CB79135169.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

D3C6F7F79AD441178C34FEAE6DC080C2.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

583ED6AF2B10475F899B8DF3A3781E3D.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

A825143CD287429FA4C1D422245D685E.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

BADB54EFD70748D0A4E93B061E81BED8.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

62D45EC45F624159B03BD0D216FBFB20.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable, and use them to solve problems.

AB167F29C25B461983FF8B3C158AFB36.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

30001ADF3E9B431A8F32E7C9BFC582C3.description: Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

7ED526AC1EE247F79BE192E916D5643E.description: Perform arithmetic operations on polynomials. (Linear and quadratic.)

22039C8F066547309C37106BBA045BB8.description: Arithmetic With Polynomials and Rational Expressions

F73221EB7FBE453F90DD7A9145E34E39.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

80E4E684720943DEAFCA285643934D51.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

F4D3551FE0BF4BDD90ADFAABF814C7B2.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems. (Quadratic and exponential.)

80A45F041B294B19AE72AC2805DB61EB.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

57D65DA7E8424A5B84C7CA4844F44760.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

F9CB6FAFBEFB4C5FAAACB8FF7BBCF0C5.description: Interpret parts of an expression such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

F9204A5E209440F2BE2EF7832A070382.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

B74134557BB048E584A6A2D1E9F29A6A.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

83130E4AD73A41BFAF89620AF04FC46A.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

5439791DAC614335A42C62A68A7AB31D.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multistep problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

33E406144A4E4D68A477CE8AAEAAC8BF.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

61CE8774BB98472EAE8748524313D1BF.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

63BC2AD58FE74B298E73E9B8621CE1B6.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

6C54ECED33E74021953A5F28EB965940.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.

7C97F0878C0541C5A62F3F9C1097C895.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: English Language Arts

D4A23BBE942C43ABAC305E6F73ECDF1F.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

B3BC3EE5E8AB4E499AD9E3FA2B62D26C.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

803D47966AA74859AC597808035E3B4D.description: Print all uppercase and lowercase letters.

2FF90EBC7058404692DB32BB8FF44D46.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

B32DEA347A8443AD9E0C24DEDD150EDE.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

5149B445CD6448E4A148ADA2B3363145.description: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide reading of a range of text types.

2C06BDC5161A4EA7897A29489BEA406B.description: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

EACEDF58C2CE4AA386A6C854963EEA67.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

7369BE9C08A74E208BDFCAE5630DCAFB.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

CF4A359ECE444081AB55ABC5B7BE44E8.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

0F3665DED4CC4BEB9172429EB56011D6.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

ED4B4F4F775948B1A81C8B17B368325A.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

F10642FBEC2F4028838089A5DE2549D6.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

F23A51FB79334A59B46F8354479D800C.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

D4795B714C5C4EAFAA1DBD8FE8CB1C48.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

9C7943534B0C4CF084B04AFBFAA9B61F.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

6BF720698D9040C7807B5B39CAD65977.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

BE92F0A225AB4D60AD76BCB77153544A.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

E92BF799E2C24C0CBF0A911CD954A7D6.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse formats and media, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

67DCD6D5AB554B34B5775ADC3B3505FA.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

27ED4E118B504BD3837B9FC7488051BB.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

CA5CEE1ADB6F4E069F365277A8B5EF7D.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.
