document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

6D095AE575744B90877EFC6D9922C65C.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

FDDD15D434C34CFCAF7BFE1F3D0AE503.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

BE292EBCF5F042BEAB6311B53630E79C.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., ½ = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

310F9E148A994968A6715BC293F7B02A.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size or the same point on a number line.

29FE88B7EEEE403B8FD8041D48E486DB.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

505492449F1A4D4391B82A476D6BFF21.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

3E526BFD20CE4723B05D9E3F05503266.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

0E0472C8D1524E729180FB2CB59789D3.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

18574F440063403F8EB9BAA427B859C0.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts and size 1/b.

D13C699BA3564D16B6626E4A1E6A3B9B.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

8813AB197D57458DB30BAA37A7D72A3F.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

0BBF7EE605F9488D96E876A3D2058919.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

E3004D7758DB47798DD3B5E09D8B43C4.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

3C30970CEBE24D42AD4261FA6611DAE1.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

8DF507A5917241459F6CB96B7EA3F4B2.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

C0C386B2BC224EABA66571FD49F5003B.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into nonoverlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the nonoverlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.

89C36E69EC4B409587702946946D1943.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

1C4C756D5C8440D184F5DDD27AA82C28.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

35248B5D404F407ABCCA24EC07F0C296.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

7DB41AD0DCBB479CA74D1986A9544630.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

0619946AA1574C05A4941EEDE03DD112.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

D16A4887ABE14B18B0C373EF7C1C2B07.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

20FAA4E75E804655B31452F9E66E48EC.description: A square with side length 1 unit called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area and can be used to measure area.

A8DE557AA7EE4EE59E73F62F2F244CD3.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures, and understand concepts of area measurement.

1F4F6525F1FA408E8A04008E5EFB7E2B.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

200EAB4DB6B542F2B16F55BA6A13E380.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units – whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

072ED1688049439D8D85CA8EBEDE36D7.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

3B2DD8A5795B4AD2817A7B20C543D8E6.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l).

4DCAC9E8413A45FAB3B1E5862D48F04E.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute, and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

97D55178B0C649FF8B1C31205AC3769B.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

7781ECEE809944A1A3D599FB06CF702B.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10 - 90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

1A8BDDF1B28D4BF6ABC89A9A628215F3.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

08BC4988A281403B8AFD25CCA95C9732.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

0C51B00391404D4E8FBB069FCA51D084.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic. (A range of algorithms may be used.)

3F5F27859BB748BF9F8BD0A7574BADAB.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

0978C8D76B8F4B67877521902F44D166.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.

E86345BD46A346B088C7E0E12EAA72A4.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

D61EA3C69927430C9DE3976522C139D8.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

FD8D6F90B5EE40B9A40A423B03C56635.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

F4A77DBD5F2E47D7A7990C1E15046889.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.

229FAEA14700475484699111C5BA1F4F.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide. (Students need not use formal terms for these properties.)

37D365F76B964731BC1C2CC4B0187852.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

A525E02569BD44D0A153A5FAABD39159.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.

15D8BD1090824880AD5A8E1840A4BA7D.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

C92DDE7FA90D443D97682AD3F056AAC8.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

1A8A7AFE405F40D484672853B3EED48F.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.

5079C1EAA1AA4E04BDDB40A32F86BEDB.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: English Language Arts

F1C69AB1CB6847F589D9791C44A9BF63.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

955D7A5B5216405B916F92F39B8BD0F7.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

1289289C9377489888AAA7B4DD6E1FC5.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., euphemism, oxymoron) in context and analyze their role in the text.

4412FF537CB540079FEB9AE4EDFCD1F0.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

79CD939B65F64D6BACADD5BC61C1763B.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

389240AE98154DD897E2317DE305903E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

D0C8FAF9954C44BF8BEE99259D687AD1.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

098AA95945D74D0AA46AF70954BDA664.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

1C544940BDBF466BA88554D3716817B4.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on Grade 9 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

678C9D1E35F04597AFF5BEB0332CB141.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., Modern Language Association's MLA Handbook, Turabian's A Manual for Writers) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

D39A13C19DBE4AAD8AADD84F6A59578A.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

1C4B509E04654FEF83C08F399356E201.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

D7486838C89A44B3B0929D0595A37405.description: Use a semicolon (and perhaps a conjunctive adverb) to link two or more closely related independent clauses.

68115F890DFF499394B15F9EE714D6C0.description: Use commas correctly with non-essential appositives.

84BA54F94A8E477FA2E6BC08F19D3EA2.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

F76AD1CAAD5D4C0AB4B0A55FFEE27488.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

04694163DA7E4C6189205D9D34D2FF99.description: Apply rules of subject-verb agreement with the subjunctive mood.

5AE929E6A40E4C4B8F781342BE246836.description: Apply rules of subject-verb agreement when the subject has compound parts joined by or with the second element as singular or plural.

74E647289570443AB4C2E9965CE828C0.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A08C50C4F4D74F699ABDEDFE379BAD25.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

BE42069AC16D4E82A0310460E6D9A8B1.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

676DE12E51C941AE834223545F58C781.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

9F19C559F4744DAE8596EB17FB4B6E20.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, identifying any fallacious reasoning or exaggerated or distorted evidence.

3D1FF5FE30DA4959A4ECD101C6613B6B.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally), evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

A53CCDAFC7AB474AA84B5AAFF689CE9E.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and disagreement, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

BF6EC5A7A7AC4AF5B7CDAA07A6508E73.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions.

09D1A28F3DE84C4F96198E9A48003A30.description: Work with peers to set rules for collegial discussions and decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views), clear goals and deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

CCCC2C89B34345ED8F49C9B765D1E874.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

FAE3F1EE5653422E9CCFE6CBF280A637.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on Grade 9 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

5B94C4B7D4EC442195B9E6DC531081E1.description: Write routinely over extended time frames, including time for research, reflection, and revision, and shorter time frames such as a single sitting or a day or two for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

4319580961AE41489E9E3AA89AC1616F.description: Apply Grade 9 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning").

923F574CA7E541669B84AC5374B7A6B7.description: Apply Grade 9 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work [e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare]").

9939EFEE9FAE485EB1E555C1A0DC54CB.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4F0A43F13B9240808478D631BCD9FC15.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

16F97BD5D794480E8FE3E85F32976FF6.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

075223667F5140BE8E4803845809E1FA.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7FEC31C1A98E4325AB6D3B236453ACDC.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

216EAFDFE2DA4E40BADE7F1273509337.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of the first three standards in the Language strand in Grades K-9.)

5486F67EB14344D3B6CD52DE98754ACF.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 20-22 above.)

7BE62E090BF84FCF8B5471D1DD491FB4.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

92FCA8F7B9F1476C883D6ED05DF7A82C.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

2C12F72166C14098A4507511EBB165FF.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole.

64AC5E0636004BDD9A7F24AF1C0A59F0.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

11D9F988EDB84F88AD7E2D3B49FC7477.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator, characters, or both; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

9E20E545047749B39D6625EF34043CFB.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

F6FC0238830346F9811FC5737AF28E91.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

714E06C93F804D76A39F8FF9AA2EE5EA.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

EA2BD41605C24B1B88EE97A32D5D40F9.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic.

56015B4A5CC04B71BE4AB1FBA06C4718.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

1D731E7567BD45AA822E8B21782894C8.description: Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant, and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

1DC9B019B0A34700BE471B333D08A540.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

33D215604B7549A0A2D5F2D223D461D8.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

CCA3D16901A24A3BA7ED21FF7F9D4CC3.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

532555E228424D85A220295E5C16087E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

B40DC7A40CF24B7FBF83C32025839939.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

12D1BB0DBDCF4F5694F16BF57875C434.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.

6E53986D1AF24463B392EC130705DB5D.description: Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

569CAF8CD82E4ADD9EA3E1E58C0B51DA.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

CCC98AD4C5A74A9396BDD43FEA3F41B3.description: By the end of Grade 9, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the Grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

5C53346E4328484A87D759C6018676CB.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

AE418DC4FEEE4C028471BC8C451831B5.description: Analyze seminal European documents of historical significance (e.g., Magna Carta; English Bill of Rights; The Social Contract, or Principles of Political Right), including how they address related themes and concepts included in United States' documents of historical and literary significance.

0C55B76F8C4040098771449D1EF5E933.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning.

EF1299C9181349FDB5BB53CF2C7B9E90.description: Analyze various accounts of a subject told in different mediums (e.g., a person's life story in both print and multimedia), determining which details are emphasized in each account.

BBC450026EE04791873E3D65F12B804C.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how an author uses rhetoric to advance that point of view or purpose.

052DF15523CF472091B565123422A197.description: Analyze in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of a text (e.g., a section or chapter).

6FFE1EDEDB3D4F4F88FF05351FA34DE5.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language of a court opinion differs from that of a newspaper).

9FAE75A2402647648158FEA2CF2E42E7.description: Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of ideas or events, including the order in which the points are made, how they are introduced and developed, and the connections that are drawn between them.

FAFC43B91C1D418AA48A50E42E7418BF.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

CCABEDDF6BF1447092F706273A0F4393.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

4C9D0110E7FE4F3D956AA1E8AF69D09F.description: By the end of Grade 9, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the Grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

44B7898D8C0346AC99CAC4F7AEAA9B10.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

542F37C792C949A7A4775DBE48142A67.description: Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work (e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare).

DC36B6861BD44F0C8D4D338A70C8BFCB.description: Analyze the representation of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment (e.g., Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).

20C27D641C3F4BB0A8141289C9E4EFBC.description: Analyze a particular point of view or cultural experience reflected in a work of literature from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature.

447553269DB04CC6A6495731660A38C2.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure a text, order events within it (e.g., parallel plots), and manipulate time (e.g., pacing, flashbacks) create such effects as mystery, tension, or surprise.

79A3B1D558284DEDBDA1B3ED71247604.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language evokes a sense of time and place; how it sets a formal or informal tone).

4E57A6075221400384DB64F053504119.description: Analyze how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

D801F1F12413495A9C60443C1EBD88B0.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze in detail its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

B6BAC957E61247CABBAD4C210157FC26.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

CDD9E4711AC84BADB32BD13A5CA18121.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression

DF9E70B6341D4D7DBE217717F5843461.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

03BC2E8D96F146F8BDE200B8FB537B59.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

420AD6EB4A5F495185EFAA79EAF59D29.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

E7F83C5D4FB74103B77D5BD6FB47F9AA.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

066AE3CDADA04AEB9FA8C21FEC756FDA.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D17EF5A08CF9443BAED4453B76E5C563.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

F7A056DD438B4810BA8367F059851453.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

C0D6E15B2B0843A3BD52033312C24233.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

F37B166427744A958ACCB1B6918A398A.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

BA46FE54307B42D182C81B7EF1B7112D.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

B45BBAD1268B402BBFFB8F5457706F6D.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

3828490A8F424E9299A63BFEDD0CFF86.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

1D674FD2BBFC48699B98AB47F1F75FBD.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

F60CA6B868CB46AC817BB3E6D454DE3A.description: Write routinely over extended time frames, including time for research, reflection, and revision, and shorter time frames such as a single sitting or a day or two for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

B08188FBF58E48729C46F104E579433A.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

33E0BA31D7E549069C34E62DA4645425.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

01D13B16008B4ED29BDC63D28C743F6B.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

6BDF05F34FBA4580B36862DABADC6B1D.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D4D8CD70359C4B92816EADFF12CD4A3D.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

CB1043979BB8459E91F71A813407C371.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

0C82DE64BC994CA9818D5A7E45B03CBD.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

14040729CD224ED6971EC05F160CE6F9.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

5271DAFE74D8412EB7B8D856556511A2.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

2AAC62483B624E09945822694A9D9385.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

42F59764D55C4CD98FB2E227983711DC.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

56701A1149464A98883AEF1CBC2E36E1.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

835F56032211449D85EF9BCA01516053.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

F030BC959010499AB01B58F57E07B537.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

2A0F403344554F5DA9E22A8E1264A540.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

AC368577D3C44365BE737AAD74EACBD3.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse formats and media, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

238794E8BC5D4DE482850B71F0C0E5F8.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

2F8F282AA2F04091A370439ACE140497.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

F68C09D0001240E9AB9ED618A9AED0FC.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

AD35CAE0D38843F5B508BDAF18BA1ADB.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

A88ACF9FD6F94FF6A75095B0F8C00AE0.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

10DAF7931B4D4141912197EFE3F10B4D.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

E8349961097D4C7E825A9CC25037C313.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares; describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc.; and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, or four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

1F7EFC51988B44AE9E570EB05B250472.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares, and count to find the total number of them.

82E5BD80AB29449EACB1623785CDC4BD.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. (Sizes are compared directly or visually, not compared by measuring.) Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.

0DD2ECCD400D4365A16EE8F9967F2931.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

DF04002D4B5A4A4585A259A8B82A6627.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

A3FCC13EDE434F548DE7A5D4FD24C7B3.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

47A0D98619C447F28B0C459C1370298E.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.

E4D52D6F82574C94A945D4AF138E5BF0.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

16627D55FE854E00ACD1A400061EB228.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2…, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

66E2879AD2BB422F83BE28FFACAEDB80.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

D9DE605A7CD84553A8091D9F4D181115.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

C0C998F286764095AF8EE1E4FF3ADEEC.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

B45B9AF159F6400E80A8D3D6857FFCC3.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

480F81185E754C479836376B925235A8.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

839899281FF54C239613358D4A014FB9.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

CBC68920908D41CB97879087A6E36B6A.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

CF9BCF78CCD04FEE973D8AA0F7972EAC.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations. (Explanations may be supported by drawings or objects.)

9D6B83CDC94746A28BAC17ACE2F34A66.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100 – 900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100 – 900.

1170082842FF4C75B1A82DFFC68334A7.description: Add and subtract within 1000 using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

D050D4C2D1474D59A21CC0C16EDD2F40.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

93F1016663F54BC591A28691FFC03344.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

2C945F27172343B2AD8B10B470F991A2.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

9D02B8836B644F9EA8E81F39B324F40F.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

5573F59F762C4506B5F2719845F6C96E.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

F2448FCD51D24961A39F20F7DACCB90F.description: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

32CC1AA4A8CA44838E8F2A2A30E9D90E.description: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens, called a "hundred."

1B1D44F810254D6FBEB114680611753B.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:

5C5B768DCCA44F4D8DDC73BEDF6FB891.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

767461C3A9094FD28C55890460A76EF3.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

E0B2877D83CC46BC88D7D8F0E4A6189A.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

101A9E032FB245479FF30E635FE8867C.description: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

E8BF776E77504E8580AD51F5C475615B.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.

40BB17BC03F742DEBB2EF2E01D8ED56D.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

1A72D44E88A34CE58F30D51FC7F2C5CC.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: English Language Arts

B8383131839D45A2AE8D06B532D8C7CA.description: Use the relationship between particular words to better understand each of the words.

85B84AEC1C0A435F94E2882725BB6473.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g. verbal irony, puns) in context.

808F6798E24144AD9B4C8E3A73510E6B.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

E289E0B2F2AF4E38BC5B8768ECDDDE88.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

1F117452D8A94CA9B26644B20C197DD8.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

F76E041A7BDE48CAADEBAC8F7917264C.description: Use verbs in the active and passive voice and in the conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects (e.g., emphasizing the actor or the action; expressing uncertainty or describing a state contrary to fact).

A520DEE8D6964E6E9B2116ACFC12EF26.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

6B50C8DA048F4E7BAEB41C05A3FC0A1B.description: Use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.

2918883EE03C420CA265898E853A9553.description: Use punctuation (comma, ellipsis, dash) to indicate a pause or break.

AC36242101E64B74BF8E80C52A7C4CFD.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4E70DDAD90B04B82BED5CCD73202F7AF.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb voice and mood.

AF8DFAA0375B4BC6AA326824A5392076.description: Form and use verbs in the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional, and subjunctive mood.

DFCCB7E251D146A3A57FACCB19F9F925.description: Form and use verbs in the active and passive voice.

8C201774980F4737ACD751DA50D59324.description: Explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives) in general and their function in particular sentences.

EE214D1F16194758B25BB7C65312B98F.description: Apply rules of subject-verb agreement when interrupted by a prepositional phrase, with inverted word order, with indefinite pronouns as subjects, compound subjects joined by correlative and coordinating conjunctions, and collective nouns when verb form depends on the rest of the sentence.

03B29C503C444D5894032517079471AE.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

C1F0D29A9B5B4276AF71926F28EEE6D1.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

378E8D495CC742CEA512AB57A197513F.description: Integrate multimedia and visual displays into presentations to clarify information, strengthen claims and evidence, and add interest.

E083592F6B13427E9D4D912DFA0A6657.description: Analyze the purpose of information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and evaluate the motives (e.g., social, commercial, political) behind its presentation.

87A88D907D42445183E3B742C6BF4A68.description: Pose questions that connect the ideas of several speakers and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant evidence, observations, and ideas.

3B91DC1173ED402BBABA181E38D12C4F.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions and decision-making, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

E95574D80C74482D8AB18FED36EB0CCF.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

712C18409F0F4ED4BA0249F1461A151E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on Grade 8 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

ABB254AB414A413E9146A55892DBEABC.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
