E15A0118E1E24B9E902AD18070BAA915.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

524A93F46BF9427680404F9D76ABC40F.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

70A0DD91E47240AE875E7B23F6220DFD.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

E834ECB0543B498C914D6A68B4E98248.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

B30DDEDEFA6F4121B1C0A68E6A9CD14D.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

1F132356093449D08462F6B5F4CEC5CD.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

7C950B94BE6C40C6AD13F7EA852C1C10.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

21FBD8267BD144B38B256B461A1A1FC3.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

5733FFA82D4748D6B2665A533F35B270.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

ECEA3D05390E49FAB0C8DA61C096B1DE.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

E6D0F9359BA643A78A4E4738A5C1BFCA.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the Grades 6-8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

AF55BD2201ED4071815539813A737C93.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1E0E4CB04A16467BB4FE44F1CA04FABC.description: Analyze a case in which two or more texts provide conflicting information on the same topic and identify where the texts disagree on matters of fact or interpretation.

DF8395E672A343918D635ECDAC7987E7.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

76455C550080411FA7B5DEB3DFF3D302.description: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using different mediums (e.g., print or digital text, video, multimedia) to present a particular topic or idea.

670D2776A03D43A98BE33F18D0B9736F.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author acknowledges and responds to conflicting evidence or viewpoints.

10F1E5E1019E4293B4C3EFFC7594861D.description: Analyze in detail the structure of a specific paragraph in a text, including the role of particular sentences in developing and refining a key concept.

167171D4316C49CFAAA2FC491FDED414.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

CAB6D45442564E1896265AFAB3617EB7.description: Analyze how a text makes connections among and distinctions between individuals, ideas, or events (e.g., through comparisons, analogies, or categories).

A31B4B40D2354E49AFE44BD0FA43B9D9.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to supporting ideas; provide an objective summary of the text.

19D60D05A57345589BD5BF3F702D128E.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

7192238534CC4EA2B9B4E9B2649C5D30.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of Grades 6-8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

2617F4CB2513486797F7ED740BABF0E5.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

74B154EDFBD34FA39AB57D62E0BC604C.description: Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works such as the Bible, including describing how the material is rendered new.

1613068D843244449888BEFA9E7C08A4.description: Analyze the extent to which a filmed or live production of a story or drama stays faithful to or departs from the text or script, evaluating the choices made by the director or actors.

093C0F6A51644710976B4581D9FC6570.description: Analyze how differences in the points of view of the characters and the audience or reader (e.g., created through the use of dramatic irony) create such effects as suspense or humor.

8A8B8FD3F777430D9D44E391F35C85D2.description: Compare and contrast the structure of two or more texts and analyze how the differing structure of each text contributes to its meaning and style.

2570AE5CF06B428C80CF9B7F986CF15E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

4C9B53ECE8BF4CCEAA54B367916E8E0C.description: Analyze how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.

071D34FE8ECE410294FCC2B601D9BF63.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to the characters, setting, and plot; provide an objective summary of the text.

9C5047868FD94AE5A5C6CFA26BA03EEE.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

F58BE0A63FBA473EB8DF2D63F3965B60.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression

9DE175197DFC454F8933657225DCB1A9.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

6CB1E76AF4DC429A99A87D6B50164E0E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

37417443B93042D38E86200D473320CE.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

88EEE20A79494B6EAC6BB6F7B9F09825.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

0C77FB21D9974F718462BED469CDF5C4.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

FAB5E88DD11348659B0763938F0DD496.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

434383211F334FA1963724F438397DF5.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

EE18EE7099DD4E9793B7B59C56379385.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

42ADA8053C304A87AE2DF0DA2B728B8D.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

1444C80165FD404D8A60F3A6FAB4A61C.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

E3E8420215CB482585CE3BF168DEFE4F.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

5F48A1FE416D4D3880C7441AD0958A9E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

7143E25AA40D45A6BD7E61E1AE3B2E6E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

15AC58485F474115A18F7356792DA07D.description: Write routinely over extended time frames, including time for research, reflection, and revision, and shorter time frames such as a single sitting or a day or two for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

623753B010BE4CA4A839BB1F03534A96.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

3EB29C0BF7D24D28BA2D2095D8EECFBC.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

CBA59A1E005E4E87B759217023D8DA8D.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

7BB80C48A1D947E8B2A5578DF871A48B.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

379A8CDD9CC647FF90FA0213B203B1E8.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

12831FA7384846398F8E4F987729500F.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

073CC9E72045438E8C17AF0F8DC90B1C.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

5FA23280F7034E42BCBD990272D70FCF.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

837167E8640A4374883C7E943B21CA49.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

8F8FFE766F424CE489140FFCA2F22AB7.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

64FCD319510A42A4BD416452F5DC2E42.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

D907C6D9B77848EA950FF5CB891C2539.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

D370B8632CE34D88B7227935F3C4BB49.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7624DED8659549BE85BA4053DECBC53D.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

25AAD798E7EA4E728CE82D391AE46B26.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

015FC607BAC44C868752AB74C051C107.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse formats and media, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

BFC5114982E04FE1AB4A78958F0FEBF1.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

0B28260B1B8A4DEEB586A4A4D44503B7.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

AD0EEA3EFE404444BCDD3DEB36848364.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

E4BE637BE29A432A817E1EF3A7D7D659.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

0041B5BCBF304E38820955A74355A460.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

92EF9A17E6E9466C8FFB46113C1CAA36.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

D8D84C016C4741AC8CC4EE12CC73E8AE.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

D54D2AAE0F9C47A790D299D0B5EA25B1.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.

22D5BF3CD0EC4038924AC68E600FB722.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

3305068C81D04EB6AF8B36116E338E76.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices or "corners"), and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

AA38CCC03607477983AD2BF6E7CEC8B2.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

5763584CCF4849A19218368913D17826.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

CE347202868043108846120419E65595.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

412B474F3C7845DB8CEA01519C0BA626.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

52D14F337C1840C2B1876696558C9E42.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

BFF07032291B4DBF89B88ED2C3BF0DD7.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the number of objects in each category, and sort the categories by count. (Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.)

17B648D21573452CA061A2D6321F3FAF.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

D203E5EC00254977ABB6424FCEE2F2E0.description: Directly compare two objects, with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of" or "less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.

D1E24D476AD54DFA91E6995ABC1855EA.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

8E7C8E707BB94B51A7F534E9D71BDB9D.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

9102002CBE3D4762BF8AB336C616AE00.description: Work with numbers 11–19 to gain foundations for place value.

C4E8AF45652B4333BFA0F4841D9CDF82.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

DC4D48F5FA584BCDBEDFAD5488024013.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

0802B9D231344B5A9C952FFDD5F265A2.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

2258A190B50B4B748DF6A746849464CA.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

1A0E57117267432BB92692C9C781F8D7.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations. (Drawings need not show details, but should show the mathematics in the problem. This applies wherever drawings are mentioned in the Standards.)

363B465BE09944CC95A1E14C61B3B2D8.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

AE77B1A550A549C8B4680CA4716AA474.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

B6E8C103C4F4493597E3FB6EE5705137.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies. (Include groups with up to ten objects.)

C84C5C41886A49D8BB22AE3A9135B1B8.description: Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1-20, count out that many objects.

5D1E913830D9461EAE80D1439C4C5541.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

1D2562EC9BE44A9A9FAA75E17340472A.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

5E4DB164015B4DF18EF67A9F0C763F26.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

EC79F73B2911408696ABF3189FE103B8.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

93C8E2BEBF274C9DB91848254DB5D4D4.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

A210976A686B4E809BB45CF902AB59E6.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

A435841C0287459DBD1357A164467816.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

CBD68368DB304E45AB78D223BB25FDF3.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

0047A0A7A26D4328B8AE0AE42D68DE7C.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

CFC97B5574CB40B288BC8E8841961599.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

8F582849FB684D65841D65E8EBBAEDE3.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables, and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

0D5DD6F73B0443FA805B579E5C2164D1.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

8E34999C6DF34E2F95B3A6A9217FB5D6.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

B18560B233B248DFA2970BEBA36037BB.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

90856D9A744C4249B07858B659B97271.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

22471A16AAEE48C3A2476E6A17697AFF.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

082E34491819418AAB49BA91DAE76CB6.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

BD48E8D8F6D04CCC9B1F361651B3314D.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

8B2F0175A4144F0DB4353200DB754FA1.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

FC395ECF333647C2B4D4C59C90B25893.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

781FD3D8929946488E906AAC3A80905A.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.

C11A5EFFC0B24C0A8DAF0E3CF133F0DB.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

94129B5034284BDD8EDB117E2419A031.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

60F8E07CD36A4C238E00A5DCE6BD5E15.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

214F4EBDAD974405914E219CF04310E0.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

CE6C558398A4471E8AFA5F99536F0CE8.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality, and interpret it in the context of the problem.

631C0B3E6DDE4FEDBFA0443446AB0AAC.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.

E7CD4EA589B74BA7A356E56D61507B7E.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

A90155C77F814ABE8CC181B2DFEF5423.description: Solve multistep real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form, convert between forms as appropriate, and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

4717C23F2357435EA82D5A76F2FBF088.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

33BEC3547BC74722BA844DBAF6A618CE.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem, and how the quantities in it are related.

DEC3136A42AF4194945B32371B5C12A2.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

4C56A354F80344E9A6DEA6F8A7CF021C.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

07AA0D2309624B7BBEB2A27C3FF0A990.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers. (Computations with rational numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex fractions.)

E13949BBCF5C4922A9C9F27ECFC86704.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

AA013326368042F7B1A78ECC2E8108F6.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

4A474B97C4A74095B87912892E2959BA.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with nonzero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then –(p/q) = (-p)/q = p/(-q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

5F914FCF714A4B1A96A21BE5994AF065.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

C3A8C0E23AB94597A7D9CC57950EDC3C.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

B9D23850811D410D9173F73908531DAD.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

D33D83F943EE4DF9802B4D6173F31E26.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

5974D0BDDFBC4EF8BB9AEAE285519FBA.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

6E5F94A70F2741D38CDCF8B81AD2FDAB.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.

B2FA199CB73340AEB9A5211E79C689CA.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

3C719DC0B59E44B1BB95321EEE5ED1BB.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

877B87D285B942B089A5CD2B334DD303.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems.

472BF69A4EDF4C2A96E17BEEA8425916.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

B192A271F48F426C925ADE71B922D3A9.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

130026C3A2D14966BC7B6E51A11122CB.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

DD66DE2B8B6A43FD9021E04551C9ED42.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

31661D0A105A4BCAADCE77755499C1D6.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas, and other quantities measured in like or different units.

6F9B4B896FFF405BAD0798B0049D5A8C.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

AA5A018EFEB848EEAE3E6CE776E5F86A.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume, and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

2D83436688784DE3921B763E88663E32.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multistep problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

A8AF7B6217B6484AA69386F5EC7B7B9C.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle, and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

6C9DE5CF8E1F44C8850878FAF7D76039.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

DB0CFDE1D86248B5B24AC561298F796D.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

BA83D9C16BAA4BAAB5D12DF16EE57AD4.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

B6D2390B4AF54C35B0062F9F4245A47F.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

5349116775194D73B4183C1D24DD6C7D.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: English Language Arts

159A729F4C0F496D8752C982629B712C.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

36154BFA12F04EFD8A9FFCC3C8E8E3D5.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

8577973742714E609FBD75424A60049A.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.

CDCA101E94424C6691BC6F031ABD2C72.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.

712E92BB3E4F4E9F89255029EC30A286.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

9071D88FBCA5475DB5D6988C666420E7.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

3C1DD008E2C64A18BD65A857D1DE9A4C.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

9897C30183ED49A4911A6B0C76C22B59.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

8FE7071E2C6C4B35AA6AF8A28742DC96.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

15445506DA024D10992B513F16DA7CF1.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on Grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

7574D782BBD94A209B59CAC64893BDE8.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

E38980BCD2104E1E98D78054303C3230.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader or listener interest, and style.

5936DCD4A4D647C59E8B16B8F9F15CEA.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

48D662546C2944AA93077DCBF9D9A319.description: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive or parenthetical elements.

EB7B232DD0474BF4B0C8594EB1FA7425.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

76D1F7580D954177839C42BB858626F9.description: Recognize variations from Standard English in their own and others' writing and speaking, and identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.

74CDB965E4D645B99BB6581390221C3A.description: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).

431D62D2188847C6821A914885DD008C.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

F36BF56167134F688C1A1714CE5CFD22.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

C6D75C09E65B4103BB3A2981BC103CD8.description: Demonstrate knowledge of subject-verb agreement when interrupted by a prepositional phrase, with inverted word order, and with indefinite pronouns as subjects.

017D7037CD9345B7950AE83C37BA8532.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9A2A4B8CDE9941D48F399ED86672D7C7.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

19C65B97E2C34C0BA239D33E28D4C18B.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, images, music, sound) and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.

9D12C88C90D3411D9A4A41F4E492CD5C.description: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

15D5BEC4C2E14A3298A674E567F72AE8.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

154F0E42297449628FAC0E492CB72E45.description: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.

4A43CB0A408B405CA8D7643C9AC2EFF8.description: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.

08F767F4840947248F7F71A9A1DD4D5D.description: Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.

C06762A03AEB44B582048E6DC735F19D.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

A722A6F5043E48A9893743783B1E83B9.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

60985DA0BAF74D0EAD234D5AE8692FD6.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on Grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

2C4D4B5D7CF74B9A86693C818702E06B.description: Write routinely over extended time frames, including time for research, reflection, and revision, and shorter time frames such as a single sitting or a day or two for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

196065BB496A4720A3421D4A5E552E61.description: Apply Grade 6 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not").

C43B0D3F2A0C4D04B78724800F622D78.description: Apply Grade 6 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres [e.g., stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories] in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics").

D0A5F5FB4D084E058EEEFDA713BA2EED.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

D59AFD02E7B44C889637732098B1CD5D.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources; assess the credibility of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic bibliographic information for sources.

3E14D66B58B54229B6AECE0B51051D94.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.

D6F2CCF9021841918E7AB366B7550806.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D42004E4B0344CA2A13DC47E6BCA1E46.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of three pages in a single sitting.

20A41CF9E0AE4EBB95CFD7E47D71255D.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of the first three Language standards in Grades K-6.)

3FB5F4B7EB4F4AEA84918E100CF5E300.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 21-23 above.)

ED94B036A2014C419AC709C7ACB118C0.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

6695934D30A14C68B69B922FE7A0F2D6.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to convey experiences and events.

BF361D5AF583455A95C266BA8EC56E7E.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.

A38B63C24919441E8EC0EECA498230AF.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

F65F728053324256BB5049AB6C4C2F1E.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and introducing a narrator, characters, or both; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

083129A0A8B4434A97515879A22BBF08.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

E6ED3AED07F04E9DA5C0EB32513B75C6.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the information or explanation presented.

47A47B261C224DBFA3CCFB6107E55C77.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

7A1A60715E2145BCAE314381800FC3A3.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

DDBD96BF159A4369894FD7855564B8E2.description: Use appropriate transitions to clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

21D7FF5FA17B4F06A7944C0FD4966296.description: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

CCFF3FC3D11B465DA12B7285CD5C8C03.description: Introduce a topic; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison or contrast, and cause and effect; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

E35AE11816A0407FA5FD80C6B64C9B2F.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

257E0B0A212748D0A2781E39D3013A83.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the argument presented.

EBB4AA946F2A4959A43DFA8FC6E69E3D.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

F3EC54A6543D404F9ED31746F0BD9A13.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to clarify the relationships among claim(s) and reasons.

70BA4A5A38D942B1BA45FB511847176D.description: Support claim(s) with clear reasons and relevant evidence, using credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

21ACEBD3CDD54AFD8D2238DDB212B04F.description: Introduce claim(s) and organize the reasons and evidence clearly.

614DBAE5C17941FEA5916D535E75DFBB.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

2932827AB7474DB1AAD83995CC8B857C.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the Grades 6-8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

E600060415E3455C94BC6AB62DC38828.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1DFC67E7BD0E474594AB8E767E7A3D12.description: Compare and contrast one author's presentation of events with that of another (e.g., a memoir written by and a biography on the same person).

11489216909B41EEB37677262CAF25EE.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

63BCF965B48A4849BAC34707C615498E.description: Integrate information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words to develop a coherent understanding of a topic or issue.

D83B48CA40124DC5BCD0565D239BACFE.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and explain how it is conveyed in the text.

72F65A49D1D54509A6AD28D80557F601.description: Analyze how a particular sentence, paragraph, chapter, or section fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the ideas.

2A92FA4B000045ED89943EEC9F23EDD7.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings.

C0BFB9820A0E4DFB82543EE4001B8E2E.description: Analyze in detail how a key individual, event, or idea is introduced, illustrated, and elaborated in a text (e.g., through examples or anecdotes).

0C013D55D39540938AEE37E01CE10F3C.description: Determine a central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

62C48A15F1534FA888BAA472F6D9C326.description: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

099D26E545D94F5693E9090DDC492019.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the Grades 6-8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

C28B92671FB340CBAE11F18E194475CE.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

619B5BD8F31549CE91DBA97E541FEA59.description: Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres (e.g., stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories) in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics.

F492273C7D8044A3A546D95B6A6C0E62.description: Differentiate among odes, ballads, epic poetry, and science fiction.

4C387BEED2654E508B2A35B94F811DDF.description: Compare and contrast the experience of reading a story, drama, or poem to listening to or viewing an audio, video, or live version of the text, including contrasting what they "see" and "hear" when reading the text to what they perceive when they listen or watch.

FC642881D3C74793B07D2936AF15C835.description: Explain how an author develops the point of view of the narrator or speaker in a text.

859ABDCF0D1E42DF8886F61FBB63E007.description: Analyze how a particular sentence, chapter, scene, or stanza fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the theme, setting, or plot.

D08CF103AE514A3B9080D20CDA2EBB51.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

5D578C1AF69D496383D92B350F5F2C49.description: Describe how a particular story's or drama's plot unfolds in a series of episodes as well as how the characters respond or change as the plot moves toward a resolution.

E9FCF8E5658D453481A93E5E2198DEFB.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

8A63BEDC6CC74FB89D90BDF94C84FA3C.description: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

68E0C4D9015C4A7DBB6C64BF38A85B5C.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression

FEE86B41A4EB4250B0B7E9B107CF0108.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

56DC779EBB6549E6B5F2A6FE3F9A349C.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

FAA75258BD3D4D96A24CA474DDAC1896.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

BED562F979204359A346EA851D229E75.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

E013E99483D94615A36E0AACA3E0D2C9.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

918DCCA2EC2D4A399CDAD0A5134E6638.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

1E3BBD921B894F5CB86CE5243D3B86A5.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

51C001C3288C4340B6024EC504E63CD5.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

6657AC11CC9C441CA59F7EBA79257408.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

55958C49F5A6421DA03EFC4B086021EE.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

C8E8ED72BEA341B3A31BBE630DB32E89.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D0A2699F40CB4CEA972C5754C1B92A4A.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

33E086E7EB35401887BB1908A58D3904.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

494F5392ADC7447D8A0C72A7A3F8BABD.description: Write routinely over extended time frames, including time for research, reflection, and revision, and shorter time frames such as a single sitting or a day or two for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

BF3CD43FA1EA45408E277777D165F2D4.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

D0FD9431557A47E4BB7DB3F6ADE78AB9.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

31260EF5C82449F4818CF8AA54829732.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4B060F561A6849488B39D5BF9809966F.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DDA8DAB2B05A45FA93106C20281A289F.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

7EB388B02EBD40F8943D09347D585C64.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

76CB5278830A4D6EBBA944C7113267A4.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

040B4162D5B640A4BECC5A06042BC497.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

A89A6368857349E69BA3138549E85988.description: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

C630C9C22DB04D8395FE746C580E59D4.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

B3141DEEB8DE4A56A93E4573EE79744C.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

9559ED5E21624E62B71DCBD69D1499E3.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

AF86CA4206214B3994A89614C09B8D86.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

0B7F2C1BE371461E8E40F741059146BD.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

80987004F98A4C05ACD981CEFAED0B36.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

B9DBEEEC57A647DD930BEC29FB090B1A.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse formats and media, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

CAE05666AC274BBFAD9F473B307BAF7F.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

0BCB28756F0640189F3AE4BEFE02F60D.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

146DC886801D4BF2A170F3C395EB352F.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

C6C5725C035741F399A0EC59DBEFA31D.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

39D6F69734AD4961B0BD85490C6901CA.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

EA4ADAF2596B4048A3EBD4F4AFCB8F4E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

2427114DD3474E75AFD6626CF3850F55.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics

406BAEC05FF04FB4B91F3F3E916EC9B4.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares; describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters; and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

FE4F1887B1F74FED98FBBF9BFE94BE63.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape. (Students do not need to learn formal names such as "right rectangular prism.")

6A65797D265A48E9993309E48279358E.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

EE99F25C63834961B82F08524ED57171.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

9544CA625EDF4B229609F8C895604DA2.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

6A66E654A20740688F9BEAE34075D863.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

7C617CA092B64DBDA03F36D6DBC0E26D.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps. Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.

37AB2958ED464D1EA77216B2179683EE.description: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

0E196603F5034769A4C46BFB0D5985C3.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.

E7DB6773E15C4F89917B54536918E020.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method, and explain the reasoning used.

BEDAC641F1CB4350B9F17F96B86546EF.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

931B43A57F66460CAD48D689AFF61D93.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method, and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

40FDD1A10822481898959A047EE8AB85.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

227FB97F10E046AFBCE115BE7CF94AB0.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.

458A75DF8E7D49829A64517683BDBD94.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

73B577BF8C9C446BA1218814B02E0F3C.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

ED3975120F02453187D562311C6DB3AC.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones, called a "ten."

1FE1FBCB9F5B4AFA9221F57057E2FD0C.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

B52951E2AB6B4CBF9AD94B888C090C8F.description: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

003BC1CC69844B6387B5598F6E0F4330.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

4A1901816E8147999506C1D957010B2E.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.

59C139F2630A41A9B4557ECBEA84EAF1.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.

1D61104581D24439902DB2C54A5FEF0B.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

CCDDD079B5584C63A315BD1D319D0664.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

A157E960E24645A199F2D2D1FBEFDF09.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

73BDEC2F66064E83BE3543E4B2EF0211.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.

8028D65BCF40454CA36996A7D32B2111.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract. (Students need not use formal terms for these properties.)

5A7F1AEE48184600AEC11AD2E9ED0461.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

F6EBE582F5D24FA089C3871761A56D40.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

FBA0E3D393D6471399C7F4A434EE8852.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

429C91FD299843B5B1D9C6AAAD4FBD34.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: English Language Arts

6FBD6B8B31124778A14AE366ED299561.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

document.title: Alabama Gifted Education Programs: Standards and Student Outcomes

05F04B12BC8F4E148ABCBDC095F25C28.description:
Collaboration:  •	Use listening skills with others.
•	Respect perspectives of others.
•	Compromise and negotiate to accomplish tasks.
•	 Relinquish control while working with others.

23B31B392EF844E0BE343C11041BEFAD.description:
Goal-Setting:    •	Develop realistic goals and objectives.
•	Evaluate the time to accomplish objectives.
•	Seek resources to accomplish objectives.
•	Set benchmarks to complete objectives.

2CA264E61AA84AECA72B54EFFD9CD286.description:
Adaptability:    •	Adjust expectations and behavior according to various academic environments.
•	Identify and articulate multiple solutions, goals, or perspectives.
•	Establish a unified solution, goal, perspective from consensus among the group.

4603A49EA31F4E6F9D647A6F6594C34F.description:
Time Management:    •	Transition from one task to another.
•	Prioritize competing interests.
•	Create schedules and to-do lists in order to adhere to time constraints.

7604FF414B0E4B73942542A7CBD095EE.description:
Project Management:   •	Prioritize project elements.
•	Plan long- and short-term tasks.
•	Execute ideas to completion.
•	Self-evaluate the final projects/ideas/tasks.

E79313B0963242358202EFE7E7F51330.description:
Impulse Control:   •	Self-monitor verbal, non-verbal, and physical responses to others (including teachers) through wait time, self-talk, and reflection.
•	Code-switch according to audience.

4105079DCCEE4193A98690899D0DC0DD.description:
Decision-Making:   •	Develop, evaluate, and select criteria when given multiple alternatives.
•	Prioritize criteria.
•	Apply criteria to alternatives.
•	Explain your chosen decision based on criteria.
•	Act on selected decision.

99011AF8BCD442EAA66F6743537E70F7.description:
Organizational Skills:    •	Develop and adhere to a time schedule.
•	Develop a priority list and adjust it as needed.
•	Develop lists of goals, projects, or “to-do’s” and complete the items on the lists.
•	Re-evaluate the lists in order to prioritize greatest needs first or adjust to changing deadlines.

1673A24A596B4668A88DB338BE84F8A6.description:
Exhibit professional or business ethical behavior:    •	Define attributes of ethical principles.
•	Identify and analyze outcomes of individual actions.
•	Evaluate the individual actions for ethical practices.
•	Uphold ethical principles.

DCD9EC7A81404DA89ED0CB06CDC5198B.description:
Grow from constructive criticism:      •	Develop a receptive attitude towards feedback.
•	Reflect on the meaning of feedback received.
•	Differentiate constructive or destructive criticism.
•	Determine how to improve based upon feedback.
•	Respond to feedback with well-reasoned explanations.
•	Provide constructive criticism to others.

1661382B214B4828B17C4FA544A7E8B9.description:
Demonstrate personal flexibility:     •	Identify alternative methods of accomplishing a task.
•	Describe the benefits of developing alternative processes to accomplish a task.
•	Develop a method of transitioning from one process to an alternative.

F75740971AF64CB689076C24426F3EEC.description:
Take academic risks:     •	Identify personal learning comfort zone.
•	Analyze the value of academic risk-taking by weighing the positive/negative outcomes of taking that risk.
•	Express the importance of risk-taking.
•	Take academic risks by accepting challenges outside of comfort zones.

6F6FFC73B455420AB80123C985A39724.description:
Increase intrinsic motivation:    •	Explore and pursue areas of personal interests/curiosity/passion.
•	Demonstrate personal motivation and task commitment.
•	Develop persistence when working on challenging activities.

72B55F5955864A458C0F4A29646A988C.description:
Monitor and evaluate learning:    •	Reflect on progress as determined by established goals/timelines.
•	Self-evaluate progress of completing final tasks.
•	Revise, refine, and modify final tasks in relation to original goals and timelines.
•	Revise, refine, and modify goals and timelines in relation to the constraints of the project/situation/issue.

D6C6E5FEA73D4952BB223E94155BDCA1.description:
Demonstrate independent learning:     •	Gather, organize, analyze, and apply new knowledge.
•	Exhaust resources prior to asking for help.
•	Formulate questions that will aid in learning.
•	Set, prioritize, and achieve goals.
•	Utilize time management skills.

788F886646DA46CB9FBD76757EE02363.description:
Demonstrate an awareness of cultural diversity:    •	Recognize contributions and achievements of various cultures.
•	Recognize various forms of bias.
•	Question stereotypes.

361F87BCE3344DD6BA7A643FC31C6FED.description:
Enhance relationships with others:   •	Analyze, evaluate, and respond appropriately to various forms of body language.
•	Demonstrate respect for and empathy with others.
•	Participate in community building skills.
•	Differentiate constructive or destructive criticism.

E997BC72BC8245D0B0023823E60A8AF8.description:
Demonstrate and evaluate responsibility for personal growth:    •	Understand how attitudes, attention, and commitment can affect one’s knowledge and self-control.
•	Identify and assess strengths and weaknesses as a baseline for improvement.
•	Set goals for self-improvement and take the necessary steps to reach them.
•	Accept responsibility for choices made.
•	Develop and model self-discipline.
•	Show evidence of delayed gratification and impulse control.
•	Demonstrate leadership skills.
•	Accept failure as part of growth.

640A07A3A00243BC9396E782A8B9959A.description:
Develop self-acceptance:   •	Appreciate their personality styles.
•	Understand their asynchronous development.
•	Develop ethical practices.
•	Embrace their giftedness.
•	Develop and demonstrate appropriate self-efficacy and self-talk.

C4488C1DC72A41BE8E10343E3D0FC4EE.description:
Cope with perfectionism, goal setting, emotional intensity, anxiety, and stress:   •	Develop a healthy perception of perfectionism in accomplishing tasks.
•	Express and manage emotions in positive ways.
•	Develop a healthy response toward peer pressure and expectations of others.
•	Develop behavioral strategies appropriate to the situation.
•	Identify sources and possible solutions of stress and anxiety.

6C3F94CBF224443183FC14FAECDBD7ED.description:
Cope with inner feelings:     •	Understand and evaluate the social, emotional, and academic implications of giftedness.
•	Understand and analyze feelings and emotions in self.
•	Identify feelings and emotions in self.
•	Identify and utilize appropriate personal perceptual filters and defense systems for situations.

968B6E9A09BB44D5927D5CEB702A9C4E.description:
Computer Programming:    •	Write basic programs and macros in one or more computer programming languages.
•	Be familiar with differences among programming languages.
•	Understand the principles of good software design.

A76C312CC3F64D2E9A3E5E085BFF3D09.description:
Web Site Creation:   •	Design Web sites that appropriately convey desired information.
•	Understand principles of good Web site design including differences between Web site design and other forms of presentation.

01A42501846244D2AA63A3DD985702E6.description:
Project Development:   •	Identify appropriate technological tools for use in academic and creative projects.
•	Plan, create, and upload technological communications and/or presentations, using technological software, online applications, or apps that may include blogs, WIKIS, podcasts, videos, and webinars.

11372D5CE50A47BBA7C76FA2284690E5.description:
Software:   •	Identify and use software appropriate to educational tasks, including but not limited to, web browsers and office-productivity suites.
•	Explore and evaluate alternative software options (e.g., compare and contrast different office-productivity programs such as Word and OpenOffice).

4C5AA902E7D745258D3967D61DE0B521.description:
Technology Use:  •	Apply troubleshooting strategies to correct issues.
•	Use digital tools and strategies to locate, collect, organize, evaluate, and synthesize information.
•	Apply the principles of safe and appropriate Internet use including cyber-safety and “netiquette.”
•	Use digital environments to collaborate and communicate.

54441FAF055148F78ABCDAE9C3CCC3DE.description:
Demonstrate the ability to communicate research findings:   •	Identify appropriate audience.
•	Select an appropriate medium (form) in terms of audience, impact and type of information/data for which it is best suited.

79AC77D2CAA04F8A95857981B3F08AB2.description: Develop conclusions and implications based on the problem:   Draw conclusions and develop generalizations based on and supported by data gathered in the course of research.

0427D0CA077445E3BE5D7DE416D11482.description: Synthesize and interpret information:   Make inferences about the data with respect to trends, future directions, similarities, and differences.

B6ED2FC54E4A44D3BC36AFBFD44DAF07.description:
Organize and integrate information/data   Create and visually organize your data (Chart, table, graph, map, web, or outline) using the various categories:
•	Chronological order.
•	Sequence of steps.
•	Generalizations. •	Evidence.
•	Patterns.
•	Outline.
•	Compare/contrast.
•	Cause/effect.

C6828278747A4967B971FDA6EBB54C5C.description:
Assess the validity, reliability, and relevance of the information collected:        •	Evaluate sources with respect to date, aspects covered, information provided, and relevance to the study.
•	Compare and contrast authors/interview subjects with respect to qualifications.

45C22324A8794500B0AD1D72730C8390.description:
Collect information from primary and secondary sources using print and electronic media:    •	Analyze the differences between primary and secondary sources.
•	Employ various digital tools, media, and strategies to locate and collect accurate and reliable information.
•	Take simple, accurate notes.
•	Understand ethics in copyright/fair use and cite sources to avoid plagiarism.

7E2F97B7354A4D04B27CC2A20AC210C1.description:
Select and apply a research methodology appropriate for the topic:    •	Select appropriate research method:  case studies; historical studies; interviews; surveys; scientific method; descriptive research.
•	Construct a hypothesis.
•	Design a plan or experiment to test the hypothesis.

527C0669CA52444889AD96469EA307D4.description:
Identify a topic and formulate questions for research:     •	Analyze the topic/problem/issue to determine areas to be researched.
•	Brainstorm questions related to the topic/problem/issue.
•	Identify related topics/problems/issues.
•	Identify a specific topic for research.
•	Formulate significant, complex questions for study.

0A7017B78C734A5FBB3676C345DB0140.description:
Nonverbal (including Artistic and Kinesthetic):   •	Plan, create, and present a nonverbal performance in order to share thoughts and ideas to a variety of authentic audiences. •	Experience expression through various nonverbal forms.
•	Select, analyze, and utilize appropriate visual aids for effective communication.

260F18A352EE447D94E17892F7270BB3.description:
Written:       •	Plan, create, and present written information in order to share thoughts and ideas to a variety of authentic audiences.
•	Create unique compositions that utilize their own voice.
•	Edit and refine all written communications by applying proofreading and editing skills.

A3B7EFAAB17549A2A9C9EECC67DE660A.description:
Oral:           •	Plan, create, and present information orally in order to share thoughts and ideas to a variety of authentic audiences.
•	Contribute (with confidence) to a group or class discussion of a concept, topic, theme, issue, or problem.
•	Develop appropriate listening and speaking skills to effectively communicate a concept and/or idea to an audience and respond appropriately.
•	Support and defend personal opinions while collaborating with and respecting the opinions of others.
•	Demonstrate effective speaking skills such as appropriate rate, volume, tone, pitch, enunciation, and pace and effective body language, such as eye contact, inflection, and gestures.

C56A9D3FB8184671A192F3D6521042E9.description:
The problem solving process requires all of the following steps:
a.	Recognize and define the problem (hypotheses).
b.	Gather ideas and data.
c.	Brainstorm aspects of the problem.
d.	Identify underlying problems or sub-problems.
e.	Produce alternative solutions.
f.	Develop criteria for judging solutions.
g.	Evaluate alternative solutions using the criteria.
h.	Determine and implement possible solutions.

C113E163D3CF4E6F8984647B6236571E.description: Combine concepts and generalizations in order to create a new understanding.

F342BC8C527242E88C1064DC3995B21C.description: Combine commonplace ideas or materials in unusual ways.

A7CAF935AF5D42EA805635D321A89E69.description: Elaboration: Provide detail that is accurate and complete to enhance meaning and understanding.

475009252E98454B803EFFA4DDEBBEFD.description: Use familiar objects in ways different from their intended purposes.

6E54C0E43CEF4D6AA2E86B98F5A36537.description: Provide different or alternate outcomes in real-world situations.

43435BA95C5D4750BE4A1FAC43921C43.description: Create original ideas in order to maximize the possibility of finding the solution to the problem.

211111E1678A49EE8E39EE064B018B0E.description:
Question relationships and interpretations.                                                                                 •	Discern various interpretations of information.
•	Apply a principle or concept to different areas.•	Develop an ability to shift approaches or change directions in thinking.

D9312186FC6E41FD820EB19FD49730A1.description: Substitute, combine, adapt, magnify/minify, put to other uses, eliminate, or rearrange to change an idea or concept.

712D9DADC9D54D759746AC80E4A06B42.description: Adapt a single idea or materials to many different uses.

5E48A5B305A54FE189560ADE18936789.description: Create varied ideas in order to maximize the possibility of finding the solution to the problem.

•	Create many ideas in order to maximize the possibility of finding the solution to the problem.
•	Accept the possibility of more than one right answer.

DF76DFD15BC44BC1AD7519BA6F5B0B47.description: Prove or disprove ideas by presenting evidence.                                                                        •	Assess accuracy and relevance of points used to support conclusions.

0689B44E8AEE4032B62611BADBFFC7A5.description: Assess the organization, content, value, effectiveness, and results of action/decision.

088F864B2070425CA9DDE3CB2CAD6F20.description:
Provide supporting evidence.                                                                                                              •	Sequence information to make points.
•	Verify solutions.

C6DA8ED5DC254ECFA71CE5FE0267BCEC.description:
Utilize inductive reasoning to solve problems.
Utilize deductive reasoning to solve problems.

12A068D754174D15B1577D593DE4588E.description:
Recognize relationships among ideas and data.                                                                    •	Compare and contrast attributes of varying ideas.
•	Classify information into logical categories.•	Analyze various perspectives.•	Analyze discrepancies in thought or information.•	Determine cause and effect of relationships and events.

79C2CAEFC13E4C4495BA1116E6FA468B.description: Identify main ideas in oral, written, and nonverbal form.

6BEE29839F9449F88142F7B8CE35B3E5.description: Analyze and evaluate the learning situation:What is known, what is not yet known, and what has been learned.                                                                                                 Summarize and justify the knowledge gained through reading, activities, and/or instruction.

790C73144A4B4A5E8A40953CFB6C91B1.description: Determine which resources  and hands-on activities will develop exploration of the topic.

BED6D3AE333C48EBBB6E95FBFDD68B8D.description: Ask questions:                                                                                                                               Before, during, and after reading and/or instruction to develop a deeper understanding. That seek reasons and evidence – why, how, what.

C1476AE85BF243E1AC7485DE977F92B0.description: Observe, analyze, implement, and record reflective thinking modeled by others

182C3810AC1F44AC9A4CE045B333FB11.description:
Develop and ask questions for cognitive development:                                                          •	Lower-level questions to develop a foundation for higher-level questions.                 •	Hypothetical questions designed to explore possibilities and test relationships.   •	Clarifying questions to examine the coherence and logic of an argument, article, an essay, editorial, or presentation.

A0FD4A4BA3664D188F6739D9ABEA83B6.description: Observe, analyze and implement abstract thinking skills modeled by others.

A4E371DD0F4E40189B0F7DCA618020DD.description: Functions model a wide variety of real situations and can help students understand the processes of making and changing assumptions, assigning variables, and finding solutions to contextual problems.

5FAE02163DAB4EB1B0C72816FDA1017C.description: Graph exponential functions, showing intercepts and end behavior.

26089195DE0744A7A051CFDAF75F2CA0.description: Graph piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

EE045D84563447A2A9427C6F63C319FA.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

8BC3670BB9844E74BDD0E44FD74E721F.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

B1E666655DDF4D1D992EBCEE397EEE04.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph. Limit to linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value functions.

2B68D8572A334C7AB81BA3254D9272E5.description: Functions can be represented graphically and key features of the graphs, including zeros, intercepts, and, when relevant, rate of change and maximum/minimum values, can be associated with and interpreted in terms of the equivalent symbolic representation.

EBCB8CE3FA3041F9BFEA0D4A8EB948E9.description: Interpret the parameters of functions in terms of a context. Extend from linear functions, written in the form mx + b, to exponential functions, written in the form abx.

76E85DF6B5A44D98BA8153386C5BC4E7.description: Use graphs and tables to show that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly or quadratically.

992A558FF17E4F36BDA057C6F360C987.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

D3846DAA02F74E208CD34A9102A0A46F.description: Define exponential functions to represent situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

3FD23B726AFE496C9BDBE506BEC66169.description: Define linear functions to represent situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

088511A6ADC84FC9A6F3A89CB7D3F6B4.description: Show that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, while exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

AFD3F02C6A9E46B193E8A3EE5E49AE75.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and those that can be modeled with exponential functions.

41992B33581840239486A7F9DA337533.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k·f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs.
