D1A5E3E957D4483DA8C3CC896B42EFB3.description: Write explicit and recursive formulas for arithmetic and geometric sequences and connect them to linear and exponential functions.

50F0B510F47B46F18FF5226130C3C432.description: Define sequences as functions, including recursive definitions, whose domain is a subset of the integers.

8C38CFD57B0945049898C15985CD2981.description: Distinguish between linear and non-linear functions.

0656DF218145490FADD82CC3617EB01C.description: Functions can be described by using a variety of representations: mapping diagrams, function notation (e.g., f(x) = x²), recursive definitions, tables, and graphs.

3799F80F49554FDCB625B44F82EEA169.description: Use arithmetic operations to combine different types of standard functions to write and evaluate functions.

4DB15C0DEA9548059E2FC07A542D2684.description: Combine different types of standard functions to write, evaluate, and interpret functions in context. Limit to linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value functions.

DB1750BB72A04E8A9E2DDB4A45FED506.description: Given a relation defined by an equation in two variables, identify the graph of the relation as the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane.

1AF7A572CAB9433781886D207CC062EA.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. Limit to linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value functions.

33CF552D77614FA782B4A5A5C26EF5ED.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

0E90A07828A34E29A025F4ABA27AC90A.description: Define a function as a mapping from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) that assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range.

81EB9672000E481787739BD583EA31F7.description: Functions shift the emphasis from a point-by-point relationship between two variables (input/output) to considering an entire set of ordered pairs (where each first element is paired with exactly one second element) as an entity with its own features and characteristics.

Limit to contexts arising from linear, quadratic, exponential, absolute value, and linear piecewise functions.

0B603330368A431D8A56BDBCFA3CB082.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities in context; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales and use them to make predictions. 1C8208EADFFE43189A0057E3E9059822.description: Contrast solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables produced by algebraic methods with graphical and tabular methods.

1E0DC5A32BAF42F6AE21F90557D840F9.description: Solve a system of two equations in two variables by using linear combinations; contrast situations in which use of linear combinations is more efficient with those in which substitution is more efficient.

B039B58CAFAD48B4AA47D7C9656B8CF6.description: Select an appropriate method to solve a system of two linear equations in two variables.

B3AA06C796B842499BADE3AFEBC83101.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Explain how the quadratic formula is derived from this form.

1F9B0CA3B0BA48ABBD726B058047ECC0.description: Select an appropriate method to solve a quadratic equation in one variable.

7FC764CE943C4B4DBB0A13DC85B3FD98.description: Explain why extraneous solutions to an equation involving absolute values may arise and how to check to be sure that a candidate solution satisfies an equation.

39A22186FA584C758F0C65AC7AB40CC6.description: Analyze the relationship (increasing or decreasing, linear or non-linear) between two quantities represented in a graph.

C74410A4F94A40DDB80FFF352085777A.description: Expressions can be rewritten in equivalent forms by using algebraic properties, including properties of addition, multiplication, and exponentiation, to make different characteristics or features visible.

681AF5E1FF2E4C67B501C0FE3B098C48.description: Analyze parallel lines cut by a transversal.

2E419A3A78394A3FA3EB1EECCB160679.description: Given a scatter plot that suggests a linear association, informally draw a line to fit the data, and assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

6AF4349E9CD84A6389131490C60626B8.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities, describing patterns in terms of positive, negative, or no association, linear and non-linear association, clustering, and outliers.

99F5C4FB4E0B49EAA25121DF185CE5BB.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

D4A70A255C994DE7BD083D32D92A1531.description: Analyze the relationship (increasing or decreasing, linear or non-linear) between two quantities represented in a graph.

B4705AD1BA944693A6DD9FD347D9EAFA.description: Interpret the rate of change (slope) and initial value of the linear function from a description of a relationship or from two points in a table or graph.

D973F6DFA4124D31BA521B7AFB59800E.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two variables.

61FD760C5B4A4937BCDA584DC8C7DE8A.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

A03CC4B86BE842DDBDB2D16F1038E2A4.description: Distinguish between linear and non-linear functions.

37339C7C32B9463D8978C85899DD4950.description: Compare properties of functions represented algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions.

430C770B8CAB44909BA6E66C4159A939.description: Evaluate functions defined by a rule or an equation, given values for the independent variable.

AEDDAA5F2B6641C9963181163EA52CB9.description: Determine whether a relation is a function, defining a function as a rule that assigns to each input (independent value) exactly one output (dependent value), and given a graph, table, mapping, or set of ordered pairs.

043D434A70F54A7892936A08989E721F.description: Explain that the solution(s) of systems of two linear equations in two variables corresponds to points of intersection on their graphs because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

667A920EE028427DB2A2F22327798E25.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables by graphing and substitution.

CB671D46CCB1494D9634B2483A8BA03B.description: Determine whether linear equations in one variable have one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b (where a and b are different numbers).

5B2D208E34354EB5B41BEB432CFF2EE2.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and systems of two linear equations.

1B78E661421B49FDA4AB15C0BCD38AC9.description: Compare proportional and non-proportional linear relationships represented in different ways (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions) to solve real-world problems.

24C1C573F24C4F2998F2564C204AB271.description: Given that the slopes for two different sets of points are equal, demonstrate that the linear equations that include those two sets of points may have different y-intercepts.

B8D39E126AB74E06936684C8CD8402F2.description: Given two distinct points in a coordinate plane, find the slope of the line containing the two points and explain why it will be the same for any two distinct points on the line.

19B677A4C5CC4FF98DE3BCA5E03D7394.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in a coordinate plane.

DC29EA62594A4523B6ADC4F9A43C8AEA.description: Interpret y = mx + b as defining a linear equation whose graph is a line with m as the slope and b as the y-intercept.

B005BE41C09A4EA687E6729349FF06E3.description: Analyze the relationship between proportional and non-proportional situations.

9CE1787DCEB540B6A6595D5A79FF5397.description: Estimate and compare very large or very small numbers in scientific notation.

668994C8155745D0BD62A89E21994ACB.description: Apply concepts of integer exponents and radicals.

BACDD85BE027421794542A664FFE0534.description: Define the real number system as composed of rational and irrational numbers.

DCE4CE5F60C14EB1B0DEF26F54EBB957.description: Understand that the real number system is composed of rational and irrational numbers.

6EEA0C89BB68470F8F94F9773B740D74.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

88BF71BF4CA64CF9948A7A362611480D.description: Look for and make use of structure.

564E676D221F4C1FBB8BE01056F2E75E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

80E9B3D69357449080BA601923232400.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

A69D23A45F224A158A5514BD082607E8.description: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials, showing that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication.

C91B0D3176D547E492E5CBDEBC4851AF.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

03059CC6F7AD4B40ABC5357242748E22.description: Use the vertex form of a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value and the axis of symmetry of the function it defines; complete the square to find the vertex form of quadratics with a leading coefficient of one.

2FFB478642714559AB5F6CCB00813986.description: Factor quadratic expressions with leading coefficients of one, and use the factored form to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

E28B9B59B0AD43A1A034E2FED0AA4F7B.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

A41B624865F24F9087DD31398C6192E6.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

FDB73116F5B84EE79283D77F6740A755.description: Interpret linear, quadratic, and exponential expressions in terms of a context by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

F059618C34FF496F9AEE48BB9378CA2D.description: Expressions can be rewritten in equivalent forms by using algebraic properties, including properties of addition, multiplication, and exponentiation, to make different characteristics or features visible.

156F51474EA441EA83B6074BBBDEB821.description: Define the imaginary number i such that i² = -1.

AC7614B560F845C6BECF4A4137868199.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

B2854D3D8ADF49B18E995F53A4CCEA38.description: Explain how the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for an additional notation for radicals using rational exponents.

7724ECC238A54B9688D2C0E031573CB9.description: Together, irrational numbers and rational numbers complete the real number system, representing all points on the number line, while there exist numbers beyond the real numbers called complex numbers.

9DDA627262E24F61BF387C5C3BCF5080.description: Use the mathematical modeling cycle involving geometric methods to solve design problems.

BE419D2064DE4AB9A5FDE3432693D302.description: Experiencing the mathematical modeling cycle in problems involving geometric concepts, from the simplification of the real problem through the solving of the simplified problem, the interpretation of its solution, and the checking of the solution's feasibility, introduces geometric techniques, tools, and points of view that are valuable to problem-solving.

A0B6B1B0FC934CA186FEA371372114D8.description: Investigate and apply relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords, including but not limited to: the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.

9E7404FD113541949D25046AE1829FA7.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to model objects and use those models to solve problems.

60764C4F1D4143D1804416E94DE8E494.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems, including finding areas of regular polygons.

C9EC980B1F2C4754B6040F2F8D575C71.description: Demonstrate the converse of the Pythagorean Theorem.

4986F03D8BF443C0AF6B9A4AB3342B4E.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

4F2E93607D37460AAF61E0E0AC35A2CE.description: Use similarity to explore and define basic trigonometric ratios, including sine ratio, cosine ratio, and tangent ratio.

8A11AEBF098346348D8DFC00A0289C33.description: Derive and apply the constant ratios of the sides in special right triangles (45˚-45˚-90˚ and 30˚-60˚-90˚).

7061CF5A5D2C465C9FE13D0A8A1594DC.description: Discover and apply relationships in similar right triangles.

F00024B709214A0E806AFD364B0FE421.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems in real-world contexts.

8EE5E0AE0DB14DA18E130ADB23AEFB08.description: Recognizing congruence, similarity, symmetry, measurement opportunities, and other geometric ideas, including right triangle trigonometry, in real-world contexts provides a means of building understanding of these concepts and is a powerful tool for solving problems related to the physical world in which we live.

C0E9BCE061044FEDA5C06E98453EC1CC.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems.

55600AC720CD456CBDE52FEE8E0E52F9.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

D0A878EE441D44D3A112C200E07C22A8.description: Proofs of theorems can sometimes be made with transformations, coordinates, or algebra; all approaches can be useful, and in some cases one may provide a more accessible or understandable argument than another.

D9871BDDE8924E9DB77A6BC5DE7B2556.description: Investigate, prove, and apply theorems about parallelograms and other quadrilaterals, including but not limited to both necessary and sufficient conditions for parallelograms and other quadrilaterals, as well as relationships among kinds of quadrilaterals.

30C2CAC4210D42B6B7278760A839D8E9.description: Investigate, prove, and apply theorems about triangles, including but not limited to: the sum of the measures of the interior angles of a triangle is 180˚; the base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem using triangle similarity.

410B9A63827E4CF6A2E5CC7456EEF668.description: Investigate, prove, and apply theorems about lines and angles, including but not limited to: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; the points on the perpendicular bisector of a line segment are those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.

08814FF2AADD4F8E8E0C6A727AC36730.description: Justify whether conjectures are true or false in order to prove theorems and then apply those theorems in solving problems, communicating proofs in a variety of ways, including flow chart, two-column, and paragraph formats.

4745236B832B4B2CAAE82DD1DE1D0705.description: Develop and use precise definitions of figures such as angle, circle, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

496450B7A03043DEA0D8E97AADFECC74.description: Proof is the means by which we demonstrate whether a statement is true or false mathematically, and proofs can be communicated in a variety of ways (e.g., two-column, paragraph).

765D7B88BA974C20806BD8DC9CF204E4.description: Identify different sets of properties necessary to define and construct figures.

F9D5EF1F602F47ECA49EBB2814FA4A6F.description: Construct figures, using technology and other tools, in order to make and test conjectures about their properties.

8ABCC1EF7B3C4B6087BD5E1543119B89.description: Find patterns and relationships in figures including lines, triangles, quadrilaterals, and circles, using technology and other tools.

972A967BE40B4BF68A987715B7566602.description: Using technology to construct and explore figures with constraints provides an opportunity to explore the independence and dependence of assumptions and conjectures.

2096491ACA9A4E46AF4ECA8E56BCB1E5.description: Verify that two triangles are similar if (but not only if) two pairs of corresponding angles are congruent (AA), the corresponding sides are proportional (SSS), or two pairs of corresponding sides are proportional and the pair of included angles is congruent (SAS).

AABC67A6DBF14BABB8D671BEFE3813C9.description: Verify that two triangles are similar if and only if corresponding pairs of sides are proportional and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

1BC900A2BDA64B58B0BF2A7270015741.description: Verify criteria for showing triangles are similar using a similarity transformation (sequence of rigid motions and dilations) that maps one triangle to another.

EE3463AEC4A544C4A395C459B9FC5BA4.description: Given two figures, determine whether they are similar by identifying a similarity transformation (sequence of rigid motions and dilations) that maps one figure to the other.

24CCB8F5E96C42CB9421E321805E80A6.description: Verify that the dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

85E7866EB28A4E069F0D364800730816.description: Verify that a dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

7BBCD9831BC44E5185BA525CA5D4769C.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor.

37004592330B4734963BAB2A13616758.description: Showing that two figures are similar involves finding a similarity transformation (dilation or composite of a dilation with a rigid motion) or, equivalently, a sequence of similarity transformations that maps one figure onto the other.

075C6C0DEB8C483799D5B28013FEEC9B.description: Verify that two triangles are congruent if (but not only if) the following groups of corresponding parts are congruent: angle-side-angle (ASA), side-angle-side (SAS), side-side-side (SSS), and angle-angle-side (AAS).

DBCDE29D85414238A548D95817449895.description: Verify that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

136D707E40FC4737AE8FBACDC3FFA111.description: Verify criteria for showing triangles are congruent using a sequence of rigid motions that map one triangle to another.

C20077F6FD754ACB9EC2112DD0A7A436.description: Define congruence of two figures in terms of rigid motions (a sequence of translations, rotations, and reflections); show that two figures are congruent by finding a sequence of rigid motions that maps one figure to the other.

27C8281DB715497AB483088B3ACE5B5E.description: Showing that two figures are congruent involves showing that there is a rigid motion (translation, rotation, reflection, or glide reflection) or, equivalently, a sequence of rigid motions that maps one figure to the other.

478C53BD95904300A4283296E5866AD2.description: Develop definitions of rotation, reflection, and translation in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

055C24647DD648039B89331C0D909FEF.description: Draw figures with different types of symmetries and describe their attributes.

6A15DC1DFE5246DB8DE4F60803C5D6B5.description: Specify a sequence of rotations, reflections, or translations that will carry a given figure onto another.

2B55FA5F773D46D0913402CE9704CA1B.description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the image of the transformed figure using graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software.

8B5607FF1DE8440CBB3A1365AB2EAA4C.description: Explore rotations, reflections, and translations using graph paper, tracing paper, and geometry software.

59A7AC178CD44DBB84F258B2F90A4A10.description: Compare transformations which preserve distance and angle measure to those that do not.

E207E31598DD4948B39C4AFEDC6D0813.description: Describe transformations and compositions of transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs, using informal and formal notation.

A86708DDA501438084801DE214BA8B51.description: Represent transformations and compositions of transformations in the plane (coordinate and otherwise) using tools such as tracing paper and geometry software.

419CFDC4DE89493F9A6FD314D0B6EE1F.description: Applying geometric transformations to figures provides opportunities for describing the attributes of the figures preserved by the transformation and for describing symmetries by examining when a figure can be mapped onto itself.

1ECF20B221634FBBBA7737F3513A9B89.description: Derive and apply the formula for the length of an arc and the formula for the area of a sector.

6A54EE233AD147C89D6453B05DFA1167.description: Derive and apply the relationships between the lengths, perimeters, areas, and volumes of similar figures in relation to their scale factor.

3EF73D80935D4F649CDC6AF447EC2CD8.description: When an object is the image of a known object under a similarity transformation, a length, area, or volume on the image can be computed by using proportional relationships.

CCFC5EB232DB4030BF0AFFE37E80EFD5.description: Given the coordinates of the vertices of a polygon, compute its perimeter and area using a variety of methods, including the distance formula and dynamic geometry software, and evaluate the accuracy of the results.

A21EFED807D748DB84CAFB6A84A3D3A8.description: Constructing approximations of measurements with different tools, including technology, can support an understanding of measurement.

82696E9EAF07483E84570793FEFC086E.description: Apply geometric concepts to find missing dimensions to solve surface area or volume problems.

CF86040D778F4D8DA1E1911BF86469BF.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the surface area and volume of a sphere, cylinder, pyramid, and cone using dissection arguments, Cavalieri's Principle, and informal limit arguments.

ADC475D142E34E9FA13BDBD9CBE0F3C5.description: Model and solve problems using surface area and volume of solids, including composite solids and solids with portions removed.

E30023DD2201401AA0B3DA1B88A9643C.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

52DA08F4B0A149409FDA9EC606480DAD.description: Areas and volumes of figures can be computed by determining how the figure might be obtained from simpler figures by dissection and recombination.

BBBEF214C195435FB9C428990B3E25D1.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the given data.

D5C8E4B781434CA98919061CAB03FD11.description: Use the linear model to solve problems in the context of the given data.

11CD302C08E54B85BF9B26050A5074E8.description: Evaluate possible solutions to real-life problems by developing linear models of contextual situations and using them to predict unknown values.

7AF3DC31A0534F429592D8BDDE59209A.description: Data analysis techniques can be used to develop models of contextual situations and to generate and evaluate possible solutions to real problems involving those contexts.

65C19228E7784E238DDE532CA60E8610.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear relationship.

BA742F39C1C24C9F8E3FA32402C4E838.description: Analyzing the association between two quantitative variables should involve statistical procedures, such as examining (with technology) the sum of squared deviations in fitting a linear model, analyzing residuals for patterns, generating a least-squares regression line and finding a correlation coefficient, and differentiating between correlation and causation.

7B18A35F1FD041A1AA879207F74AA0C4.description: Use technology to find the least-squares line of best fit for two quantitative variables.

7A864D31DD6E4A70B8B9B44E173646CA.description: Find a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association and informally assess its fit by plotting and analyzing residuals, including the squares of the residuals, in order to improve its fit.

DEF59F95ABA7461994B1372672F8D84E.description: Represent data of two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

ADCE31C5C7004648A565F3C489A36426.description: Scatter plots, including plots over time, can reveal patterns, trends, clusters, and gaps that are useful in analyzing the association between two contextual variables.

9C32733DB6124EBFA0DE3D43A5E70B92.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers) on mean and standard deviation.

E3F97BC88949437BB9893E143F215ECC.description: Calculate the standard deviation for a data set, using technology where appropriate.

82E10C17FF324F3789EF0C4CA8594EC1.description: Explain how standard deviation develops from mean absolute deviation.

F5C0945D5DDD49818DA2F66AAF3C69EE.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare and contrast two or more data sets, utilizing the mean and median for center and the interquartile range and standard deviation for variability.

0F9AB7E7A577465EB20BB739C1680874.description: Represent the distribution of univariate quantitative data with plots on the real number line, choosing a format (dot plot, histogram, or box plot) most appropriate to the data set, and represent the distribution of bivariate quantitative data with a scatter plot. Extend from simple cases by hand to more complex cases involving large data sets using technology.

362155E6E5D04907BE8B026E2C03514D.description: Distributions of quantitative data (continuous or discrete) in one variable should be described in the context of the data with respect to what is typical (the shape, with appropriate measures of center and variability, including standard deviation) and what is not (outliers), and these characteristics can be used to compare two or more subgroups with respect to a variable.

3644D2AE5A044D5BA13B00EF06A14CFD.description: Use technology to organize data, including very large data sets, into a useful and manageable structure.

427C41D0ACF64A69BF9F7FC84B00245B.description: Data arise from a context and come in two types: quantitative (continuous or discrete) and categorical. Technology can be used to "clean" and organize data, including very large data sets, into a useful and manageable structure – a first step in any analysis of data

90FC4C7468B64880821C7A5BA507902E.description: Use mathematical and statistical reasoning with quantitative data, both univariate data (set of values) and bivariate data (set of pairs of values) that suggest a linear association, in order to draw conclusions and assess risk.

49C72D980DA241E1A1483FB0F3DDEE88.description: Mathematical and statistical reasoning about data can be used to evaluate conclusions and assess risks.

6BA40D15976549D6910AEB8FCC6D9D46.description: Derive the distance formula from the Pythagorean Theorem.

49F2585AF98346E5A5079558F96E03D6.description: Given the endpoints of the diameter of a circle, use the midpoint formula to find its center and then use the Pythagorean Theorem to find its equation.

B91CA8DE80C54292AA34B0A20831872F.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem.

9536D5A2BAA641A5A15F90ED9BAA1D19.description: Verify that the graph of a linear equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, which forms a line.

EAB0B0807ED74870BEF244BB44144B41.description: Graphs can be used to obtain exact or approximate solutions of equations, inequalities, and systems of equations and inequalities—including systems of linear equations in two variables and systems of linear and quadratic equations (given or obtained by using technology).

CA72025413FB488A8371CFB02D6B788F.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

CB003A5DE2EA4F8789A9F1392DE482BF.description: Expressions, equations, and inequalities can be used to analyze and make predictions, both within mathematics and as mathematics is applied in different contexts – in particular, contexts that arise in relation to linear, quadratic, and exponential situations.

E8970DE3CEDD44A29964363FFE42652D.description: Find the coordinates of the vertices of a polygon determined by a set of lines, given their equations, by setting their function rules equal and solving, or by using their graphs.

8164C9B067A440B0B395D35661CC65F1.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

50C2404C8D894110BA7486379B109B99.description: Choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

971AFBF2F5344BBF8307689526CEF530.description: Choose and interpret units consistently in formulas.

A97DBEB9BEA94927B5781403FF74E47D.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems.

EB84B13E7F9843D4AEC41958341C4849.description: Quantitative reasoning includes and mathematical modeling requires attention to units of measurement.

AF8FBF25E6DE4A4AAF16871E05D0A6C7.description: Extend understanding of irrational and rational numbers by rewriting expressions involving radicals, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, in order to recognize geometric patterns.

C40968B80A3C4039881EFD3A1BA8E5C9.description: Together, irrational numbers and rational numbers complete the real number system, representing all points on the number line, while there exist numbers beyond the real numbers called complex numbers.

16CD29C5297C4341A6B8EC95FB3BE47F.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

7872893540704578B7BC4F508F8511CE.description: Look for and make use of structure.

C0F0BD1B9F274C6EB2B946F9E83E9C4C.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

767B0ED7CC8E400BA7A76798A0C4B3DA.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

847D32A3FDB943C38F600C51CA7CEF72.description: Explain whether two events, A and B, are independent, using two-way tables or tree diagrams.

41F55A26E9BD408F88413941760CF513.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

B9B549A8DAD743E2B9ED5F7101767843.description: Two events are independent if the occurrence of one event does not affect the probability of the other event. Determining whether two events are independent can be used for finding and understanding probabilities.

3E4FE9F412ED4CCCA3F5BF925E128294.description: Design and carry out an investigation to determine whether there appears to be an association between two categorical variables, and write a persuasive argument based on the results of the investigation.

F66007AA9491457D90B4CDDBBE3B5427.description: Making and defending informed, data-based decisions is a characteristic of a quantitatively literate person.

88474C4EB4F440ACBEBB02604AB76A44.description: Use mathematical and statistical reasoning with bivariate categorical data in order to draw conclusions and assess risk.

F9EF9275869748D8A1C0A0DAF9E32392.description: Mathematical and statistical reasoning about data can be used to evaluate conclusions and assess risks.

D2C530A2FC6144DE87DE1FEF868168BF.description: Recognize and explore situations where the association between two categorical variables is reversed when a third variable is considered (Simpson's Paradox).

61E3C7BE89904C45BC1017AF99366293.description: Aggregate data from several groups to find an overall association between two categorical variables.

63DC8F5DED5D49D89C125990A8FF0647.description: Generate a two-way categorical table in order to find and evaluate solutions to real-world problems.

22D9B3AB95024A0D9636842F514F939F.description: Data analysis techniques can be used to develop models of contextual situations and to generate and evaluate possible solutions to real problems involving those contexts.

A1408F4B75C8481AA8B9FA42572DFB04.description: Identify possible associations and trends in categorical data.

1D3554AD86B943658EAD2691A74956D0.description: Interpret relative frequencies in the context of categorical data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies).

D565645A683045CC8C9F4C98EA0DC19B.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables and represent using segmented bar graphs.

B90632BEC46641DD9F8F020B9FCF8542.description: Analyze the possible association between two categorical variables.

EDE99927E79641DB905A56CF9E0DA92B.description: The association between two categorical variables is typically represented by using two-way tables and segmented bar graphs.

6D4814ACF7394C79AD23F97CD5872E3E.description: Distinguish between quantitative and categorical data and between the techniques that may be used for analyzing data of these two types.

FD6F01D5314C4887B56B43F8C008C19D.description: Data arise from a context and come in two types: quantitative (continuous or discrete) and categorical. Technology can be used to "clean" and organize data, including very large data sets, into a useful and manageable structure – a first step in any analysis of data.

4B2542B507074DE19DF981624BE6B454.description: Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects, using relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible associations between the two variables.

4564CAC895AB4D63BEB714DA4541FA8A.description: Describe the rate of change and y-intercept in the context of a problem using a linear model of a real-world situation.

9C9ECDA344214A2282976DE9639A77EE.description: Use a linear model of a real-world situation to solve problems and make predictions.

FA71DE101B0F48678D6682CA89E86622.description: Given a scatter plot that suggests a linear association, informally draw a line to fit the data, and assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

433F21FCAE1F43588AA779C14C180531.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities, describing patterns in terms of positive, negative, or no association, linear and non-linear association, clustering, and outliers.

052E4812E29D4F6B9C21B3BD742B485E.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

6592D5F4C1A4448789DE041D6B16D48D.description: Use the mathematical modeling cycle to solve real-world problems involving linear, quadratic, exponential, absolute value, and linear piecewise functions.

BD819401A8C449B4A51506CCCA5BC3E7.description: Functions model a wide variety of real situations and can help students understand the processes of making and changing assumptions, assigning variables, and finding solutions to contextual problems.

7622C514FB3A475D936F167F73A9DBF4.description: Graph exponential functions, showing intercepts and end behavior.

F8BB94EF8E4348AEBDE3B000F09E39EB.description: Graph piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

02745BAD63D64950A52EA3D8A26545A2.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

6D2B4F0EF9C64FCCB25F71ED82AF7CE3.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

3D657530EDE14132A9D5DEE8FB1A1A93.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph. Limit to linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value functions.

63F1FAA8392D46BCAF4E886F63E9AD4B.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Extend from relationships that can be represented by linear functions to quadratic, exponential, absolute value, and general piecewise functions.

4965FB2982984BC39384470C66E2A84A.description: Functions can be represented graphically and key features of the graphs, including zeros, intercepts, and, when relevant, rate of change and maximum/minimum values, can be associated with and interpreted in terms of the equivalent symbolic representation.

417AB6A9CE024C6EAD2AF21E0AAA8058.description: Interpret the parameters of functions in terms of a context. Extend from linear functions, written in the form mx + b, to exponential functions, written in the form abx.

CF6BFA2EA98D492F93554395412A0F26.description: Use graphs and tables to show that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly or quadratically.

A2F7DCF2C72B4D0CB1E763C422604A1E.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

621ACE1238944AEF9A74B1E5513C21EB.description: Define exponential functions to represent situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

F0504D6EEB6143168D4FAD68E0C984B4.description: Define linear functions to represent situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

0AD334A3A97B4E339926ACD84127FA07.description: Show that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, while exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

98F201EB4DDB4906AFC4424F3DF3FC8B.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and those that can be modeled with exponential functions.

C21D0A9CDAF5492A86E428694D14DF77.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k·f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and explain the effects on the graph, using technology as appropriate. Extend from linear to quadratic, exponential, absolute value, and linear piecewise functions.

A82B389461A14F2A9E319D987BB1F13F.description: Functions that are members of the same family have distinguishing attributes (structure) common to all functions within that family.

5418727BAB9A4FD986C8BFE8B5D2B3D3.description: Write explicit and recursive formulas for arithmetic and geometric sequences and connect them to linear and exponential functions.

3F225448A3DD42D986EB053634C0718F.description: Define sequences as functions, including recursive definitions, whose domain is a subset of the integers.

FFBB9D59835C457FAEF55519D16F43E6.description: Distinguish between linear and non-linear functions.

AE7656FD39DB45E2B6C3AB6343B02B91.description: Compare properties of two functions, each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Include linear, quadratic, exponential, absolute value, and linear piecewise.

70D9FCC24AE74177AC4FB96E7605411F.description: Functions can be described by using a variety of representations: mapping diagrams, function notation (e.g., f(x) = x²), recursive definitions, tables, and graphs.

5EAB521E70A44BE88AF3170C3528A3D3.description: Solve systems consisting of linear and/or quadratic equations in two variables graphically, using technology where appropriate.

49D6C2FC06F5449DAD860FEA28126C47.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes, using technology where appropriate.

CB079330D41D493AB9E2E5BC80AFB1AE.description: Find the approximate solutions of an equation graphically, using tables of values, or finding successive approximations, using technology where appropriate.

0CFEA445090640498FC4FD68DA8DD4A4.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x).

BBFD927C31DB439AAE1F54BBF496B79D.description: Graphs can be used to obtain exact or approximate solutions of equations, inequalities, and systems of equations and inequalities – including systems of linear equations in two variables and systems of linear and quadratic equations (given or obtained by using technology).

AC1DDD0AD7A748338A01E6478689FA37.description: Use function composition to combine different types of standard functions to write and evaluate functions.

A42AFC96E7284E079305DD36D1168CA8.description: Use arithmetic operations to combine different types of standard functions to write and evaluate functions.

FE1E9B93C92E403998D5C47497B2370E.description: Combine different types of standard functions to write, evaluate, and interpret functions in context. Limit to linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value functions.

6B8B0751F14049F4BD598E7D31BDD36B.description: Compare and contrast relations and functions represented by equations, graphs, or tables that show related values; determine whether a relation is a function. Identify that a function f is a special kind of relation defined by the equation y = f(x).

6818651D287740E59AB994D2D777D5D6.description: Given a relation defined by an equation in two variables, identify the graph of the relation as the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane.

D91488EE93E245B6B5FCDC0B73CC6350.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. Limit to linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value functions.

D68BD2B1ADBF4F3BAC9C967C3247D494.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

261D43DAE0C64D2B97512D646036FA6D.description: Define a function as a mapping from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) that assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range.

0A990EB5020B4F04938C6A08C527CCE7.description: Functions shift the emphasis from a point-by-point relationship between two variables (input/output) to considering an entire set of ordered pairs (where each first element is paired with exactly one second element) as an entity with its own features and characteristics.

18C56C48DBD540AD998EEF33DD3D2E28.description: Represent constraints by equations and/or inequalities, and solve systems of equations and/or inequalities, interpreting solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context. Limit to contexts arising from linear, quadratic, exponential, absolute value, and linear piecewise functions.

7F4230082E6F44C4B4AEB4CF9924DDBC.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities in context; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales and use them to make predictions. Limit to contexts arising from linear, quadratic, exponential, absolute value, and linear piecewise functions.

FEE971A97A5C434CB771F3BB8EFC46D1.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems in context, either exactly or approximately. Extend from contexts arising from linear functions to those involving quadratic, exponential, and absolute value functions.

EBDAC2A195964A09A5D88602B1C30D20.description: Expressions, equations, and inequalities can be used to analyze and make predictions, both within mathematics and as mathematics is applied in different contexts – in particular, contexts that arise in relation to linear, quadratic, and exponential situations.

EE76ACB8471143E99C525806C631D256.description: Contrast solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables produced by algebraic methods with graphical and tabular methods.

A0280B47E344439FBC0FF8BAE082974C.description: Solve a system of two equations in two variables by using linear combinations; contrast situations in which use of linear combinations is more efficient with those in which substitution is more efficient.

4797DA82FD2C4A1184C368DC7A05F4AC.description: Select an appropriate method to solve a system of two linear equations in two variables.

83810E768EAA4311BEFC1A8C70269B32.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (such as x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula, and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation, and recognize that some solutions may not be real.

5AC9F2AE0DC540D88667422278D258BF.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Explain how the quadratic formula is derived from this form.

32D1D4CC25DB49638D45B22D98A58A71.description: Select an appropriate method to solve a quadratic equation in one variable.

129C1B80C05144C99942163323FB1C44.description: The structure of an equation or inequality (including, but not limited to, one-variable linear and quadratic equations, inequalities, and systems of linear equations in two variables) can be purposefully analyzed (with and without technology) to determine an efficient strategy to find a solution, if one exists, and then to justify the solution.

4E62B0EC1C4D4740AF41D15D6FFFC762.description: Explain why extraneous solutions to an equation involving absolute values may arise and how to check to be sure that a candidate solution satisfies an equation.

5F64B7CAB481469791CCF07CAC1D4C3F.description: Finding solutions to an equation, inequality, or system of equations or inequalities requires the checking of candidate solutions, whether generated analytically or graphically, to ensure that solutions are found and that those found are not extraneous.

8256FC45389641C0B036923166406CC7.description: Interpret and justify the results of systems of two linear equations in two variables (one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions) when applied to real-world and mathematical problems.

EA79920A3E3E4B8A9AE00542C1DF03D4.description: Explain that the solution(s) of systems of two linear equations in two variables corresponds to points of intersection on their graphs because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

BAE4A0CF8BF04F62ACE2ED53B0F7AD93.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables by graphing and substitution.

B46DDA4C7A744C55AB33F927ADEDD44D.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and systems of two linear equations.

D2686018C6634BB6AF699CA9CCD5FF7A.description: Analyze the relationship (increasing or decreasing, linear or non-linear) between two quantities represented in a graph.

D8C6DB215F4945E299CA3978CDDA3E02.description: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials, showing that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication.

BE2B2E2BC6674006BBE4F320B5878281.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

AF2C3683A6A24C0FA93D3DF4D8C43FF9.description: Use the vertex form of a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value and the axis of symmetry of the function it defines; complete the square to find the vertex form of quadratics with a leading coefficient of one.

23BFFE189DDB4F08B0ED2BC576586565.description: Factor quadratic expressions with leading coefficients of one, and use the factored form to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

A845227D2B39457DA030D57FE110CD72.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

1C26130AE95646239DFC6922D3792F26.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

6E4A271132BA4F239A12D3D5C9BA6B5D.description: Interpret linear, quadratic, and exponential expressions in terms of a context by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

B237E461EBFD41CBB3386EDB3309C56A.description: Expressions can be rewritten in equivalent forms by using algebraic properties, including properties of addition, multiplication, and exponentiation, to make different characteristics or features visible.

F524968AAED34C159006747AAE1FE2D1.description: Define the imaginary number i such that i² = -1.

98181F90F7C94820A1CA913F7317CF59.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

EFEBEAA54C2A4D5FBD2ED3E2EAF2BE46.description: Explain how the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for an additional notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.

47CFFDF2B83F4A37B019E779DBE226A2.description: Together, irrational numbers and rational numbers complete the real number system, representing all points on the number line, while there exist numbers beyond the real numbers called complex numbers.

68ABB536918647B3A18326FEA500BF6A.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

81D3232A3273464999ED7272825FF481.description: Look for and make use of structure.

90136563D58A4638B4A2938444E732EC.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

B5AEDF5B1F504238A1921F1F85611EA9.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Alabama Course of Study: English Language Arts

336F047D5C7C49858A64423689A1E46B.description: Select and utilize effective words and phrases that are suitable for purpose and audience to communicate clearly in a variety of situations.

FD0474D9A87D482FA037D13F939D7451.description: Apply vocabulary in writing to convey and enhance meaning.

9BE2BD09AD6244DCA4BFDA06BE75EAB9.description: Infer word meaning through active listening in various contexts for purposeful, effective communication.

84D06B9CFD9E4D58A08E9FB1C3A9587D.description: Read and evaluate texts from science, social studies, and other academic disciplines to determine how those disciplines treat domain-specific vocabulary and content organization.

9AD8D4A2B6F948C9BEA0FEE4CF9B7B3E.description: Determine word meaning through the use of word parts, context clues, connotation and denotation, or print or digital reference tools.

555C7AB29ADB40DCA68008FF2AEB65C6.description: Increase academic, domain-specific, and grade-level-appropriate vocabularies through reading, word study, and class discussion.

3608DE848CB54400B0903B2FEEA92333.description: Collect information through the research process to answer follow-up questions and participate in discussions about their research findings.

28DE96616CEC4677B359FFB40C5590C7.description: Incorporate research into oral presentations, summarizing and supporting opinions and ideas with relevant details.

F5859E4C68914056AF2B1140339B8AF7.description: Quote, paraphrase, summarize, and present findings, following an appropriate citation style and avoiding plagiarism.

611235D4528C4879B9C5375A71BE73A5.description: Produce research writings over extended periods with time for research, reflection, and revision and within shorter time frames, with minimal guidance.

2F43F2D2B61B47FFBA765E92D7AAB00F.description: Use active listening to acquire information and assess its relevance and credibility.

BCCD2EA82E9E4343B18EB1F28276CABF.description: Determine the relevance, reliability, and validity of information from nonfiction and fictional printed and/or digital texts.

A91E26A01DC649CDB012A26E2497A890.description: Implement ethical guidelines while finding and recording information from a variety of primary, secondary, and digital sources.

FF63A4F9D0C149D68E6B7A64D7D520B8.description:
Engage in inquiry through the research process to locate, acquire, refine, and present relevant and credible findings in multiple
modes.

C33184B7CD9C4CCC8D39F433D1997F30.description: Choose language that expresses ideas precisely and concisely.

5182D3D1885041219F8CD926478030B7.description: Embed phrases and clauses within a sentence, recognizing and correcting misplaced or dangling modifiers.

0A9FB6EF35B7484BB1EEF4547ED9E563.description: Construct simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to represent relationships among ideas.

90FDC2D7679E41B08970E791DB1CDB21.description: Revise their own writing using correct mechanics with a focus on commas, apostrophes, quotation marks, colons, and semicolons.

FC4AF308B00A4559AE89B3DA128040D4.description: Create written work using standard English grammar, usage, and mechanics.

F4E9CD91F7C64ED299ECEE52CA69E102.description: Identify a speaker's formality of language in order to comprehend, interpret, and respond appropriately.

E6C4ECDF6F504662ABD5E32ED872C3B1.description: Evaluate a speaker's organizational choices to determine point of view, purpose, and effectiveness.

46C50567245D41469D229AA46803FEEC.description: Correct improper usage of commas, apostrophes, quotation marks, colons, and semicolons through peer editing.

88675FB3BF7044AC9ACFE58D42D08399.description: Identify the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling in a variety of texts.

634ADFFBB9FC466B9BE988031B374F05.description: Evaluate the functions of phrases and clauses in general and their function in specific sentences.

AE69FBBB99F24A408FD0B54F36A4B36C.description: Identify the usage of simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex statements and questions to signal differing relationships among ideas in a text.

376BF879FCB541F7A42E36A9908950FC.description: Identify subject-verb agreement with compound subjects joined by correlative and coordinating conjunctions and with collective nouns when verb form depends on the rest of the sentence.

D0F61226426C4F2DA8772F4F4484B04B.description: Identify the conventions of standard English grammar and usage in writing.

5778F73A352943D7B9C59C9ECAAF864D.description:
Recognize and demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar, mechanics, and usage, including appropriate
formality of language.

C05B003C3947434D9D89BB4A219F16AB.description: Convey ideas in an appropriate digital format with specific attention to subject, occasion, audience, purpose, and tone.

B4ECDC0C8D47434CB4EDFB01A8BF4E80.description: Utilize digital tools and/or products to enhance meaning.

66A1E1F5C51C4996B68EBD3CD7275EE3.description: Create and edit digital products that are appropriate in subject, occasion, audience, purpose, and tone.

77DCDBA55ED4423EA09D44076CF4D520.description: Interpret language through active listening to determine subject, occasion, audience, purpose, tone, and credibility of digital sources.

83215ABD9C92420CAA0F617A360563F7.description: Determine the intended purposes of techniques used for rhetorical effect in multiple digital sources.

280A9A2E1FDB4F17AE928AE4A3DFBEE4.description: Compare and contrast the effectiveness of techniques used in a variety of digital sources to generate and answer literal, interpretive, and applied questions and create new understandings.

D4C816E62C7D4445B190EE1F87F4E8F3.description: Assess subject, occasion, audience, purpose, tone, and credibility of various digital sources.

0584327F9E17414FBC4CA71C128629A1.description:
Use technology, including the Internet, to research, analyze, produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products,
taking advantage of technology’s capacity to link to other information, people, and resources and to display information flexibly and
dynamically.

17ADECE884844B0D9CEB1C16B9C86750.description: Participate in collaborative discussions about prose and poetry by evaluating the use of literary devices and elements.

6C6F0C3E2E7D488492331223D72E3095.description: Participate in collaborative discussions about arguments by evaluating claims, findings, and evidence from a source.

90AC9A9ABFED4693BE57894F81D282FF.description: Write an argument to defend a position by introducing and supporting claim(s), acknowledging alternate or opposing claims, and presenting reasons and relevant text evidence from accurate and credible sources.

2130A0EE3D0B4BBEB41BDC1C4F193484.description: Write informative or explanatory texts with an organized structure and a formal style to examine ideas or processes effectively while developing the topic and utilizing appropriate transitions, precise vocabulary, and credible information or data when relevant.

C27014F09E8F44EDBAB8BAE721B0A6F5.description: Write narratives to convey a series of events incorporating key literary elements, establishing a clear purpose, using narrative techniques (dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection), and sequencing events coherently (chronological and/or flashback).

C740C213B35F44EE928F915B7037DD16.description: Produce clear, coherent narrative, argument, and informative/explanatory writing in which the development, organization, style, and tone are relevant to task, purpose, and audience, using an appropriate command of language.

DFADBE2CB80A445AB72EB1C1195A3506.description: Evaluate the speaker's use of hyperbole, tone, symbolism, imagery, mood, irony, and onomatopoeia in a live or recorded presentation.

21B92B9B9AA741CA9135DEC3564BA9F1.description: Evaluate rhetorical strategies used to develop central and supporting ideas in recorded or live presentations, including point of view, purpose, comparison, categories, and word meanings (figurative, connotative, and technical).

4B9A499C7326437C8C8935746D4B6547.description: Evaluate literary devices to support interpretations of literary texts using textual evidence, including simile, metaphor, personification, onomatopoeia, hyperbole, imagery, tone, symbolism, irony, and mood.

2942AA05A6DA442FA07E2A0523049D0C.description: Explain how the author's choice of setting, plot, characters, theme, conflict, dialogue, and point of view contribute to and/or enhance the meaning and purpose of prose and poetry, using textual evidence from the writing.

AFD5D3C9E1D54818AE0FC1EA8C7E100D.description: Evaluate how effectively an author uses structures of informational texts, including comparison and contrast, problem and solution, cause and effect, and substantiated or unsubstantiated claims and evidence, to achieve a purpose.

23619024679F4332B4DF255FE6211704.description: Evaluate the contributions of informational text elements, including categories, point of view, purpose, and figurative, connotative, and technical word meanings, to develop central and supporting ideas.

85B2F1CA20644DEAB399C20AE813A0E5.description: Process and employ information for a variety of academic, occupational, and personal purposes.

52F689B2A6B248CB969688C2FDE2B68B.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4FB88DE8E122464991172D85809C2C16.description: Assess the formality of occasions in order to speak or write using appropriate language and tone.

92C674AAA9FC4DE9926AAC94A1A9AE5E.description: Utilize a writing process to plan, draft, revise, edit, and publish writings in various genres.

CC59544317634934A3D8C15D656AB6C5.description: Use digital and electronic tools appropriately, safely, and ethically when researching and writing, both individually and collaboratively.

4BE3ECD7FBC24D8BB178E976F0546B1F.description: Use context clues to determine meanings of unfamiliar spoken or written words.

58D2363CDB704023BA8D0C9A1AE3BA55.description: Utilize active listening skills during discussion and conversation in pairs, small groups, or whole-class settings, following agreed-upon rules for participation.

document.title: 2023 Alabama Course of Study: Science

D15075891D2643D884D062310891A542.description:
Evaluate multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the
shape of Earth’s surface.

B17228263B7C4E8B85A1F36CD4D0230D.description:
Use a variety of sources to provide evidence that Earth’s events can occur slowly or rapidly.
Examples: erosion, melting of glaciers; earthquakes, volcanic eruptions

E21277EA0ED04610B0B14933D08F5403.description:
Obtain information to identify where water is found on Earth and determine whether it is a solid
or a liquid.

053FD1EBB0974FD8884233890A923F3A.description: Use models to distinguish between the shapes and kinds of land and water on Earth.

29B01407263C48F8920D4D44B38D349A.description:

90F8735E84AE446EABABD0A61441C44E.description: Stability and Change: Some things stay the same while other things change. Things may change slowly or rapidly.

1BA45BD8D9854AA7A50AA24C1A6354BD.description: Structure and Function: The shape and stability of structures of natural and designed objects are related to their function(s).

EA1717D576D448F9936C44826B837799.description:
Energy and Matter:
Flows, Cycles,
and Conservation: Objects may break into smaller pieces, be put together into larger pieces, or change shapes.

382B03CF5E1843D19CD15FA759A43C35.description:
Systems and System Models: Objects and organisms can be described in terms of their parts. Systems in the natural and designed world have parts
that work together.

DFA62C7410CB4CBDBF982297E2FC8581.description:
Cause and Effect:
Mechanism and Prediction: Events have causes that generate observable patterns. Simple tests can be designed to gather evidence to support or
refute students’ ideas about causes.

71094A7BC5A9431CB17122DAC838B564.description:
Patterns: Patterns in the natural and human-designed world can be observed, used to describe phenomena, and used as
evidence.

86BBC60A6D2847118E1572D64423431A.description:
Obtaining, Evaluating,
and Communicating
Information: Using observations and texts to gather and communicate new information

A1A34337F21F40AD9A0CF9CCA8EF8461.description:
Engaging in Argument
from Evidence: Comparing ideas and representations about the natural and designed world(s).

1CBCA85F05EE405BACAACB81DC4DB1B9.description:

and Designing Solutions: Using evidence and ideas in constructing evidence-based accounts of natural phenomena and designing solutions.

26B4F5B566B541A4AD06E5F611C6F3DE.description:

Computational Thinking: Recognizing ways that mathematics can be used to describe the natural and designed world(s).

3EB4DFFDDDBD45B2B12C97816E299CED.description:

Interpreting Data: Collecting, recording, and sharing observations.

97C3FAF4A3E84CB2ADC6FE61BCC1C40D.description:
Planning and Carrying
Out Investigations: Designing and conducting simple investigations, based on fair tests, which provide data to support explanations or
design solutions.

AEB983EBE837492D89CB64582E85721F.description:
Developing and Using
Models: Using and developing models that represent concrete events or design solutions, including diagrams, drawings,
physical replicas, dioramas, dramatizations, or storyboards.

33C844DAC49843EF9ADA14AE828CEF2E.description:
Asking Questions
and Defining Problems: s Formulating simple descriptive questions that can be tested.

document.title: 2023 Alabama Course of Study: Science

AAD6FAC52DDD44FCA04B5B7DA9BB9CD3.description:
Stability and Change: Change is measured in terms of differences over time and may occur at different rates. Some systems appear stable,
but over long periods of time will eventually change.

DC2B6086E222495DA3E20DA97C9AD71B.description:
Structure
and Function: Different materials have different substructures, which can sometimes be observed. Substructures have shapes and
parts that serve functions.

F00F94C7D6574E00A636DE7E6ED1EC50.description:
Energy and Matter:
Flows, Cycles,
and Conservation: Matter is made of particles. Matter flows and cycles can be tracked in terms of the weight of the substances before
and after a process occurs. The total weight of the substances does not change. This is what is meant by conservation
of matter. Matter is transported into, out of, and within systems. Energy can be transferred in various ways; energy
can be transferred between objects.

4D927658F51E4D39AE2EFF7714D0F6CA.description:
Systems
and System Models: A system is a group of related parts that make up a whole and can carry out functions its individual parts cannot. A
system can be described in terms of its components and their interactions.

5D3A6B4CB816421FB6CCB39AF57283BA.description:
Scale, Proportion, and
Quantity: Natural objects and/or observable phenomena exist from the very small to the immensely large or from very short to
very long time periods. Standard units are used to measure and describe physical quantities such as weight, time,
temperature, and volume.

ACCDF5C0270B49248BC8BCFE3C7A2D58.description:
Cause and Effect:
Mechanism and
Prediction: Cause and effect relationships are routinely identified, tested, and used to explain change. Events that occur together
with regularity might or might not be a cause and effect relationship.

7EBE1D7BF21B478DB245207FAFA27CAE.description:
Patterns: Similarities and differences in patterns can be used to sort, classify, communicate, and analyze simple rates of change
for natural phenomena and designed products. Patterns of change can be used to make predictions. Patterns can be
used as evidence to support an explanation

B0E56671C95D43C897D094B41A48D5A1.description:
Obtaining, Evaluating,
and Communicating
Information: Evaluating the merit and accuracy of ideas and methods.

07A37F223399436A979F185A6026C51D.description:
Engaging in Argument
from Evidence: Critiquing the scientific explanations or solutions proposed by peers, citing relevant evidence about the natural and
designed world(s).

7517B95739C7491FB567D7BED8F2CD57.description:
Constructing
Explanations and
Designing Solutions: Using evidence in constructing explanations that specify variables, describing and predicting phenomena, and
designing multiple solutions to design problems.

B65C31642DA044B1ABBB3FFD3B14D1AB.description:
Using Mathematics and
Computational Thinking: Extending quantitative measurements to a variety of physical properties; using computation and mathematics to
analyze data and compare alternative design solutions.

7439C8B1191149F7A34479CB12A11C7A.description:
Analyzing and
Interpreting Data: Introducing quantitative approaches to collecting data and conducting multiple trials of qualitative observations,
using digital tools whenever possible.

6EA26AC781DB49EBBF0739B0909C0735.description:
Planning and Carrying
Out Investigations: Designing and conducting investigations with controlled variables; providing evidence to support explanations or
design solutions

3069A56B5143491FB496DD4966837F62.description:
Developing and Using
Models: Building and revising simple models; using models to represent events and design solutions

069E5865982F4FCE89ED3C39D0FD0D5A.description:
Asking Questions and
Defining Problems: Specifying qualitative relationships.

document.title: 2023 Alabama Course of Study: Science

67609BFCE14345A49F9AC9C000FA136C.description:
Stability
and Change: Explanations of stability and change in natural or designed systems can be constructed by examining the changes
over time and processes at different scales, including the atomic scale. Small changes in one part of a system might
cause large changes in another part. Stability might be disturbed either by sudden events or gradual changes that
accumulate over time. Systems in a dynamic equilibrium are stable due to a balance of feedback mechanisms.

F3EACA10A5234985BDF0CBD77B3770E3.description:
Structure
and Function: Complex and microscopic structures and systems can be visualized, modeled, and used to describe how their function
depends on the shapes, composition, and relationships among its parts; therefore, complex natural and designed
structures and systems can be analyzed to determine how they function. Structures can be designed to serve particular
functions by taking into account the properties of different materials and how materials can be shaped and used.

0C11D51AE99F4C7285DCAC301EF9735A.description:
Energy and Matter:
Flows, Cycles,
and Conservation: Matter is conserved because atoms are conserved in physical and chemical processes. Within a natural or designed
system, the transfer of energy drives the motion and/or cycling of matter. Energy may take different forms (e.g.,
energy in fields, thermal energy, energy of motion). The transfer of energy can be tracked as energy flows through a
designed or natural system.

0273A259B5324F5AB348335D50DF34AF.description:
Systems
and System Models: Systems may interact with other systems; they may have sub-systems and may be part of larger complex systems.
Models can be used to represent systems and their interactions (such as inputs, processes and outputs) and energy, matter, and information flow within systems. Models are limited in that they represent only certain aspects of the
system under study.

E3773B7B423D4A3A96D690B070E0068C.description:
Scale, Proportion,
and Quantity: Time, space, and energy phenomena can be observed at various scales using models to study systems that are too
large or too small. The observed function of natural and designed systems may change with scale. Proportional
relationships among different types of quantities (e.g., speed as the ratio of distance traveled to time taken) provide
information about the magnitude of properties and processes. Scientific relationships can be represented through the
use of algebraic expressions and equations. Phenomena that can be observed at one scale may not be observable at
another scale.

06977FB2106C4E58B5D1B047F6D4823E.description:
Cause and Effect:
Mechanism
and Prediction: Relationships can be classified as causal or correlational, and correlation does not necessarily imply causation. Cause
and effect relationships may be used to predict phenomena in natural or designed systems. Phenomena may have
more than one cause, and some cause and effect relationships in systems can be described only by using probability.

9B702D4B851C48F690680BFF3AA89944.description:
Patterns: Macroscopic patterns are related to the nature of microscopic and atomic-level structure. Patterns in rates of change
and other numerical relationships can provide information about natural and human-designed systems. Patterns can
be used to identify cause and effect relationships. Graphs, charts, and images can be used to identify patterns in data.

F861EC0B3414431DA1D75B9E4D1AA834.description:
Obtaining, Evaluating,
and Communicating
Information: Evaluating the merit and validity of ideas and methods.

A8761C5059A44A2FB467511278194692.description:
Engaging in Argument
from Evidence: Constructing a convincing argument that supports or refutes claims for either explanations or solutions about the
natural and designed world(s).

45EBD9E99D7B4A03881517ED18D0F10E.description:
Constructing
Explanations and
Designing Solutions: Constructing explanations and designing solutions supported by multiple sources of evidence consistent with
scientific ideas, principles, and theories.

0E2BC14F528E42A09CAEDB0911A0A563.description:
Using Mathematics and
Computational Thinking: Identifying patterns in large data sets and using mathematical concepts to support explanations and arguments.

A66EF38AC4EC4DCC84DE5B4D0BA1EC64.description:
Analyzing and
Interpreting Data: Extending quantitative analysis to investigations, distinguishing between correlation and causation, and employing
basic statistical techniques of data and error analysis.

855B7555196B4931907FA4E87E5B3295.description:
Planning and Carrying
Out Investigations: Designing and conducting investigations that use multiple variables and provide evidence to support explanations or
solutions.

8349BBF279F241D6803EFC327B7A2C40.description:
Developing and Using
Models: Developing, utilizing, and revising models to describe, test, and predict more abstract phenomena and to design
systems.

264C474FD50442F491C5D85000303940.description:
Asking Questions and
Defining Problems: Specifying relationships between variables, clarifying arguments, and models

5394E80901B54E5B95DDDFF631396082.description:
Stability
and Change: Much of science deals with constructing explanations of how things change and how they remain stable. Change and
rates of change can be quantified and modeled over very short or very long periods of time. Some system changes are
irreversible. Feedback (negative or positive) can stabilize or destabilize a system. Systems can be designed for greater
or lesser stability.

ADEB29F696634605919450622A71EE07.description:
Structure
and Function: Investigating or designing new systems or structures requires a detailed examination of the properties of different
materials, the structures of different components, and connections of components to reveal the structure’s function
and/or solve a problem. The functions and properties of natural and designed objects and systems can be inferred
from their overall structure, the way their components are shaped and used, and the molecular substructures of their
various materials.

BF91E5EF6D0D43CB8041ECF47D547C01.description:
Energy and Matter:
Flows, Cycles,
and Conservation: The total amount of energy and matter in closed systems is conserved. Changes of energy and matter in a system can
be described in terms of the flow of energy and matter into, out of, and within that system. Energy cannot be created
or destroyed; it only moves between one place and another place, between objects and/or fields, or between systems.
Energy drives the cycling of matter within and between systems. In nuclear processes, atoms are not conserved, but
the total number of protons plus neutrons is conserved.

E6A882256F004C8294B14C423BEEDE76.description:
Systems
and System Models: Systems can be designed to do specific tasks. When investigating or describing a system, the boundaries and initial
conditions of the system need to be defined and their inputs and outputs analyzed and described using models.
Models (e.g., physical, mathematical, computer models) can be used to simulate systems and interactions (including
energy, matter, and information flows) within and between systems at different scales. Models can be used to predict
the behavior of a system, but these predictions have limited precision and reliability due to the assumptions and
approximations inherent in models.

BA7E412E728B401DA68AB6D9A9E903EA.description:
Scale, Proportion, and
Quantity: The significance of a phenomenon is dependent on the scale, proportion, and quantity at which it occurs. Some
systems can be studied only indirectly as they are too small, too large, too fast, or too slow for direct observation.
Patterns observable at one scale may not be observable or exist at other scales. Using the concept of orders of
magnitude allows one to understand how a model at one scale relates to a model at another scale. Algebraic thinking
is used to examine scientific data and predict the effect of a change in one variable on another (e.g., linear growth vs.
exponential growth).

8F5361482E4B40ACBB10472471A76A19.description:
Cause and Effect:
Mechanism
and Prediction: Empirical evidence is required to differentiate between cause and correlation and to make claims about specific
causes and effects. Cause and effect relationships can be suggested and predicted for complex natural and
human-designed systems by examining what is known about smaller-scale mechanisms within the system. Systems
can be designed to cause a desired effect. Changes in systems may have various causes that may not have equal
effects.

F0786C9AC3D54AA4A22E29FD5B3C3276.description:
Patterns: Different patterns may be observed at each of the scales at which a system is studied and can provide evidence for
causality in explanations of phenomena. Classifications or explanations used at one scale may fail or need revision
when information from smaller or larger scales is introduced, thus requiring improved investigations and
experiments. Patterns of performance of designed systems can be analyzed and interpreted to reengineer and improve
the system. Mathematical representations are needed to identify some patterns. Empirical evidence is needed to
identify patterns.

D548A58E4B734BED906E8CCB2F1B3950.description:
Obtaining, Evaluating,
and Communicating
Information: Evaluating the validity and reliability of claims, methods, and designs.

02C7D590EC224D769C307C7E729A77C3.description:
Engaging in Argument
from Evidence: Using appropriate, sufficient evidence and scientific reasoning to defend and critique claims and explanations about
the natural and designed world(s). Arguments may also come from current or historical episodes in science.

49FF131AFE3C49EAA724E778D83AF3B4.description:
Constructing
Explanations and
Designing Solutions: Constructing explanations and designs that are supported by multiple, independent, student-generated sources of
evidence consistent with scientific ideas, principles, and theories.

44D11980C4DF47A6A54EA74903CF6872.description:
Using Mathematics and
Computational Thinking: Using algebraic thinking and analysis, a range of linear and nonlinear functions (including trigonometric functions,
exponentials and logarithms), and computational tools for statistical analysis to analyze, represent, and model data.
Simple computational simulations are created and used based on mathematical models of basic assumptions.

B9F9AA80409C4626BE154F2A890E0D21.description:
Analyzing and
Interpreting Data: Introducing more detailed statistical analysis, the comparison of data sets for consistency, and the use of graphs and
models to generate and analyze data.

5F259586539342AF82011B6055194DF4.description:
Planning and Carrying
Out Investigations: Designing and conducting investigations that test and provide evidence for conceptual, mathematical, physical, and
empirical models.

BCF74A38B26A4F6A852A593BC60360FD.description:
Developing and Using
Models: Using, synthesizing, and developing models to predict and show relationships among variables between systems and
their components in the natural and designed world(s).

5ABEA74B426F4AD9818BD0BFD5BDA437.description:
Asking Questions and
Defining Problems: Formulating, refining, and evaluating empirically testable questions and design problems using models and
simulations.

secondary learning.

integrate, create, and share information within the postsecondary learning

HyperStudio, video, or animation; other digital and word processing tools such

environments in which technology support will be beneficial or essential for
