89C92E3743C1453E92D96C1F4BD4056D.description:

learning environments prior to high school graduation.

1ACB85B4DCC24D01BF31BC2BE5A080BD.description: Demonstrate the need for technology support in future learning environments.

postsecondary education or training.

Complete Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and/or other fiscal
reporting and application forms with assistance from family members and staff as
needed.

A96C3FB6879A4B96A420EBBEE84058CB.description:
Formulate and implement a plan for seeking needed financial assistance from

9575653665D745D18440966A014D3A74.description:

application procedures; prerequisites or competitive tactics such as merit,
community service, leadership or extracurricular activities; and lining up
references).

6E307FFDD5E14EEDBDB51EC558E01932.description:

CBD95F5885454FC7B67BBD7A0D0D35E6.description:

likely sources of financial aid and/or income support.

E021F3B3209646EC8DD526CD8D8EFB2A.description:

03E441A6F58F45B89F4BCD6AE5CEF2A8.description:

Schedule and implement strategies for postsecondary education/training

education.

Advocate for oneself in arranging support or accommodations from one or more

9C62B8517F42499FAD1585408AFCFCDA.description:
State and appropriately request accommodations and/or other support needs for

4361190E1CF54482B825651A655494BD.description:

or volunteer experiences, short essay, exam) for later admission to a
postsecondary learning program of choice.

FB4E73972A2348D789469540CD3AD283.description:

postsecondary education or training program choices (e.g., entrance exams

1617BD39E7AA4F45A909D9A2221938B1.description:

Assess abilities in relation to admissions requirements for selected postsecondary
education or training system(s).

19F7498DCAF547168E11F9550325F479.description:
Demonstrate the academic knowledge and skills required to pursue personal
choice(s) of postsecondary education/training options (e.g., diploma, grade-point

C40424CE7F424176937E8C721E491D11.description:

training system(s) (e.g., forms, fees, financial aid or funding, selection or

requirements).

9FEF65AFBD3140FB94E58439D4BAC509.description:

859BB839630240D8AE9B2B72BFFD9EFE.description:

universities, online research).

0C0EC11FA3D54D388717A3D474E495C1.description:

individual post-school goals and the positive and negative aspects of each.

A61CBB0AC81646A69A806C61C9AF7817.description:

16478CFF07244B92AA1E617F6D25CE2E.description:

B2CC38B9F3774DEFB7F2698D5BBC6E4C.description:

Assess and select three specific potential areas of interest, preference, and/or need

25FA1257436D42B1A8F65766C37465B7.description:

2605313FD6E842B09A8CE26AD1570232.description:
Identify postsecondary education or training area(s) of interest, preference,
and/or needs (e.g., arts-skilled, outdoor-skilled, technical-skilled, clerical-skilled

C6EA0277B8F14F8E99F1C307CAECDE50.description:

goals.

EBEC207D75BF4975BB769CA199F7F047.description:
Assess how employment allows for the meeting of personal needs and wants and
apply these insights or results in an individualized career planning process.

AE56DF5B7425448E8716C9E1E5D2AA35.description: State the purpose of gainful employment to meet personal needs and wants.

4675B0A82E1E45BE977C2C1792482FC7.description:
Identify the general impact of receiving wages (e.g., ability to pay bills and
purchase necessary goods).

C2EE77412C5F4151B2B8BDBFF2DA2C96.description:
Describe the short-term impact of receiving wages and other benefits (e.g.,
having money for a concert or movie or vacation days).

E7EE5EEC19744C99B35CCAA569B94C5A.description:
Describe the long-term impact of receiving wages and other benefits (e.g.,
ability to save for college or a home, health insurance in case of injury or
illness).

8EC7F52545C543BDB1D677BC081335AD.description:
Analyze both the short-term and long-term impacts of receiving wages and
other benefits and explain the need to plan for employment with this impact in
mind (e.g., identifying careers with greater and lesser impact of wages and
benefits).

13862DE9AB6A481688C52AA8D252A796.description: Describe the impact of wages on personal financial status.

062FA558F1F3423688EAE1A85F36116A.description: Transition Target: Analyze the impact of employment on financial status.

A42BBBD6367247BDB6E5F51A234DBD82.description: Review, and revise as needed, personal career goals and objectives.

CC531FBDC0E34827B9441CAA38C25472.description:
Prioritize and sequence action steps needed to reach personal career goals and
objectives.

D003C6940BAE4F4490ABC0B83B6D7021.description:
Develop timelines and ways to monitor achievement of action steps needed to
reach personal career goals and objectives.

148A9AA9F0EC405D843AC86D928EC811.description:
Predict how pursuit of personal career interest(s) relates to achieving individual
postsecondary education goals (and independent living goal, if appropriate).

E76EC7BC287742F29AF4952627E38D3C.description: Create a personal career plan to meet career goal(s) and objectives.

6F226D0022FF4FE8BCE18A27B8B735BF.description:
Describe multiple personal assets that match the requirements of five given
occupations.

150EB6190A7845FBB416FF805E4CD312.description:
Describe multiple individual needs that contrast with the demands of five given
occupations.

35390EE4FEA841ACBB65F2B78785BC19.description:
Compare at least five varied career choices to individual assets, needs, and
career plan objectives.

DE068B23D9634BF8963BDA56A60277A3.description:
Evaluate and predict the outcomes of multiple employment options based upon
individual assets, needs, and career plan objectives.

5B94BB9E490C4B77A8E61CD73D2AA861.description: Compare personal assets with requirements of specific jobs or careers.

CBF6E41E7FA3446595578151EA6406BB.description:
Identify at least five sources of job descriptions (e.g., career guidance programs,
O*NET online, Department of Labor and other online resources, OneStop Career
Center, and ASVAB Web site).

98E3715675964C0DBE6EAF41D8635D0E.description:
List standards and qualifications that must be met to enter at least five given
industries/careers.

93A160E1852C46DC8037051D52C16E19.description:
Complete and utilize at least two work-related forms and documents for
obtaining employment (e.g., resumes, job applications, and tax forms).

540898216A3C4718BBB76ACAD0128861.description: Research, analyze, and report employment trends in a selected occupation.

294061B8A8624A9AB110DCC0BA82B132.description: Report and document information about specific jobs and careers of interest.

3415978804FA41BBB8AC3E3A8052BE38.description:
Identify three or more major skills learned through experience with hobbies,
chores, and work experiences.

3DE4C88FE22740E597B9C0B57DD48D67.description:
Describe results of transition assessments that highlight career-related aptitudes
and motivations.

A35D05ADEA0C4055A7D7004382880F22.description:
Categorize five or more skills or areas of knowledge that one has acquired from
a range of workplace experiences since middle school (e.g., job shadowing,
information-gathering interviews, volunteer work, unpaid and paid internships).

9E0D8B74E8234850B73F232D150AF618.description:
Analyze and report which occupational skills are essential to individual career
choice(s).

7E3622253C8C4785ADAD34482413C033.description:
Discuss and demonstrate personal career-related skills, aptitudes, and
dispositions.

D04F6D3E6BC243DD9A8C3E4048DA2A9C.description:
Identify a number of possible goals related to at least one domain (e.g.,
personal-social, occupational, further learning).

BC60DE249F9D498791AB7A9FF258D1FB.description:
Document at least one meaningful long-term goal in personal-social,
occupational, and other learning domains.

5AB9D321DCAA4B77A8E8CE229655AF91.description: Express at least one specific occupational interest.

807EB02225D544488B85161CABF2DED6.description: Identify the future career goal of greatest interest.

FB1CE5682AB14BD88DA5630C3548B6D7.description:
Express and document long-term goals in personal-social, occupational, and
further learning domains.

E5D2AE3FB51F4FADA5F0FF64889B8890.description:
Transition Target: Identify personal career interests and aptitudes helpful to achieve
Postsecondary Education, Employment, and/or Community Independent Living goals.

document.title: Alabama Transition Standards

87FCD134F2DB4E9B9EF7ADD2A94701FC.description: Identify the values and beliefs held by parents or authority figures.

7F852C52217646F5A2CE6FD21D7D9232.description:
Analyze the values and beliefs held by others in society and how these compare
with those of parents or authority figures, understanding that different
perspectives can be held by different people.

7ADAF6AAA7C14FA18E2FDA6C1C5CC761.description:
Distinguish between personal values and beliefs and those of parents, authority
figures, and others in society.

19D63B7AB6B8408AAE973251826993CD.description:
Demonstrate an ability to make decisions that are informed by personal values
and beliefs (e.g., personal valuing of higher education informing the decision to
apply to college, rather than pursuing college only due to suggestions of others).

8BABEBE4D7364A2785D77922FF8BE75A.description: Demonstrate an ability to identify and act upon personal values and beliefs.

F2A7EB1EB42C43378EF7AAE8449039E4.description:
Identify personal responsibilities across settings (e.g., academic or employment
requirements, paying bills, and upkeep of living arrangements).

E6F8C85A9EE64FFC9EC759B6E6D04B61.description:
Discuss personal responsibilities and expectations of others (e.g., parents,
administrators, or others may provide assistance but are ultimately not
responsible for success).

9DE2E6777DD749E1A63D7D3F962B3FEF.description:
Analyze the consequences associated with completing or not completing personal
responsibilities (e.g., effort put into academics affecting the likelihood of
attending college).

3A37FC9B0A764E469AD7C4A992F4773A.description:
Demonstrate acceptance of personal responsibility by fulfilling responsibilities
and/or accepting consequences of not fulfilling responsibilities.

1C4ACFE58225443496044E5ED93A98C3.description: Transition Target: Demonstrate independence and responsibility across settings.

80943F1FABFF4A79B36E323AF1A4022D.description:
Identify responsible behaviors (e.g., social interactions, appropriate social
behavior, and conflict resolution skills) across various environments.

D7D9B26F3627440DA89F010574DC8D23.description:
Recognize responsible and irresponsible behaviors and outcomes of behavior as
it relates to personal goals across various environments.

097EAB9549A2423891E528B2E820573B.description: Explore responsible behaviors that lead to positive post-school outcomes.

DCFD4DD1F1FE4B7D87411745E21EC65E.description:
Apply the identified behavioral skills in order to achieve postsecondary
outcomes and goals.

36C96249D48542F78B21005353C5B1BD.description:
Develop socially responsible behaviors (e.g., social interaction, appropriate
behaviors, conflict resolution skills).

ECDBEF60D1EA4DB9813CDE8F46E119B3.description:
Identify effective communication skills for sharing and gaining information
(e.g., written, verbal, nonverbal, and use of augmentative devices).

8E3EE67267B24858AA9455AE2DDF1F40.description:
Distinguish between effective and ineffective communication skills (e.g.,
assertive but not aggressive, negotiating skills, taking turns, listening skills)
within integrated settings, and explore benefits and consequences.

E3D2D253E5BC474EBD877891BE21A15D.description:
Engage in effective communication skills and self-monitoring of ineffective
skills via role-play, peer feedback, and real-life experiences.

1F53E57955A44C32BF0DF69CEE5B4FF5.description:
Apply effective communication skills to interact with others in integrated
settings using various methods (e.g., written, verbal, nonverbal, and use of
augmentative devices).

B17B70047EF04D1B9AFCB69422E1F435.description:
Develop communication skills to interact with others in integrated settings
(e.g., written, verbal, nonverbal, use of augmentative devices).

9C928C3B8C5D4FC78C00B1DBFD1EB5CA.description:
Identify personal management skills (e.g., behavioral self-control, personal
space, social norms) to manage oneself in various environments
(home/work/community).

3ED79EE413984F2BABD4F85C875A03D7.description:
Distinguish between appropriate and inappropriate behaviors across various
environments (home/work/community).

C2DC866DFEF04BE88E5020E4048D8453.description:
Engage in appropriate social interactions in multiple environments
(home/work/community).

B6FC97463B0E47B0874EDC6B8DF2B544.description:
Apply appropriate skills for interpersonal relationships, including
teamwork/collaboration, active/passive listening, and respect for self and
others.

FC0E19D9F30C4C7E9704E039FC03C5BF.description:
Develop personal management skills needed for successful interpersonal
relationships in home, work, and community.

3BC572CE49BA461999D8280F29D5AA21.description:
Transition Target: Demonstrate personal management and communication skills in
order to interact with others in integrated settings.

46C8D72BFFA54381BFCB20FE18610A4D.description:
Discuss types of socially responsible behavior across various environments
(e.g., identify assertive, passive, and aggressive behavior in written scenarios).

558C0F8A35594685B533B9648A212650.description:
Investigate self-advocacy as it relates to attainment of postsecondary goals
(e.g., self-knowledge of interests, list of strengths, and areas of need).

74885BF547BF474893DB4E581E6B00D6.description:
Analyze postsecondary options and openly discuss concerns and preferences,
asking questions when needed (e.g., actively participate in IEP
planning/evaluation).

F6EF498B4197445B8F7DC6F430DCADC5.description:
Demonstrate self-advocacy by applying effective skills in preparation for
transition to postsecondary environment (e.g., call and request information about
a needed service for transition from school to community, postsecondary
education, or workforce).

EB196B50F8B34EE6932BBFF167C4912E.description: Demonstrate self-advocacy across social, academic, and work environments.

257885D680CF4A85967B08A48E94867A.description:
Identify a range of desired positive adult outcomes in social, academic, and work
environments (e.g., desire to have friends, live independently, maintain
employment).

040F7BACEF8C408E81C1B4A48E7800B5.description: Discuss personal goals, decisions, and options.

B83866FEB5CC43A98E0B1362834923F6.description:
Analyze personal successes and failures in order to identify available supports
and evaluate positive/negative outcomes.

3F5B49338F0B4CAC9FC4D50B55B92461.description:
Demonstrate self-determination through integration of personal experiences in
social, academic, and work environments into individual’s view of the self
(e.g., incorporate positive use of knowledge of self-characteristics, strengths, and
limitations based on life experiences).

BE024168273C46D88D12C7AB194FCE43.description:
Demonstrate self-determination across social, academic, and work
environments.

64A88FB2B5D24B2EA36D59E4217F6BE7.description:
Identify strengths and weaknesses through self-exploration and assessment of
prior successes, failures, and other personal learning experiences.

69F2AE73FDF7446FA6A60A0ACDAB1983.description:
Distinguish between positive and negative social influences (e.g., peers,
family members, mentors, and role models) and manage feedback received about
the self from others.

1845E56BF5D74D01B3192CDFF84C57CC.description:
Analyze and revise beliefs about the self and expected outcomes (e.g., assess
which beliefs are accurate or inaccurate, how these beliefs have been shaped by
others, and how these might impact goals and decisions).

B76ABDA6F2B944809FB400189E65C6FE.description:
Demonstrate self-efficacy through goal-setting and decision-making (e.g.,
stating that a particular goal is possible, setting the goal, and making decisions
that will lead to meeting that goal).

A9DEEA3D1C5C482EBF589FBE9E6D75BE.description: Demonstrate self-efficacy across social, academic, and work environments.

02992B5C3C824E38BF74858ACFE59E52.description:
Transition Target: Demonstrate self-efficacy, self-determination, and self-advocacy
across social, academic, and work environments.

649D9A3ADF1A40CFA04CEDB412BA9585.description:
Discuss transportation and/or mobility issues (e.g., transportation to/from
school, home, within community, associated costs, routes, and schedules) and
positive/negative aspects of use.

6E90CB8F4F3D4C46A780C676DD187766.description:
Assess personal transportation services and/or mobility issues; develop
strategies for obtaining, using, and maintaining transportation (e.g., public or
private transportation); and examine related rules and regulations.

DCD9E465A8644ECD9ABD4D02C9F7D5C1.description:
Develop a plan that utilizes private or public transportation services, following
related rules and regulations (e.g., driver’s education, bus costs, routes, and
schedule, local resources such as taxi or door-to-door pickup).

A83691BD69644AE58F8B6A7E3D35B3D1.description:
Utilize identified method of transportation to reach a desired location while
obeying related laws and regulations (e.g., using a bus pass, wearing a seat belt,
using a helmet when biking, and using crosswalks).

0E7AAF4267164EBCAFE6E9A6C2F36DE4.description:
Identify and select options for meeting personal transportation or mobility needs
and develop strategies for obtaining those options.

405A5856E53A430D80532C84193A7188.description:

issues and mobility needs.

CD1F397901944CF4A7E2986B157DCDDA.description:
Discuss wellness needs and examine approaches to addressing those needs
through available resources (e.g., optometrist, dentist, exercise program, and
healthy food options).

A7362C2FEA3442F7BED97AEFA444A7C6.description:
Assess steps to work toward personal wellness needs and list resources to address
those needs.

1E9811327C704810A6224D49BC5DDEAE.description:
Develop a personal wellness plan that includes goals related to specific wellness
needs as identified by prior assessment.

9FEFDCA5B6CB4E9DBDEA2D8358CC4DDF.description:
Implement and evaluate an individualized plan that addresses wellness needs
such as an exercise plan, balanced meal options, and routine health check-ups.

7110AC3139D1486F99B47A228B677D0C.description:
Develop and select strategies to address wellness (e.g., maintenance of good
health and prevention of illness).

7F39203B80A747D19C01188363BEDF3D.description:
Discuss healthcare needs and examine approaches to addressing those needs
through available resources (e.g., emergency needs, doctor visits, and pharmacy
care).

D5A263591DC24A499EA0228BCEF49715.description: Assess personal healthcare needs and list resources to address those needs.

5671B038D4D640D3BBD5379C0FA62C61.description:
Develop a personal healthcare plan that includes goals related to specific medical
needs as identified by prior assessment.

1D6AB5B2328A400C8963C147B897A072.description:
Implement and evaluate an individualized plan that addresses healthcare needs
such as regular doctor visits, prescription maintenance, and emergencies.

B35967FFBFC845998AABFF9F4FFFCB2E.description: Identify and develop a plan to address personal healthcare needs.

2DDB81D2A41449EEA682E384FC610C5D.description:

wellness needs.

11206937A18D4DD1B812905A6F9A4695.description:
Identify appropriate hygiene, grooming, and dress routines for a variety of settings
(school, community, and work).

CADFF17C91E847F993800765195AEBA4.description:
Investigate the importance and possible results of dressing
appropriately/inappropriately for differing environments (e.g., interviews, school,
and community).

00D5865151214B2AB1AF53275A1925CD.description:
Select and discuss choice of grooming and dress as they relate to various
environments (e.g., school, community, and work).

ABF11656895242ECB1A87F9DC1A71BCD.description:
Apply proper hygiene and grooming based on understanding of requirements in
various environments (e.g., interview setting, job setting, school setting, and
social setting).

7CE19A54C01642AE917F5DDD652C99AC.description:
Exhibit appropriate hygiene and grooming for different environments (e.g.,
school, community, work).

6BB19D28997841DFBCADB7753DC66BC2.description: Identify appropriate clothing options based on weather, budget, and care.

A2F57F969A2940D0A355681B153FA22E.description:
Determine personal clothing options based on size, preference, and
season.

D895D0E99DB9415FB5C0B16FEB5A9AF4.description: Assess personal needs to make appropriate clothing purchases.

AE8FBD77D7644EE884B4430E794EA685.description:
Prepare appropriate wardrobe (e.g., laundry, ironing, and purchasing articles
of clothing as needed).

177FB64922084C89B7D41CEA845DED1F.description: Demonstrate the ability to select and purchase appropriate clothing.

Identify general safety issues and procedures applicable to home and community
environments, including fire safety and severe weather drills.

9AC5C78EBDFB443D82660105D1EF5E3B.description:
Demonstrate appropriate protocol via role play for various emergency situations
(e.g., fire in home, heart attack, flooded pipes, and severe weather).

84C970560ACD43F0BB4FCD1EFDA27BF4.description:
Generate a plan for monthly household repairs and maintenance and determine
appropriate resources to resolve current safety issues.

67906A0DD7A244D68B45F4BBAE34C53D.description:
Assess repairs or safety issues according to current plan (e.g., making a purchase,
and calling for services).

1D807BA3C6F84A61BEB9E8BC5DF38D9A.description:
Identify procedures for household safety, as well as maintenance and improvement
of personal living situation.

CDD074B704FA4EC98E6D01B44EA84FC0.description:
Transition Target: Formulate a plan to address issues related to the acquisition and
maintenance of independent living skills.

2FF07CAD5F4D4B3BAC654EE50104B3A9.description: Discuss and illustrate wants/needs in relation to income and living arrangements.

D0241405FA934181B597621EB5D808CB.description:
Diagram budget according to necessities, utilities, and rent and identify possible
living arrangements.

241CDE5DC8264993B7120A2B19CADBD4.description:
Design a plan addressing living arrangements and wants/needs (e.g.,
independent living, school dorm, and transitional living).

E7063859E3DA4A3B984B7EF813C0CB9A.description:
Appraise appropriateness of identified living arrangements (e.g., size, distance
to employment, family, relation to budget, and utilities).

81CD1DCF6BA8428EBA73E32B5C9632B5.description: Integrate the process of budgeting within living arrangements.

74FBFC65F03E45658096E77BE8A3CBD9.description:
Determine and prioritize personal needs and wants according to current or
expected income.

662DC35EB92E4B12BFAF2F42C03BBD79.description:
Determine various modes of payment options (e.g., cash, check, money order,
and debit cards) for daily living needs according to current or expected income.

E55CAC1E717E4BEE81F721FC66C9E7F1.description:
Create personal budget according to daily living needs (e.g., food, clothing,
housing, transportation, wellness needs, healthcare, utilities, insurance, and
benefits).

3380AFD6272548BFB3CDBD31EC9AE199.description:
Prepare, maintain, and assess a personal budget (e.g., housing, food, clothing,
transportation, wellness needs, healthcare, utilities, insurance, benefits).

C6F85154034443F48C06039E341AB441.description:
Employ and evaluate financial management skills for personal daily living
needs.

3EF1C2FF486E424186AE6B90A41E8101.description:
Transition Target: Formulate and implement financial management skills to be used
in daily living.

3A48B73ACCCD45BAB433A2EDCF9201DF.description:
Examine interests in leisure and recreational activities available in the school
and community.

F50383A5AE6F447AACAEE0A3E7A704DA.description: Self-evaluate to determine specific interests in leisure and recreational activities.

CF20ED03E84C47039CCC87B90B658270.description:
Report on a specific school or community activity (e.g., school, band, civic
club, YMCA, camp) and how it aligns with personal interests.

BBC160D2D2924046BB5CEBCB031B84BD.description:
Arrange requirements and expectations for participation in the chosen school or
community recreational activities (e.g., rules, associated fees, and time
commitment).

F0E6B2747ABB48199AD203BB069AE21F.description:
Develop and practice recreational and leisure interests available within the
school and community.

85A8F3755A7D42FC886C6ED225994F61.description: Identify community resources individuals associated with providing services.

2EC99790DD0A48FE820878AA6C3E5D62.description: Differentiate individual needs for specific community resources and services.

A347F725E1A14283800B1577DB31FB4D.description: Contrast specific community resources and services when needed.

9B1DEDD47F7F4E399BB5AE523343D039.description: Formulate specific community resources and services when needed.

A2FFD36DD37147AFB7F6CCC0755A2E58.description: Identify resources and services within the community.

E7B4DD20FA9043C3BDBA7649B5F2DDEB.description:
Describe community issues, laws, and the consequences of disobeying rules or
laws.

4403C4A469174A0BAEE84638F61ECD84.description: List individual legal rights as a member of society.

D4068A474AA0433DA8F40F9BCAFCCDF0.description: Analyze the legal and judicial processes on the local, state, and federal levels.

55401E8A1A9444039BCDFFDEA34C8392.description: Interpret and prepare legal forms (e.g., tax, employment, and voter registration).

1ED3B17C8A7B48E9B64A459F05994F50.description: Identify the basic elements of the legal and judicial process.

ABB48A6102F5433892E23EDF4F97CF5C.description:
Transition Target: Formulate ideas and identify issues related to citizenship,
community, and cultures within communities in order to become engaged in daily life.

C478CFBAB2A1498B8C36164DFAF46A68.description:
Demonstrate cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), use of an automated external defibrillator (AED),
and first aid for choking victims.

86249DABA314413D94B31E38342568D7.description: Demonstrate medical aseptic techniques for handwashing.

F0CD137D017240FB941AD02CA9F150A9.description: Measure, record, and graph height and weight.

Summarize practices for the prevention and early detection of diseases, including health screenings
and examinations.

359C1BFAA9CA43CA9F29664BD2EE472D.description:
Explain how cultural and individual differences relate to wellness and quality of life and how these
differences impact the overall health of society.

9C0880A98F0E48219579806630AAA3E3.description: Describe environmental conditions and lifestyle choices that affect wellness.

DF269BFA050642FDAFEBFEA9242EDBA6.description: Explain risk factors that contribute to illness, including heredity, environment, lifestyle, diet, and age.

D9E5C1F823B348588E63660305207B7E.description: Research and report on current health and wellness topics.

AAC8ACD3D1434D77AF1C662FB849210F.description: Describe basic structures and functions of the human body systems.

2071B2A3B85945C9968AF102346586D5.description: Identify common medical terms and abbreviations associated with the healthcare industry.

521ED44F646E4D629B27444038BDDC41.description: Determine time using the 24-hour time format utilized in the healthcare industry.

6479C293DAA64DFB85E613B15358EE43.description:
Apply the metric system to convert standard weights, measurements, and volumes commonly used in a
healthcare setting.

075C9D0B4E514FEF9DD08D067192B64A.description: Demonstrate verbal and nonverbal communication techniques appropriate for healthcare industry settings.

9528C9AE67534440B5278554EB04796E.description: Research and report on a medical malpractice case.

952B895E5E834BFA93CDE618678DDBFF.description:
Identify and explain legal and ethical practices related to the healthcare industry, including malpractice,
negligence, invasion of privacy, HIPAA, ethics and law, Patients’ Bill of Rights, licensure, and use of social
media.

E0136032AE6E4C0D8F33E0AD45D221A1.description: Investigate and present information about a healthcare career area of interest.

3232BEA84FA34118860620508A244DAC.description: Research and report on the impact of medical research on the healthcare industry.

C588B68930C94E0484B225FA2F3FF5CF.description:
Research and report on the historical development of the healthcare industry, its leaders, and its
response to major scientific advancements.

F532599D8340495581A09AF01F576FD4.description: Describe a variety of healthcare professions, indicating the purpose and scope of practice of each one.

C3733E8886E8494CBA028A88C9CF6A5D.description:
Demonstrate effective infection control techniques as defined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
(CDC) and The Joint Commission guidelines.

3E8F09C2809847A190A4390B06ED38D1.description:
Participate in a Career and Technical Student Organization (CTSO) to increase knowledge and skills and to
enhance leadership and teamwork.

43E4E67747204A7BA86AEFF20F3A63A7.description:
Advocate and practice safe, legal, responsible, and ethical use of information and technology tools specific to
the industry pathway.

43D7B86C71494CCCAB9DC430E909FFAA.description:
Explore the range of careers available in the field and investigate their educational requirements and
demonstrate job-seeking skills including resume-writing and interviewing.

C21324AD1860455D8076EB7439EA7CE8.description:
Demonstrate effective workplace and employability skills, including communication, awareness of diversity,
positive work ethic, problem-solving, time management, and teamwork.

D87D25FA07144ED2AA0F76C0D4D5FB4A.description:

is composed of
rational and
irrational
numbers.

2E63FC8BAF4449F0BB8AB00BA30C0872.description:
When given a real-world
scenario, choose the independent or dependent variable. Ex.: If I buy 5 books
that cost $8.00 each, the total cost is $40. Which variable is independent?

EC7B90C5DE3A4C6599F8D1735E5CB12F.description:
Analyzing the association between two quantitative variables should involve statistical
procedures, such as examining (with technology) the
sum of squared deviations in
fitting a linear model, analyzing residuals for patterns,
generating a least-squares regression line and finding a
correlation coefficient, and
differentiating between correlation and causation.

D232EE906BD0497FAF16C01233880A67.description:
Scatter plots, including plots
over time, can reveal patterns, trends, clusters, and
gaps that are useful in analyzing the association between
two contextual variables.

EE8B3A8B5601403787CA872FD2ACE6DC.description:
Interpret general trends on a
graph. (Limited to increase
and decrease)

361E7F607FE544F296A774BF99DD7370.description:
Distributions of quantitative
data (continuous or discrete)
in one variable should be described in the context of the
data with respect to what is
typical (the shape, with appropriate measures of center and
variability, including standard
deviation) and what is not
(outliers), and these characteristics can be used to compare
two or more subgroups with
respect to a variable.

32E756D4ACA84260B3E5C321CCEBF1CA.description:
After collecting data, or
with given data, construct a
simple graph (line, pie, bar,
picture, etc.) or table and
interpret the data in terms
of range and mode.

63B4803B024A47BC84D1F67B6FEE0606.description:
Mathematical and statistical
reasoning about data can be
used to evaluate conclusions
and assess risks.

51E601A5B65D4142851997A336647FD0.description:
Graphs can be used to obtain exact or approximate solutions of
equations, inequalities, and systems of equations and inequalities—including systems of linear
equations in two variables and
systems of linear and quadratic
equations (given or obtained by
using technology).

4152C92D44094AC2B9B9DCDA80B99872.description:
Graphs can be used to obtain exact or approximate solutions of
equations, inequalities, and systems of equations and inequalities—including systems of linear
equations in two variables and
systems of linear and quadratic
equations (given or obtained by
using technology).

5C13A1292592490E8C72A5BA64AC6ED8.description:
The structure of an equation or
inequality (including, but not
limited to, one-variable linear
and quadratic equations, inequalities, and systems of linear equations in two variables) can be
purposefully analyzed (with and
without technology) to determine
an efficient strategy to find a solution, if one exists, and then to
justify the solution.

0DE0C16475CD4F71B5AA7861A16B6B90.description:
Given a real-world scenario, identify the appropriate unit to obtain the most
accurate measurement. (Ex:
When baking a cake,
should you measure 1 cup
of sugar with a teaspoon or
a measuring cup?)

B92CE786C24C48ABA19A0977DF4E85EC.description:
Quantitative reasoning includes
and mathematical modeling requires attention to units of
measurement.

A9C483BAE599464CA0754A0A41352850.description:
Solve real world problems
involving addition and/or
subtraction of rational numbers (whole numbers of
decimals) using models
when needed.

12EB450652524A12A69C1F62EA7EC689.description:
Together, irrational numbers
and rational numbers complete
the real number system, representing all points on the number
line, while there exist numbers
beyond the real numbers called
complex numbers.

document.title: 2019 Alabama Alternate Achievement Standards

BB21BAD85CAB4A52A496FE9727C55868.description: Use geometric shapes to describe real world objects.

395E8686AB1545ADA4ED8EC9A6D52183.description:
Experiencing the mathematical
modeling cycle in problems involving geometric concepts,
from the simplification of the
real problem through the solving
of the simplified problem, the interpretation of its solution, and
the checking of the solution’s
feasibility, introduces geometric
techniques, tools, and points of
view that are valuable to problem-solving

AC0F7981F9F74C09BD006D3874F36629.description:
Recognizing congruence, similarity, symmetry, measurement
opportunities, and other geometric ideas, including right triangle
trigonometry, in real-world contexts provides a means of building understanding of these concepts and is a powerful tool for
solving problems related to the
physical world in which we live.

C08BF15247254B988A178D04F78D61F2.description:
Proofs of theorems can sometimes be made with transformations, coordinates, or algebra;
all approaches can be useful, and
in some cases, one may provide a
more accessible or understandable argument than another.

337D728FDC6741629C1B5DDFD2F267DB.description:
When given a parallelogram
and the measure of one side
or one angle, identify the
measure of the opposite side
or angle.

DA4AF2345C0A4E63A4C1EBE39214AE54.description:
When given an isosceles triangle and a measure of a leg
or base angle, identify the
measure of the other leg or
base angle.

2D02350145CF412BA93332F6D536DB4D.description:
Demonstrate perpendicular
lines, parallel lines, line segments, angles, and circles by
drawing, modeling, identifying, or creating.

7DA3890496674BECA3E6551970978C23.description:
Proof is the means by which we
demonstrate whether a statement
is true or false mathematically,
and proofs can be communicated
in a variety of ways (e.g., twocolumn, paragraph).

95BCBBF2E8E243548A8B550762004FBF.description:
Using technology to construct
and explore figures with constraints provides an opportunity
to explore the independence and
dependence of assumptions and
conjectures.

F6EAD23924984C7083480EAFBAABECCA.description:
When given two congruent
triangles that have been
transformed (limit to a translation), determine the congruent parts.
(Ex: Determine which leg
on Triangle A is congruent
to which leg on Triangle B).

B817122525884CD5A08EF9136758B73B.description:
Showing that two figures are
congruent involves showing that
there is a rigid motion (translation, rotation, reflection, or glide
reflection) or, equivalently, a sequence of rigid motions that
maps one figure to the other.

24D570DB4E064F049762E78E65DBCA3D.description:
Identify and/or model characteristics of a geometric
figure that has undergone a
transformation (reflection,
rotation, translation) by
drawing, explaining, or using manipulatives.

25DD01F4FE454E88B6F2CF31A0680E5D.description:
Applying geometric transformations to figures provides opportunities for describing the attributes of the figures preserved
by the transformation and for
describing symmetries by examining when a figure can be
mapped onto itself.

505BFE391789406D954B0605603C7912.description:
Find the perimeter or area
of a square, rectangle, or
equilateral triangle to solve
real-world problems when
given the length of at least
one side.

B49F884BD1834EFCB818B87F10D63195.description:
When an object is the image of
a known object under a similarity transformation, a length,
area, or volume on the image
can be computed by using proportional relationships.

76B3E8AE027947C6AF22D2BE4CC69973.description:
Constructing approximations of
measurements with different
tools, including technology, can
support an understanding of
measurement.

EAA9EDABAD1F4A93B90F607FD1F53DDF.description:
Compare and contrast the
volume of real-world geometric figures.

C356A04D3D9D45E5BF18EB89243FE3B2.description:
Given a cross section of a
three-dimensional object,
identify the shapes of twodimensional cross sections
(limited to sphere, rectangular prism, or triangular
prism).

D4AA19F3FA9E4D83863DE32669B484D9.description:
Areas and volumes of figures
can be computed by determining how the figure might be obtained from simpler figures by
dissection and recombination.

independent or dependent
variable.

cost $2.00 each, the total
cost is $4. Which variable
is independent?

Conditional probabilities – that

“conditioned” by some known
information – can be computed
from data organized in
contingency tables. Conditions
or assumptions may affect the
computation of a probability.

2525FD3E023449D5ADBFB4921EE8B0B4.description:
Two events are independent if
the occurrence of one event
does not affect the probability
of the other event. Determining
whether two events are
independent can be used for
finding and understanding
probabilities.

0E7EB025EADA4FDDA99F0B815C8237C3.description:
Data analysis techniques can
be used to develop models of
contextual situations and to
generate and evaluate
possible solutions to real
problems involving those
contexts.

0BC5738205854A3FB9446FCF5570C50B.description:
Interpret general trends on a
graph. (Limited to increase
and decrease).

8FFA8023E0C24E84A50B4A10A4D438B3.description:
Data arise from a context and
come in two types: quantitative
(continuous or discrete) and
categorical. Technology can be
used to “clean” and organize
data, including very large data
sets, into a useful and
manageable structure—a first
step in any analysis of data.

A9402392621A489AB8EB78591A1DDA78.description:
When given a two-way
table summarizing data
on two categorical
variables collected from
the same subjects,
identify possible
association between the
two variables.

Making and defending
informed, data-based decisions
is a characteristic of a
quantitatively literate person.

B705379BCEEF491397D1827A208B773F.description:
Make predictions and draw
conclusions from two
variable data based on data
displays and apply the
results to a real-world
situation.

DC14E091C9DA47ACB4FA8229358CF79D.description:
Mathematical and statistical
reasoning about data can be
used to evaluate conclusions
and assess risks.

inequalities can be used to
analyze and make predictions,
both within mathematics and as
mathematics is applied in
different contexts – in
particular, contexts that arise in
relation to linear, quadratic, and
exponential situations.

Identify equivalent
expressions given a linear
expression using arithmetic
operations.

E0FEBE08AF994BC796E1FC62B2E6BEF9.description:
The structure of an equation or
inequality (including, but not
limited to, one-variable linear

inequalities, and systems of
linear equations in two
variables) can be purposefully
analyzed (with and without
technology) to determine an

to justify the solution.

Finding solutions to an
equation, inequality, or system
of equations or inequalities
requires the checking of
candidate solutions, whether
generated analytically or
graphically, to ensure that
solutions are found and that
those found are not extraneous.

F8AB734AC54D4A0397028D7CA3B94058.description:
Solve simple algebraic

scenarios with one variable
using multiplication or
division.

Expressions can be rewritten in

different characteristics or
features visible.

problem.

Expressions can be rewritten in

algebraic properties, including
properties of addition,

different characteristics or
features visible.

the real number system,
representing all points on the
number line, while there exist
numbers beyond the real
numbers called complex
numbers.

real-world scenario. (Ex:
Choose the graph that
shows a steady increase or
decrease rather than a graph
with fluctuating data).

Functions model a wide variety
of real situations and can help
students understand the processes
of making and changing
assumptions, assigning variables,
and finding solutions to
contextual problems.

Given the graph of a linear

Functions can be represented
graphically and key features of

graphically and key features of
the graphs, including zeros,
intercepts, and, when relevant,
rate of change and

be associated with and
interpreted in terms of the
equivalent symbolic
representation.

Functions that are members of
the same family have
distinguishing attributes
(structure) common to all
functions within that family.

Functions can be described by
using a variety of
representations: mapping
diagrams, function notation
(e.g., f(x) = x2), recursive
definitions, tables, and graphs.

01D953BFAA9845ECAEEC19C730D74296.description:
Functions can be described by
using a variety of

diagrams, function notation
(e.g., f(x) = x2), recursive
definitions, tables, and graphs.

of linear equations in two
variables and systems of linear
and quadratic equations (given
or obtained by using
technology).

EC65C369F2F6486B90D10BF5F62D7A2C.description:
Graphs can be used to obtain
exact or approximate solutions
of equations, inequalities, and
systems of equations and
inequalities – including systems
of linear equations in two
variables and systems of linear
and quadratic equations (given
or obtained by using
technology).

13C54971C2F242B487D45CA6D3A1D39B.description:
When given a relation in
table form, identify the
graph that represents the
relation (Ex: The points
(5,5); (6,4); (3,7) are given
to the student along with
three graphs, and the
student chooses the graph
that represents the relation).

Functions shift the emphasis
from a point-by-point
relationship between two
variables (input/output) to
considering an entire set of
ordered pairs (where each first
element is paired with exactly
one second element) as an entity
with its own features and
characteristics.

document.title: SOCIAL STUDIES ALTERNATE ACHIEVEMENT STANDARDS

ECEF74D19BF64E69B39BD4932E17BF81.description:
Demonstrate an awareness of current
events at the local, state, or national level.

BD0EB94C51FF46C2B593BDF129419AA0.description:
Recognize opportunities for participation in
community and civic action.

2359A272C7C446CE944B36B044CE118F.description:
Recognize Alabama’s growing role in the
world politically and socially including its impact of the
modern Civil Rights Movement from 1954 to the present.

D58552BDA9474A7389BF9F8F1B0CAB32.description:
Recognize modern social and economic
opportunities and define what they are. Examples
include legal protections for workers with disabilities and
anti-discrimination laws.

DB49629E5C01482B9C40E7AB67305F7F.description:
Demonstrate that individuals have a
responsibility to be good citizens and community
members; identify the legal definition of a United States
citizen and non-citizen.

4D0A7AA0D4824755A20C3E0BC5CD5A2D.description:
Identify the principles and purposes of a
budget; identify wants and needs and recognize that
each has a cost, including food, clothing, shelter,
entertainment, utilities.

A438124395B74D55B00B6E414454A96E.description:
Recall that consumers have to make
decisions based on resources and scarcity; recognize
examples of consumer and marketplace interaction;
identifying economic systems, including market,
command, and traditional.

02A920EB5DF94B9898467F5D5F045273.description:
Define goods and services; identify the basic
modern economic system based around currency;
identify goods and services and ways consumers get
access to them.

54E9671505FC4D3E9F40F19087608028.description:
Identify the basic rights under the Bill of
Rights; recognize how government protects individual
rights; recognize that citizens have a responsibility to
follow laws and that there are consequences for
breaking laws.

EAA61B77F23A4E659CA81D4BB8AF9EB2.description:
Recognize that there are different levels of
government, including local and state government.

58D279C57EB247189E97CA37F11A41E7.description:
Describe the basic ideals of American
democracy, including natural rights, basic freedoms, and
democratic representation; identify characteristics of
other government systems including, monarchy,
dictatorship, and democracy.

C34EC811DD5B434DB2BCE6AA9AD97620.description:
Define political parties; identify that political
leaders are elected in the United States and that political
parties work to get their candidates elected.

768FB1655E0046EF93B240A37783A72F.description:
Identify and recognize the various countries
and cultures that influenced the government of the
United States.

document.title: SOCIAL STUDIES ALTERNATE ACHIEVEMENT STANDARDS

D3B9B042D60840DCB717A57677673CD9.description:
Identify at least one key event,
accomplishment, or person from the late Middle Ages.

74293A01F2F64C9F8D30A28592AF06A1.description:
Identify at least one cultural change in the
High Middle Ages.

34C0B554C92A4543A02F7C08188CB88B.description:
Recognize an example of military or
governmental events that shaped Europe in the early
Middle Ages (600–1000 A.D./C.E.).

6CA1C90C0F4B4BF3A2A47ED977ADFE17.description:
Recognize the key aspects of at least one preColumbian culture, including Aztec, Incan, Mayan, Olmec,
Inuit, Creek and North American tribes; locate Central and
South America on a world map.

60DBF8D50CE64C5DADD096AA176C85C4.description:
Identify Africa on a world map; recognize the
language, religion, and customs of one early African
kingdom, including Ghana, Mali, and Songhai; identify the
importance of the gold and salt trade and Timbuktu.

DE1631BEEACB46C99F8CD1BAAB3FDE7A.description:
Locate China’s neighbors on a map including
Japan and Korea; identify at least one influence of China on
Japan, Korea, and Southeast Asia.

FE918E10E3CD47A5BB8D60A3C10ABE41.description:
Locate the Middle East and northern Africa on
a world map, specifically, the Arabian Peninsula; list at least
one religious, social, culture, or political characteristic of
early Islamic civilizations.

402167906B214D828EC14F01FA23A830.description:
Locate Russia on a world map; recognize how
Russia was important to the interaction of people and
trade between Asia and Europe in at least one area.

945465D61B3B41948EFBDB8F7C61BE1F.description:
Locate the Byzantine Empire and
Constantinople (Istanbul) on a world map; identify at least
one accomplishment or characteristic of the Byzantine
Empire.

E33B51B3F11541779CA9C2D90C27E2C3.description:
Locate India and China on a world map;
recognize at least one accomplishment of classical
civilizations in India and China including the Great Wall,
gunpowder, fireworks, and the Taj Mahal; recognize major
landforms and climate patterns including monsoon season,
the Himalayas, and the Yellow River.

4E7FFA73AD774E6E8E2E28551C44D38E.description:
Compare at least one modern aspect of culture
to one ancient aspect.

Recognize that civilizations and empires thrive
under strong leadership using Alexander the Great as an
example; identify characteristics of strong leadership.

6C2FD548FDD040CE845C1151445C3849.description:
Locate the ancient Greek peninsula on a map;
identify at least one significant contribution from ancient
Greece in the fields of politics, intellectual life, arts,
literature, architecture, or science.

D121F2C0D0F34B7A9E5890C0FA27BDE9.description:
Recognize that different world cultures have
different values, beliefs, and traditions.

5EF5E6D71C6345178CBF78612FB271B2.description:
identify and list characteristics of early
civilizations.

F0DE7554C56443448096CC154321E43F.description:
Identifying terms B.C. and A.D. used to
describe to describe time.

0A3E8FDC9DFA4295A8F2E381335DC076.description:
Recognize that cave paintings, fossils, and
pottery remnants provide evidence of early groups of
people; draw logical conclusions about sample artifacts.

document.title: SOCIAL STUDIES ALTERNATE ACHIEVEMENT STANDARDS

5A846B79CAB146798445345456537368.description:
Define and list characteristics of democracy
including civil liberties, human rights and separation of
powers.

7A077D035EC247FEB16BA71720A4A822.description:
List some changes in world conditions that
led to globalization from 1945–present; recall the
definition of globalization; define terrorism and
recognize its impact on the world.

50883FD2A6AA4347A9D4C14DE3755F21.description:
Recognize causes of the Cold War and the
United States’ new role in world affairs; identify key
events and/or people of the Cold War.

03B665CF6BE04E2DBF5A15B08043656B.description:
Identify the Axis and Allied Powers.
SS.AAS.9.14d- Identify the end results of World War II
including VE-Day and VJ-Day.

57C3A149AE6B414E91DE674082277E1B.description:
Identify the map changes in national
borders as a result of World War II.

621560F395F84A42AC32651C9FE6B2E3.description:
Define global conflict and describe how
World War II was a global conflict; recognize social,
economic, and/or political changes, key events, and
people from World War II including the Holocaust,
Atomic Age, and the Nuremberg Trials.
SS.AAS.9.14a- Identify turning points of World War II in
the European and Pacific Theaters.

695CECEADF5C4AC4800BEF7BE15AF2FF.description:
Identify the causes and effects of the
Great Depression including the stock market crash,
collapse of farm economy, Dust Bowl, collapse of savings
and loans banks, inflation, poverty, homelessness, soup
kitchens, and unemployment.

85D2152B973F4ABEB3E19040AD341467.description:
Identify challenges in the United States
after World War I.

4DC0EC0B38DF420CBCB295B03F29F9E1.description:
Identify alliances during World War I and
boundary changes after World War I.

6C79C11C2B5341008D1228A5DCD64C7D.description:
Identify problems created by the Treaty of
Versailles of 1919 including Germany’s reparations and
the war guilt clause.

3B5EF4EEE36448FABDA28C824D727D62.description:
Describe the rise of communism in Russia
during WWI.

16702BF9E999414288831C1864C835D3.description:
Define total war; identify key events and/or
people from World War I; describe military technology
used during World War I.

4CE8BFCD098745A79650B0E73813A6F5.description:
Identify factors that caused Western
imperialism.

8BCA783973D448E29361BC4515ECCDFE.description:
Identify factors that caused European
nationalism.

6CAB716FBF004E5998EFD402FA50115B.description:
Identify the Emancipation
Proclamation, Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and
Fifteenth Amendments.

815155AD47B343CCB7A8C71D0A15D302.description:
Identify leaders of the abolitionist
movement including Frederick Douglass, William
Lloyd Garrison, Harriet Beecher Stowe, and Harriet
Tubman.

FBE4AE86D5434CDF944B4E26127F1054.description:
Identify leaders of the women’s rights
movement including Elizabeth Cady Stanton,
Sojourner Truth, and Susan B. Anthony.

B9BBAA8A310D4FE89FF3B8DD3C6B748A.description:
Define urbanization; recognize changes in
society as a result of the Industrial Revolution;

E88DB81C84494D359757ED3278477CB6.description:
Define capitalism, liberalism, socialism,
Marxism; identify important inventors in Europe during
the Industrial Revolution.

6868120AEA9745AE930D657C66A37C63.description:
List the causes and effects of the revolutions
in Latin America and the Caribbean including Haiti,
Colombia, Venezuela, Argentina, Chile, and Mexico.

66936460F03B4927889F13652865B069.description:
Identify causes, people, and key events of
the French Revolution.

AC93334F44EE4D6C9025197E5135E49E.description:
Recognize important factors of the Scientific
Revolution and the Age of Enlightenment; identify the
scientific advancements that led to the Enlightenment.

English Bill of Rights by giving examples of civil liberties
and limited government.

Define natural right; identify common
characteristics of a monarchy and of a constitutional
government.

Identify the location, geographical
resources, and natural resources of Africa, India, Japan,
and/or China; recognize that trade between countries
leads to cultural development.
